# zimrag — cited answers from offline ZIM archives

Drop `.zim` files into `E:\LocalLLM\zims` and ask questions. **There is no index
to build**: Kiwix archives ship their own Xapian full-text index, and one
`Searcher` spans every archive at once, so a new file is searchable the moment
it finishes downloading.

```powershell
python zimrag\ask_zim.py --list
python zimrag\ask_zim.py "what causes ocean acidification?"
python zimrag\ask_zim.py --sources-only "pH of the ocean surface"   # no model call
python zimrag\ask_zim.py --model qwen3.5:4b --top-k 6 "how do carbon markets work?"
python zimrag\ask_zim.py --json "..."                                # for scripting
```

Runs entirely on Windows against Ollama — no WSL, no GPU training, no embedding
pass.

## Why retrieval instead of training

Measured on this machine: fine-tuning 745 facts about the operator's own code
into a LoRA produced **19% exact identifier recall** — four in five specifics
confidently wrong (`IntegrityError` for `IntegrityReport`, invented repo URLs).
The model learned the *shape* of an answer, not its content.

Retrieval moves the facts into the prompt, where they are exact and attributable:

```
Q: what causes ocean acidification and how much has the ocean surface pH fallen?
A: Carbon dioxide emissions from human activities are the primary cause of ocean
   acidification [1]. The average pH of the ocean surface fell from approximately
   8.15 to 8.05 between 1950 and 2020 [1].
   [1] Ocean acidification — wikipedia_en_climate-change_mini
```

Those numbers are checkable against the cited article. And when the corpus does
not hold the answer it says so, rather than guessing:

```
Q: What is the population of Tokyo and its average commute time?
A: The provided sources do not contain information about the population of Tokyo
   or its average commute time. The text mentions Tokyo as a member of the C40
   steering committee but does not include demographic data [1].
```

## How it works

```
search all ZIMs      libzim Searcher over every archive, with query backoff
fetch + strip HTML   scripts/styles/nav removed, entities unescaped
passage rerank       the paragraphs that contain the query terms, in order
grounded prompt      numbered sources + cite-or-admit-the-gap instruction
local model          qwen3.5:9b at temperature 0.2
```

Two non-obvious details carry most of the quality:

**Query backoff.** ZIM indexes use **AND** semantics, so a natural question
matches nothing. On the climate archive, `ocean acidification` finds 53
articles, `ocean acidification pH` leaves 6, and the full sentence *"what causes
ocean acidification and how much has pH fallen?"* finds **0**. Xapian's own
operators are not honoured reliably through the Python wrapper (`a OR b OR c`
returned 0), so `_search_backoff` ranks terms by specificity — length, plus a
boost for words capitalised in the question — and drops the least specific one
at a time until the index answers. The first non-empty result set is also the
most constrained, which is what ranks best.

**Passage selection, not truncation.** The index ranks *articles*; the answer
may be one paragraph near the bottom of a long one. `best_passages` scores
paragraphs by query-term overlap, keeps the lead paragraph in contention
(it defines the subject), then restores document order for readability.

## Defaults worth knowing

| flag | default | why |
|---|---|---|
| `--model` | `qwen3.5:9b` | **not** the `qwen3.5-srini:*` persona tags — those carry ~4.7k tokens of operator and repo context that competes with the retrieved sources |
| `--top-k` | 4 | relevance falls off fast; more sources mostly buys latency |
| `--chars` | 1600 | per source; the whole prompt stays inside a 16k context |
| temperature | 0.2 | grounded extraction, not invention |

## Choosing archives

From <https://download.kiwix.org/zim/>, sizes as of 2026-11:

| archive | size | note |
|---|---|---|
| `wikipedia_en_all_maxi` | 119 G | everything, with images |
| `wikipedia_en_all_nopic` | 49 G | everything, no images |
| `wikipedia_en_all_mini` | 13 G | lead sections only — best size/价value for Q&A |
| `wikipedia_en_top_mini` | 283 M | most-read articles |
| topic subsets | 12 M – 2 G | `chemistry_mini` 22 M, `climate-change_mini` 12 M, `physics_mini` 51 M, `medicine_mini` 166 M, `computer_nopic` 493 M |

`E:` has ~1.8 TB free, so even `all_maxi` fits. For factual Q&A the `mini`
flavours are usually the better trade: lead sections answer most questions and
搜索 stays fast.

Non-Wikipedia archives work identically — Stack Exchange, Gutenberg, DevDocs,
Wiktionary are all on the same server and all carry full-text indexes.

## Files

```
zimrag.py        library: search, extract, rerank, prompt, answer
ask_zim.py       CLI
testdata/        a 12 MB climate-change ZIM used to verify the pipeline;
                 searched only with --include-testdata, so it never
                 contaminates the real corpus in ../zims
```

## Licensing

ZIM content keeps its upstream licence — Wikipedia is CC BY-SA. Quoting with a
citation is exactly the attribution that licence expects, which is a second
reason to prefer retrieval over baking the text into model weights.

---
name: project-zimrag
description: E:\LocalLLM\zimrag gives cited offline answers from ZIM archives with no index build — ZIM indexes are AND-only so query backoff is essential
metadata:
  type: project
---

Built 2026-11-24. `E:\LocalLLM\zimrag\` answers questions from Kiwix `.zim`
archives dropped into `E:\LocalLLM\zims\`, with citations, entirely on Windows
against Ollama. No WSL, no embeddings, no GPU, **no index build** — Kiwix
archives carry their own Xapian full-text index (`Archive.has_fulltext_index`)
and one `Searcher(*archives)` spans the whole corpus, so a new file is
searchable as soon as it lands.

```
python zimrag\ask_zim.py --list
python zimrag\ask_zim.py "what causes ocean acidification?"
python zimrag\ask_zim.py --sources-only "..."      # retrieval only, no model
```

`zimrag.py` is the importable library (search / strip_html / best_passages /
build_prompt / answer); `ask_zim.py` is the CLI.

**The gotcha that makes or breaks it: ZIM full-text indexes are AND-only.** On
the climate archive, `ocean acidification` matches 53 articles, adding `pH`
leaves 6, and the full question *"what causes ocean acidification and how much
has pH fallen?"* matches **0**. Xapian's operators are not honoured reliably
through python-libzim (`a OR b OR c` returned 0 matches), so `_search_backoff`
ranks terms by specificity (length, plus a boost for words capitalised in the
question) and drops the least specific one at a time until the index answers.
Without that, every natural-language question returns nothing.

Other details: `libzim` installs and imports fine on **Windows** (`pip install
libzim`) — no WSL needed. `SearchResult` carries `.archive`, `.path`, `.title`
and a highlighted `.snippet`. The Search object uses snake_case
(`get_estimated_matches`, `get_results`), not the camelCase in some docs.
`best_passages` picks paragraphs by query-term overlap rather than truncating,
because the index ranks articles while the answer may sit near the bottom of a
long one.

Defaults to plain `qwen3.5:9b`, deliberately **not** the `qwen3.5-srini:*`
persona tags — those carry ~4.7k tokens of operator/repo context that competes
with the retrieved sources for attention.

Verified behaviour: exact figures with citations ("pH fell from approximately
8.15 to 8.05 between 1950 and 2020 [1]"), a clean "nothing matched" when the
corpus has no hits, and — the important one — an explicit refusal when sources
are retrieved but do not contain the answer. That is the direct contrast with
[[project-code-facts-training]], where fine-tuned facts gave 19% exact recall
and confident fabrication.

`zimrag/testdata/test_climate.zim` (12 MB, 17,008 articles) is a regression
fixture, searched only with `--include-testdata` so it never contaminates the
real corpus.

{

    "file_path": "E:\LocalLLM\zimrag\fetch_zims.py",
    "content": "#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
fetch_zims.py - Resolve and download ZIM archives into ../zims.

Resolution goes through the Kiwix OPDS catalog rather than hard-coded URLs,
because filenames carry a dump date (`wikipedia_en_all_nopic_2026-06.zim`) and
go stale every few months. Ask for a name plus a flavour and this finds the
current file, its exact size, and its mirror URL.

Downloads resume. These archives run to tens of gigabytes, so a dropped
connection must not mean starting over: each file is fetched to `.part` with an
HTTP Range header and only renamed once its length matches the catalog's.

    python zimrag/fetch_zims.py --list-sets
    python zimrag/fetch_zims.py --set core           # text-first, ~95 GB
    python zimrag/fetch_zims.py --set reference --dry-run
    python zimrag/fetch_zims.py --name wikipedia_en_all --flavour nopic
    python zimrag/fetch_zims.py --set core --jobs 2  # parallel, if bandwidth allows
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import concurrent.futures
import os
import sys
import urllib.error
import urllib.parse
import urllib.request
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
ZIM_DIR = HERE.parent / "zims"
CATALOG = "https://library.kiwix.org/catalog/v2/entries"
NS = {"a": "http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom"}
ACQ = "http://opds-spec.org/acquisition/open-access"
CHUNK = 1 << 20

# Curated from ostechnix.com/best-kiwix-zim-files/. The article recommends the
# NoPic flavour as the default - full article text, far less storage than Maxi -
# so that is what the wiki entries ask for.
#
# Sets are split by what retrieval can actually use. A ZIM of video lectures is
# mostly media payload with little indexable text, so it inflates the corpus
# without improving answers; those live in `media`, off by default.
SETS: dict[str, list[tuple[str, str]]] = {
    "core": [
        ("wikipedia_en_all", "nopic"),        # ~53 GB, the foundation
        ("wiktionary_en_all", ""),            # ~15 GB
        ("wikibooks_en_all", "nopic"),        # ~3.5 GB
        ("wikisource_en_all", "nopic"),       # ~3.9 GB
        ("wikivoyage_en_all", "nopic"),       # ~0.3 GB
        ("wikiversity_en_all", "nopic"),      # ~1.6 GB
        ("wikiquote_en_all", "nopic"),        # ~0.4 GB
        ("wikispecies_en_all", "nopic"),      # ~1.7 GB
        ("mdwiki_en_all", "maxi"),            # ~2.3 GB, WikiMed
        ("archlinux_en_all", ""),             # ~0.04 GB, ArchWiki
        ("freecodecamp_en_all", ""),          # ~0.01 GB
        ("phet_en_all", ""),                  # ~0.11 GB
    ],
    # Developer docs: dozens of tiny archives, picked for this operator's stack.
    "devdocs": [(f"devdocs_en_{t}", "") for t in (
        "python~3.12", "javascript", "typescript", "node", "docker", "git",
        "postgresql", "sqlite", "bash", "rust", "go", "react", "pytorch",
        "numpy", "pandas", "http", "regex",
    )],
    "stackexchange": [
        ("stackoverflow.com_en_all", ""),             # ~115 GB
        ("serverfault.com_en_all", ""),               # ~1.6 GB
        ("askubuntu.com_en_all", ""),
        ("superuser.com_en_all", ""),
        ("unix.stackexchange.com_en_all", ""),
        ("math.stackexchange.com_en_all", ""),        # ~7.4 GB
    ],
    "books": [("gutenberg_en_all", "")],              # ~221 GB
    "education": [(f"libretexts.org_en_{t}", "") for t in (
        "chem", "bio", "math", "phys", "eng", "stats",
    )],
    "media": [                                        # video-heavy, little text
        ("ted_mul_ted-ed", ""),
        ("khanacademy_en_all", ""),                   # ~180 GB, dated 2023
    ],
}


@dataclass
class Target:
    name: str
    flavour: str
    url: str
    size: int
    filename: str

    @property
    def dest(self) -> Path:
        return ZIM_DIR / self.filename

    @property
    def part(self) -> Path:
        return ZIM_DIR / (self.filename + ".part")


def resolve(name: str, flavour: str = "") -> Target | None:
    """Find the current archive for a catalog name, preferring `flavour`."""
    q = urllib.parse.urlencode({"q": name.split("_")[0], "count": 120})
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(f"{CATALOG}?{q}", timeout=90) as r:
            root = ET.fromstring(r.read())
    except (urllib.error.URLError, ET.ParseError, TimeoutError) as e:
        print(f"  !! catalog lookup failed for {name}: {type(e).__name__}: {e}")
        return None

    best: Target | None = None
    for entry in root.findall("a:entry", NS):
        fields = {c.tag.split('}')[-1]: (c.text or "").strip() for c in entry}
        if fields.get("name") != name:
            continue
        link = next((l for l in entry.findall("a:link", NS)
                     if l.get("rel") == ACQ and "zim" in (l.get("type") or "")), None)
        if link is None:
            continue
        href = (link.get("href") or "").removesuffix(".meta4")
        cand = Target(name=name, flavour=fields.get("flavour", ""), url=href,
                      size=int(link.get("length") or 0),
                      filename=href.rsplit("/", 1)[-1])
        if flavour and cand.flavour == flavour:
            return cand
        # No flavour asked for, or none matched yet: keep the smallest, which is
        # the least wasteful default when a collection ships several editions.
        if best is None or cand.size < best.size:
            best = cand
    if flavour and best is not None:
        print(f"  (no '{flavour}' flavour for {name}; using "
              f"'{best.flavour or 'default'}')")
    return best


def human(n: int) -> str:
    return f"{n / 1e9:.2f} GB" if n >= 1e9 else f"{n / 1e6:.0f} MB"


def download(t: Target, *, dry_run: bool = False) -> bool:
    ZIM_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    if t.dest.exists() and t.dest.stat().st_size == t.size:
        print(f"  = {t.filename}  already complete ({human(t.size)})")
        return True
    if dry_run:
        print(f"  + {t.filename:<52} {human(t.size):>10}")
        return True

    have = t.part.stat().st_size if t.part.exists() else 0
    if have > t.size:                       # stale part from a different dump
        t.part.unlink()
        have = 0

    req = urllib.request.Request(t.url)
    if have:
        req.add_header("Range", f"bytes={have}-")
        print(f"  ~ {t.filename}  resuming at {human(have)} of {human(t.size)}")
    else:
        print(f"  > {t.filename}  {human(t.size)}")

    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=120) as resp:
            # A server that ignores Range replies 200 and restarts the body.
            mode = "ab" if (have and resp.status == 206) else "wb"
            if mode == "wb":
                have = 0
            done = have
            with t.part.open(mode) as fh:
                while True:
                    buf = resp.read(CHUNK)
                    if not buf:
                        break
                    fh.write(buf)
                    done += len(buf)
                    if t.size:
                        pct = done / t.size * 100
                        print(f"\r    {pct:5.1f}%  {human(done)} / {human(t.size)}",
                              end="", flush=True)
            print()
    except (urllib.error.URLError, TimeoutError, OSError) as e:
        print(f"\n  !! {t.filename}: {type(e).__name__}: {e}  (rerun to resume)")
        return False

    actual = t.part.stat().st_size
    if t.size and actual != t.size:
        print(f"  !! {t.filename}: got {human(actual)}, expected {human(t.size)} "
              f"- left as .part, rerun to resume")
        return False
    os.replace(t.part, t.dest)
    print(f"  ok {t.filename}")
    return True


def main() -> int:
    for stream in (sys.stdout, sys.stderr):
        try:
            stream.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
        except (AttributeError, OSError):
            pass

    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Download ZIM archives into ../zims.")
    p.add_argument("--set", action="append", default=[], dest="sets",
                   choices=sorted(SETS), help="Named set (repeatable).")
    p.add_argument("--name", action="append", default=[],
                   help="Explicit catalog name (repeatable).")
    p.add_argument("--flavour", default="", help="Flavour for --name.")
    p.add_argument("--jobs", type=int, default=1,
                   help="Parallel downloads. 1 is kindest to the mirrors.")
    p.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true")
    p.add_argument("--list-sets", action="store_true")
    args = p.parse_args()

    if args.list_sets:
        for name, items in SETS.items():
            print(f"{name:<14} {len(items):>3} archive(s)")
            for n, f in items:
                print(f"               {n} {('[' + f + ']') if f else ''}")
        return 0

    wanted: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
    for s in args.sets:
        wanted += SETS[s]
    wanted += [(n, args.flavour) for n in args.name]
    if not wanted:
        p.error("choose --set or --name (see --list-sets)")

    print(f"resolving {len(wanted)} archive(s) via the Kiwix catalog ...")
    targets: list[Target] = []
    for name, flavour in wanted:
        t = resolve(name, flavour)
        if t is None:
            print(f"  !! not found in catalog: {name}")
            continue
        targets.append(t)

    total = sum(t.size for t in targets)
    free = __import__("shutil").disk_usage(ZIM_DIR.parent).free
    print(f"\n{len(targets)} resolved, {human(total)} total; "
          f"{human(free)} free on the volume")
    if total > free:
        print("  !! not enough free space - aborting")
        return 1

    print()
    if args.jobs > 1 and not args.dry_run:
        with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(args.jobs) as pool:
            results = list(pool.map(lambda t: download(t), targets))
    else:
        results = [download(t, dry_run=args.dry_run) for t in targets]

    ok = sum(1 for r in results if r)
    print(f"\n{ok}/{len(results)} complete")
    if ok < len(results):
        print("rerun the same command to resume the rest")
    return 0 if ok == len(results) else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
"
  }
}

"""Resolve the ostechnix-recommended collections to concrete ZIM downloads."""
import re
import urllib.parse
import urllib.request
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET

NS = {"a": "http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom"}
ACQ = "http://opds-spec.org/acquisition/open-access"

# search term -> label from the article
WANTED = [
    ("wikipedia", "Wikipedia"),
    ("wiktionary", "Wiktionary"),
    ("wikibooks", "Wikibooks"),
    ("wikisource", "Wikisource"),
    ("wikivoyage", "Wikivoyage"),
    ("devdocs", "DevDocs"),
    ("archwiki", "ArchWiki"),
    ("freecodecamp", "freeCodeCamp"),
    ("stackoverflow", "Stack Exchange (Stack Overflow)"),
    ("khanacademy", "Khan Academy"),
    ("libretexts", "LibreTexts"),
    ("phet", "PhET Simulations"),
    ("ted", "TED"),
    ("gutenberg", "Project Gutenberg"),
    ("wikiversity", "Wikiversity"),
    ("mdwiki", "WikiMed (MDWiki)"),
    ("wikem", "WikEM"),
    ("wikiquote", "Wikiquote"),
    ("wikispecies", "Wikispecies"),
]


def fetch(term: str) -> list[dict]:
    url = ("https://library.kiwix.org/catalog/v2/entries?"
           + urllib.parse.urlencode({"q": term, "lang": "eng", "count": 40}))
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=60) as r:
            root = ET.fromstring(r.read())
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"  !! {term}: {type(e).__name__}: {e}")
        return []

    out = []
    for e in root.findall("a:entry", NS):
        def txt(tag, ns="a"):
            el = e.find(f"{ns}:{tag}", NS)
            return (el.text or "").strip() if el is not None else ""

        link = None
        for l in e.findall("a:link", NS):
            if l.get("rel") == ACQ and "zim" in (l.get("type") or ""):
                link = l
                break
        if link is None:
            continue
        href = link.get("href") or ""
        size = int(link.get("length") or 0)
        name = txt("name", "a") or ""
        if not name:
            for child in e:
                if child.tag.endswith("name"):
                    name = (child.text or "").strip()
        out.append({
            "title": txt("title"),
            "name": name,
            "size_gb": size / 1e9,
            "href": href,
            "articles": txt("articleCount"),
        })
    return out


print(f"{'collection':<32} {'candidates':>10}")
print("=" * 96)
for term, label in WANTED:
    cands = fetch(term)
    # English, prefer the flavours the article recommends
    eng = [c for c in cands if re.search(r"_en[_\b]|_en$", c["name"] or "")] or cands
    def rank(c):
        n = c["name"]
        flav = 0 if "nopic" in n else 1 if "maxi" in n else 2 if "mini" in n else 3
        allv = 0 if "_all_" in n else 1
        return (allv, flav, -c["size_gb"])
    eng.sort(key=rank)
    print(f"\n### {label}  ({len(cands)} eng candidates)")
    for c in eng[:4]:
        print(f"   {c['name'][:52]:<52} {c['size_gb']:>7.2f} GB  {c['articles'] or '?':>9} art")

"""Resolve flavour + direct URL for each collection, and find the missing four."""
import json
import urllib.parse
import urllib.request
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET

NS = {"a": "http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom"}
ACQ = "http://opds-spec.org/acquisition/open-access"
TERMS = ["stack", "khan", "wikem", "wikispecies", "wikipedia", "wiktionary",
         "gutenberg", "ted", "mdwiki", "devdocs"]


def entries(term, count=60):
    url = ("https://library.kiwix.org/catalog/v2/entries?"
           + urllib.parse.urlencode({"q": term, "count": count}))
    with urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=90) as r:
        root = ET.fromstring(r.read())
    out = []
    for e in root.findall("a:entry", NS):
        d = {}
        for child in e:
            tag = child.tag.split("}")[-1]
            if tag in ("title", "name", "flavour", "language", "articleCount"):
                d[tag] = (child.text or "").strip()
        for l in e.findall("a:link", NS):
            if l.get("rel") == ACQ and "zim" in (l.get("type") or ""):
                d["href"] = l.get("href") or ""
                d["size_gb"] = int(l.get("length") or 0) / 1e9
        if "href" in d:
            out.append(d)
    return out


for term in TERMS:
    rows = entries(term)
    eng = [r for r in rows if r.get("language", "").startswith("eng")
           or "_en_" in r.get("name", "") or r.get("language") == "mul"]
    print(f"\n##### {term}  ({len(rows)} total, {len(eng)} eng/mul)")
    seen = set()
    for r in sorted(eng, key=lambda x: -x["size_gb"])[:8]:
        key = (r.get("name"), r.get("flavour"))
        if key in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(key)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
fetch_zims.py - Resolve and download ZIM archives into ../zims.

Resolution goes through the Kiwix OPDS catalog rather than hard-coded URLs,
because filenames carry a dump date (`wikipedia_en_all_nopic_2026-06.zim`) and
go stale every few months. Ask for a name plus a flavour and this finds the
current file, its exact size, and its mirror URL.

Downloads resume. These archives run to tens of gigabytes, so a dropped
connection must not mean starting over: each file is fetched to `.part` with an
HTTP Range header and only renamed once its length matches the catalog's.

    python zimrag/fetch_zims.py --list-sets
    python zimrag/fetch_zims.py --set core           # text-first, ~95 GB
    python zimrag/fetch_zims.py --set reference --dry-run
    python zimrag/fetch_zims.py --name wikipedia_en_all --flavour nopic
    python zimrag/fetch_zims.py --set core --jobs 2  # parallel, if bandwidth allows
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import concurrent.futures
import os
import sys
import urllib.error
import urllib.parse
import urllib.request
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
ZIM_DIR = HERE.parent / "zims"
CATALOG = "https://library.kiwix.org/catalog/v2/entries"
NS = {"a": "http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom"}
ACQ = "http://opds-spec.org/acquisition/open-access"
CHUNK = 1 << 20

# Curated from ostechnix.com/best-kiwix-zim-files/. The article recommends the
# NoPic flavour as the default - full article text, far less storage than Maxi -
# so that is what the wiki entries ask for.
#
# Sets are split by what retrieval can actually use. A ZIM of video lectures is
# mostly media payload with little indexable text, so it inflates the corpus
# without improving answers; those live in `media`, off by default.
SETS: dict[str, list[tuple[str, str]]] = {
    "core": [
        ("wikipedia_en_all", "nopic"),        # ~53 GB, the foundation
        ("wiktionary_en_all", ""),            # ~15 GB
        ("wikibooks_en_all", "nopic"),        # ~3.5 GB
        ("wikisource_en_all", "nopic"),       # ~3.9 GB
        ("wikivoyage_en_all", "nopic"),       # ~0.3 GB
        ("wikiversity_en_all", "nopic"),      # ~1.6 GB
        ("wikiquote_en_all", "nopic"),        # ~0.4 GB
        ("wikispecies_en_all", "nopic"),      # ~1.7 GB
        ("mdwiki_en_all", "maxi"),            # ~2.3 GB, WikiMed
        ("archlinux_en_all", ""),             # ~0.04 GB, ArchWiki
        ("freecodecamp_en_all", ""),          # ~0.01 GB
        ("phet_en_all", ""),                  # ~0.11 GB
    ],
    # Developer docs: dozens of tiny archives, picked for this operator's stack.
    "devdocs": [(f"devdocs_en_{t}", "") for t in (
        "python~3.12", "javascript", "typescript", "node", "docker", "git",
        "postgresql", "sqlite", "bash", "rust", "go", "react", "pytorch",
        "numpy", "pandas", "http", "regex",
    )],
    "stackexchange": [
        ("stackoverflow.com_en_all", ""),             # ~115 GB
        ("serverfault.com_en_all", ""),               # ~1.6 GB
        ("askubuntu.com_en_all", ""),
        ("superuser.com_en_all", ""),
        ("unix.stackexchange.com_en_all", ""),
        ("math.stackexchange.com_en_all", ""),        # ~7.4 GB
    ],
    "books": [("gutenberg_en_all", "")],              # ~221 GB
    "education": [(f"libretexts.org_en_{t}", "") for t in (
        "chem", "bio", "math", "phys", "eng", "stats",
    )],
    "media": [                                        # video-heavy, little text
        ("ted_mul_ted-ed", ""),
        ("khanacademy_en_all", ""),                   # ~180 GB, dated 2023
    ],
}


@dataclass
class Target:
    name: str
    flavour: str
    url: str
    size: int
    filename: str

    @property
    def dest(self) -> Path:
        return ZIM_DIR / self.filename

    @property
    def part(self) -> Path:
        return ZIM_DIR / (self.filename + ".part")


def resolve(name: str, flavour: str = "") -> Target | None:
    """Find the current archive for a catalog name, preferring `flavour`."""
    q = urllib.parse.urlencode({"q": name.split("_")[0], "count": 120})
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(f"{CATALOG}?{q}", timeout=90) as r:
            root = ET.fromstring(r.read())
    except (urllib.error.URLError, ET.ParseError, TimeoutError) as e:
        print(f"  !! catalog lookup failed for {name}: {type(e).__name__}: {e}")
        return None

    best: Target | None = None
    for entry in root.findall("a:entry", NS):
        fields = {c.tag.split('}')[-1]: (c.text or "").strip() for c in entry}
        if fields.get("name") != name:
            continue
        link = next((l for l in entry.findall("a:link", NS)
                     if l.get("rel") == ACQ and "zim" in (l.get("type") or "")), None)
        if link is None:
            continue
        href = (link.get("href") or "").removesuffix(".meta4")
        cand = Target(name=name, flavour=fields.get("flavour", ""), url=href,
                      size=int(link.get("length") or 0),
                      filename=href.rsplit("/", 1)[-1])
        if flavour and cand.flavour == flavour:
            return cand
        # No flavour asked for, or none matched yet: keep the smallest, which is
        # the least wasteful default when a collection ships several editions.
        if best is None or cand.size < best.size:
            best = cand
    if flavour and best is not None:
        print(f"  (no '{flavour}' flavour for {name}; using "
              f"'{best.flavour or 'default'}')")
    return best


def human(n: int) -> str:
    return f"{n / 1e9:.2f} GB" if n >= 1e9 else f"{n / 1e6:.0f} MB"


def download(t: Target, *, dry_run: bool = False) -> bool:
    ZIM_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    if t.dest.exists() and t.dest.stat().st_size == t.size:
        print(f"  = {t.filename}  already complete ({human(t.size)})")
        return True
    if dry_run:
        print(f"  + {t.filename:<52} {human(t.size):>10}")
        return True

    have = t.part.stat().st_size if t.part.exists() else 0
    if have > t.size:                       # stale part from a different dump
        t.part.unlink()
        have = 0

    req = urllib.request.Request(t.url)
    if have:
        req.add_header("Range", f"bytes={have}-")
        print(f"  ~ {t.filename}  resuming at {human(have)} of {human(t.size)}")
    else:
        print(f"  > {t.filename}  {human(t.size)}")

    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=120) as resp:
            # A server that ignores Range replies 200 and restarts the body.
            mode = "ab" if (have and resp.status == 206) else "wb"
            if mode == "wb":
                have = 0
            done = have
            with t.part.open(mode) as fh:
                while True:
                    buf = resp.read(CHUNK)
                    if not buf:
                        break
                    fh.write(buf)
                    done += len(buf)
                    if t.size:
                        pct = done / t.size * 100
                        print(f"\r    {pct:5.1f}%  {human(done)} / {human(t.size)}",
                              end="", flush=True)
            print()
    except (urllib.error.URLError, TimeoutError, OSError) as e:
        print(f"\n  !! {t.filename}: {type(e).__name__}: {e}  (rerun to resume)")
        return False

    actual = t.part.stat().st_size
    if t.size and actual != t.size:
        print(f"  !! {t.filename}: got {human(actual)}, expected {human(t.size)} "
              f"- left as .part, rerun to resume")
        return False
    os.replace(t.part, t.dest)
    print(f"  ok {t.filename}")
    return True


def main() -> int:
    for stream in (sys.stdout, sys.stderr):
        try:
            stream.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
        except (AttributeError, OSError):
            pass

    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Download ZIM archives into ../zims.")
    p.add_argument("--set", action="append", default=[], dest="sets",
                   choices=sorted(SETS), help="Named set (repeatable).")
    p.add_argument("--name", action="append", default=[],
                   help="Explicit catalog name (repeatable).")
    p.add_argument("--flavour", default="", help="Flavour for --name.")
    p.add_argument("--jobs", type=int, default=1,
                   help="Parallel downloads. 1 is kindest to the mirrors.")
    p.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true")
    p.add_argument("--list-sets", action="store_true")
    args = p.parse_args()

    if args.list_sets:
        for name, items in SETS.items():
            print(f"{name:<14} {len(items):>3} archive(s)")
            for n, f in items:
                print(f"               {n} {('[' + f + ']') if f else ''}")
        return 0

    wanted: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
    for s in args.sets:
        wanted += SETS[s]
    wanted += [(n, args.flavour) for n in args.name]
    if not wanted:
        p.error("choose --set or --name (see --list-sets)")

    print(f"resolving {len(wanted)} archive(s) via the Kiwix catalog ...")
    targets: list[Target] = []
    for name, flavour in wanted:
        t = resolve(name, flavour)
        if t is None:
            print(f"  !! not found in catalog: {name}")
            continue
        targets.append(t)

    total = sum(t.size for t in targets)
    free = __import__("shutil").disk_usage(ZIM_DIR.parent).free
    print(f"\n{len(targets)} resolved, {human(total)} total; "
          f"{human(free)} free on the volume")
    if total > free:
        print("  !! not enough free space - aborting")
        return 1

    print()
    if args.jobs > 1 and not args.dry_run:
        with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(args.jobs) as pool:
            results = list(pool.map(lambda t: download(t), targets))
    else:
        results = [download(t, dry_run=args.dry_run) for t in targets]

    ok = sum(1 for r in results if r)
    print(f"\n{ok}/{len(results)} complete")
    if ok < len(results):
        print("rerun the same command to resume the rest")
    return 0 if ok == len(results) else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

def true_size(t: Target) -> int:
    """The size the mirror will actually serve.

    The catalog's declared `length` is not byte-exact - it reads 42 to 180 bytes
    larger than the files it describes - so comparing a finished download
    against it fails every time, leaving complete archives stranded as `.part`
    and re-downloading them on the next run. Ask the server instead, and keep
    the catalog figure only for progress display and disk-space planning.
    """
    req = urllib.request.Request(t.url, method="HEAD")
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=60) as resp:
            n = int(resp.headers.get("Content-Length") or 0)
            return n or t.size
    except (urllib.error.URLError, TimeoutError, ValueError):

def verify(path: Path) -> tuple[bool, str]:
    """Open the archive with libzim - a real integrity check, not a byte count."""
    try:
        from libzim.reader import Archive

        a = Archive(str(path))
        return True, f"{a.article_count:,} articles"
    except Exception as e:                  # a truncated ZIM raises from C++
        return False, f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"


def download(t: Target, *, dry_run: bool = False) -> bool:
    ZIM_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    if dry_run:
        print(f"  + {t.filename:<52} {human(t.size):>10}")
        return True

    total = true_size(t)

    if t.dest.exists() and t.dest.stat().st_size == total:
        print(f"  = {t.filename}  already complete ({human(total)})")
        return True

    have = t.part.stat().st_size if t.part.exists() else 0
    if have > total:                        # stale part from a different dump
        t.part.unlink()
        have = 0
    elif have == total and have:
        # Fully transferred on a previous run but never renamed.
        ok, detail = verify(t.part)
        if ok:
            os.replace(t.part, t.dest)
            print(f"  ok {t.filename}  (completed earlier; {detail})")
            return True
        print(f"  !! {t.filename}: complete but unreadable - {detail}; refetching")
        t.part.unlink()
        have = 0

_STUB_RE = re.compile(r'(?i)<meta\s+http-equiv="refresh"')
_PAGE_ID_RE = re.compile(r"page_(\d+)\b")


def spa_text(archive, path: str) -> str:
    """Article text for single-page-app archives, which hide it from the entry.

    Not every ZIM stores one HTML document per article. LibreTexts (and other
    scrapers of JavaScript sites) index a stub - 280 bytes of
    `<meta http-equiv="refresh">` pointing at `index.html#/...` - while the real
    document sits in a sibling JSON blob, `content/page_content_<id>.json`
    against a stub at `index/page_<id>`. The Xapian index covers the real text,
    so these articles rank correctly and then extract to nothing, which is the
    worst combination: confident retrieval of empty sources.
    """
    m = _PAGE_ID_RE.search(path)
    if not m:
        return ""
    try:
        item = archive.get_entry_by_path(
            f"content/page_content_{m.group(1)}.json").get_item()
        data = json.loads(bytes(item.content).decode("utf-8", "replace"))
    except (RuntimeError, KeyError, ValueError, UnicodeDecodeError):
        return ""
    if not isinstance(data, dict):
        return ""
    # The payload key is `htmlBody` today; take every string value so a
    # renamed or split field does not silently yield nothing.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
probe_models.py - Check which local tags are fit for the Claude Code harness.

Three things decide that, and none of them are benchmark scores:

  1. does it answer at all, and how fast (tok/s, and prompt-eval latency, which
     is what a system prompt costs you on every single request)
  2. does it emit a *well-formed tool call* when given a tool - a model that
     fumbles this loops with "Invalid tool parameters" in an agent harness and
     is unusable regardless of how clever it is
  3. does it keep its reasoning out of the answer channel

Usage:
    python bench/probe_models.py
    python bench/probe_models.py --models granite-srini:8b qwen3.5-srini:9b
    python bench/probe_models.py --json
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import sys
import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

HOST = "http://127.0.0.1:11434"

DEFAULT_MODELS = [
    "qwen3.5-srini:9b",
    "qwen3.5-srini:4b",
    "granite-srini:8b",
    "granite-srini:3b",
    "gemma-srini:e2b",
]

# A deliberately unambiguous tool call: one required string argument whose value
# is stated in the prompt. Any model that cannot do this will not survive an
# agent loop.
TOOLS = [{
    "type": "function",
    "function": {
        "name": "read_file",
        "description": "Read a file from disk and return its contents.",
        "parameters": {
            "type": "object",
            "properties": {
                "path": {"type": "string", "description": "Path to the file."},
                "start_line": {"type": "integer"},
            },
            "required": ["path"],
        },
    },
}]

TOOL_PROMPT = "Read the file E:/LocalLLM/curriculum.yaml. Use the tool."
SPEED_PROMPT = "In one sentence: how much VRAM can I use for a model on this machine?"


def chat(model: str, prompt: str, *, tools: list | None = None,
         think: bool = False, max_tokens: int = 200, timeout: int = 300) -> dict:
    payload = {
        "model": model,
        "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
        "stream": False,
        "think": think,
        "options": {"num_predict": max_tokens, "temperature": 0.2},
    }
    if tools:
        payload["tools"] = tools
    req = urllib.request.Request(
        f"{HOST}/api/chat", data=json.dumps(payload).encode("utf-8"),
        headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"}, method="POST")
    started = time.time()
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=timeout) as resp:
            data = json.loads(resp.read().decode("utf-8"))
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
        return {"error": f"HTTP {e.code}: {e.read().decode('utf-8', 'replace')[:200]}"}
    except Exception as e:
        return {"error": f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"}
    data["_wall"] = time.time() - started
    return data


def probe(model: str) -> dict:
    out: dict = {"model": model}

    # --- speed, and what the system prompt costs -----------------------------
    r = chat(model, SPEED_PROMPT, max_tokens=150)
    if "error" in r:
        out["error"] = r["error"]
        return out
    msg = r.get("message", {}) or {}
    eval_count = r.get("eval_count") or 0
    eval_dur = r.get("eval_duration") or 0
    prompt_count = r.get("prompt_eval_count") or 0
    prompt_dur = r.get("prompt_eval_duration") or 0
    out["tok_s"] = round(eval_count / (eval_dur / 1e9), 1) if eval_dur else 0.0
    out["prompt_tokens"] = prompt_count
    out["prompt_eval_s"] = round(prompt_dur / 1e9, 2) if prompt_dur else 0.0
    out["first_answer_s"] = round(out["prompt_eval_s"], 2)
    out["wall_s"] = round(r["_wall"], 1)
    answer = (msg.get("content") or "").strip()
    out["answer_head"] = answer[:90]
    # Reasoning leaking into the answer channel wastes tokens and confuses a
    # harness that expects content to be the answer.
    out["leaks_think"] = "<think>" in answer or "</think>" in answer

    # --- tool calling --------------------------------------------------------
    t = chat(model, TOOL_PROMPT, tools=TOOLS, max_tokens=200)
    if "error" in t:
        out["tool"] = f"ERROR {t['error'][:40]}"
        return out
    tmsg = t.get("message", {}) or {}
    calls = tmsg.get("tool_calls") or []
    if not calls:
        # Some models describe the call in prose instead of emitting one.
        prose = (tmsg.get("content") or "")
        out["tool"] = "prose" if "read_file" in prose else "none"
    else:
        fn = (calls[0].get("function") or {})
        args = fn.get("arguments")
        if isinstance(args, str):
            try:
                args = json.loads(args)
            except ValueError:
                args = {}
        ok_name = fn.get("name") == "read_file"
        ok_path = isinstance(args, dict) and "path" in args
        no_junk = isinstance(args, dict) and set(args) <= {"path", "start_line"}
        out["tool"] = "ok" if (ok_name and ok_path and no_junk) else "malformed"
        out["tool_args"] = json.dumps(args)[:70] if isinstance(args, dict) else str(args)[:70]
    return out


def main() -> int:
    for s in (sys.stdout, sys.stderr):
        try:
            s.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
        except (AttributeError, OSError):
            pass

    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Probe local tags for harness fitness.")
    p.add_argument("--models", nargs="*", default=DEFAULT_MODELS)
    p.add_argument("--json", action="store_true", dest="as_json")
    args = p.parse_args()

    rows = []
    for m in args.models:
        print(f"probing {m} ...", file=sys.stderr)
        rows.append(probe(m))

    if args.as_json:
        print(json.dumps(rows, indent=2))
        return 0

    print(f"\n{'model':<22}{'tok/s':>7}{'prompt':>8}{'p-eval':>8}"
          f"{'tools':>10}{'think-leak':>12}")
    print("-" * 70)
    for r in rows:
        if "error" in r:
            print(f"{r['model']:<22}  ERROR {r['error'][:40]}")
            continue
        print(f"{r['model']:<22}{r['tok_s']:>7}{r['prompt_tokens']:>8}"
              f"{r['prompt_eval_s']:>7}s{r.get('tool', '?'):>10}"
              f"{'YES' if r.get('leaks_think') else 'no':>12}")
    print("\nanswers:")
    for r in rows:
        if "error" not in r:
            print(f"  {r['model']:<22} {r['answer_head']}")
            if r.get("tool_args"):
                print(f"  {'':<22} tool args: {r['tool_args']}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

---
name: project-local-model-lineup
description: Five local models set up with a 304-token lean profile and wired into the Claude Code harness; gemma4 e2b is fastest at 129.6 tok/s, granite4.2:8b's tool calls are broken
metadata:
  type: project
---

Set up 2026-11-24. `bench/probe_models.py` measures what actually decides harness
fitness — warm tok/s, prompt-eval cost, whether a model emits a *well-formed
tool call*, GPU placement, and whether reasoning leaks into the answer channel.

**Always warm up before measuring.** The first cold run reported gemma4 e2b at
**2.1 tok/s** and granite 3b with a 9.6 s prompt eval; warm, the same models do
**129.6** and **0.02 s**. A cold-load measurement would have led to exactly the
wrong recommendation.

| tag | warm tok/s | size | tools | note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `gemma-srini:e2b` | **129.6** | 4.3 GB | ok | fastest; vision + audio input |
| `granite-srini:3b` | 99.8 | 2.2 GB | ok | cheapest; slightly garbles nuance |
| `qwen3.5-srini:4b` | 75.8 | 3.3 GB | ok | |
| `granite-srini:8b` | 46.7 | 5.3 GB | **BROKEN** | describes the call in prose instead of emitting one — loops in an agent harness, so excluded from defaults |
| `qwen3.5-srini:9b` | 45.0 | 6.6 GB | ok | best quality, the main model |

All five sit fully on the GPU. granite4.2:8b failing tool calls is reproducible
across runs and contradicts its own marketing; suspect Ollama's granite4.2
template/parser rather than the weights.

**Lean profile.** `build_persona_models.py --lean` (now the default; `--full`
restores the old behaviour) emits a **304-token** block instead of ~1.5k, holding
only facts that change an answer: the 6.6 GB usable ceiling, Windows-inference /
WSL-training split, that `E:\Github\repo2graph` v5.0.0 is authoritative while the
`C:` clone is stale, the `make lint/typecheck/test` verification order, no
co-author trailers, and answer style. Prompt eval is 0.02–0.15 s, so context is
no longer a latency factor. Verified: gemma and granite both name the right
checkout and the right VRAM figure.

**Harness wiring.** `run-claude-local.ps1` and `.sh` now resolve shorthands
`9b / 4b / 35b / gemma / granite3b / granite8b / raw9b / raw4b`, defaulting to
`qwen3.5-srini:9b` as the main model and **`gemma-srini:e2b` as the small/fast
model** (1.7x the 4b's speed, still valid tool calls). Unknown tags pass through
untouched. `~/.claude/settings.json` modelPicker lists the four usable tags with
measured speeds; granite8b is deliberately absent.

**Watch out:** `run-claude-local.*` sets `PROXY_URL` to **port 11435**, which is
also `serve_adapter.py`'s default port. Running a lesson grade and a local Claude
Code session at once will collide — pass `--port` to one of them.

Also confirmed this day: the `qwen3.5:4b`/`9b` tags contain **stock registry
weights** (blob digests match `library/qwen3.5:4b` byte-for-byte) plus a baked
SYSTEM profile. The distilled LoRA work is *not* merged into them; it still lives
in `adapters/lesson_01..05` behind `serve_adapter.py`. See
[[project-code-facts-training]].

def _normalise(text: str) -> str:
    """Collapse whitespace so cosmetic reformatting is not read as a change."""
    return " ".join(text.split())


def installed_system(tag: str) -> str | None:
    """The SYSTEM block currently baked into a tag, or None if it has none.

    `ollama show --modelfile` prints it as SYSTEM \"\"\"...\"\"\". Reading it back is
    how we detect the two ways a profile goes wrong: an `ollama pull` replaced
    the manifest and dropped it, or the profile files changed and the tag still
    carries yesterday's text.
    """
    ollama_cmd = "ollama.exe" if sys.platform == "win32" else "ollama"
    proc = subprocess.run([ollama_cmd, "show", "--modelfile", tag],
                          capture_output=True, text=True, encoding="utf-8",
                          errors="replace")
    if proc.returncode != 0:
        return None
    m = re.search(r'SYSTEM\s+"""(.*?)"""', proc.stdout, re.DOTALL)
    return m.group(1) if m else None


def audit(system: str) -> list[tuple[str, str, str]]:
    """(key, tag, state) for every target. state: ok | stale | missing | absent."""
    want = _normalise(system)
    rows: list[tuple[str, str, str]] = []
    for key, (base, derived) in sorted(TARGETS.items()):
        have = installed_system(derived)
        if have is None:
            # Distinguish "tag exists without a profile" from "no such tag".
            ollama_cmd = "ollama.exe" if sys.platform == "win32" else "ollama"
            exists = subprocess.run([ollama_cmd, "show", derived],
                                    capture_output=True, text=True).returncode == 0
            rows.append((key, derived, "missing" if exists else "absent"))
        elif _normalise(have) == want:
            rows.append((key, derived, "ok"))
        else:
            rows.append((key, derived, "stale"))
    return rows

# pull-model.ps1 - `ollama pull`, then put the operator profile back.
#
# The profile is baked into each tag's SYSTEM block, which is the right place for
# it (facts belong in the prompt, not in weights) but has one sharp edge:
# `ollama pull <tag>` replaces the tag's manifest and takes the SYSTEM block with
# it, silently. The model still answers - it just no longer knows the hardware
# ceiling or which repo2graph checkout is authoritative, and nothing says so.
#
# Use this instead of `ollama pull` and the question never arises.
#
# Usage:
#   powershell -File E:\LocalLLM\pull-model.ps1 qwen3.5:9b
#   powershell -File E:\LocalLLM\pull-model.ps1 gemma4:e2b-it-qat granite4.2:3b
#   powershell -File E:\LocalLLM\pull-model.ps1 -All        # refresh every tag

param(
    [Parameter(ValueFromRemainingArguments = $true)]
    [string[]]$Tags,
    # Re-pull every tag the profile builder knows about.
    [switch]$All
)

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$builder = 'E:\LocalLLM\profile\build_persona_models.py'

if ($All) {
    $Tags = @('qwen3.5:4b', 'qwen3.5:9b', 'granite4.2:3b', 'granite4.2:8b',
              'gemma4:e2b-it-qat', 'nemotron-3.5-lightning:30b')
}
if (-not $Tags) {
    Write-Error 'Name at least one tag, or pass -All.'
    exit 2
}

$failed = @()
foreach ($t in $Tags) {
    Write-Host "pulling $t" -ForegroundColor Cyan
    & ollama pull $t
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { $failed += $t }
}

# Rebuild only what drifted. --repair reads each tag's current SYSTEM block and
# compares it against the profile, so this is a no-op when nothing changed.
Write-Host 'restoring profiles' -ForegroundColor Cyan
& python $builder --repair

if ($failed) {
    Write-Warning ("failed to pull: " + ($failed -join ', '))
    exit 1
}
exit 0

def base_revision(cfg: dict) -> str | None:
    """The Hugging Face commit the training base is currently resolved to.

    A LoRA is a delta against *specific* weights, so an adapter is only
    meaningful against the revision it trained on. If the base is re-uploaded
    upstream and the cache refreshes, every adapter still loads - the shapes
    match - and quality degrades silently. Recording the revision is what makes
    that detectable instead of mysterious.
    """
    repo = cfg["meta"].get("student_hf_repo", "")
    if "/" not in repo:
        return None
    cache = os.environ.get("HUGGINGFACE_HUB_CACHE")
    if not cache:
        home = os.environ.get("HF_HOME") or str(Path.home() / ".cache" / "huggingface")
        cache = str(Path(home) / "hub")
    ref = (Path(cache) / f"models--{repo.replace('/', '--')}" / "refs" / "main")
    try:
        return ref.read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip() or None
    except OSError:
        return None


def verify_base(cfg: dict) -> bool:
    """Compare each trained lesson's recorded base against the current cache."""
    ledger_path = ADAPTERS / "lesson_ledger.json"
    if not ledger_path.exists():
        print("no ledger yet - nothing to verify")
        return True

    now = base_revision(cfg)
    repo = cfg["meta"].get("student_hf_repo", "?")
    print(f"base repo         {repo}")
    print(f"cache revision    {now or '(not cached)'}")

    data = json.loads(ledger_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    lessons = data.get("lessons", [])
    unknown = [l for l in lessons if not l.get("base_revision")]
    mismatched = [l for l in lessons
                  if l.get("base_revision") and l["base_revision"] != now]

    print(f"lessons recorded  {len(lessons)}")
    if unknown:
        print(f"  {len(unknown)} trained before revisions were recorded "
              f"(lesson {', '.join(str(l['lesson']) for l in unknown[:8])}"
              f"{'...' if len(unknown) > 8 else ''}) - provenance unknown, not "
              f"necessarily wrong")
    if mismatched:
        print(f"\n  !! {len(mismatched)} lesson(s) trained against a DIFFERENT base:")
        for l in mismatched:
            print(f"       lesson {l['lesson']:>2}  {l['base_revision'][:12]} "
                  f"!= {(now or '?')[:12]}")
        print("     Those adapters will still load - the shapes match - but "
              "their deltas no longer correspond to these weights.")
        print("     Retrain them, or restore the recorded revision with:")
        print(f"       huggingface-cli download {repo} --revision <sha>")
        return False
    if not unknown:
        print("\nall lessons match the cached base revision")
    return True

    "file_path": "E:\LocalLLM\profile\build_persona_models.py",
    "content": "#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
build_persona_models.py - Bake USER_PROFILE.md into the local models.

Creates a derived Ollama tag per base model whose Modelfile carries the operator
profile as its SYSTEM block, so every local session starts already knowing the
hardware ceiling, the stack, and the working preferences - with no fine-tuning.

Why a system prompt and not training: the profile is *facts*, and facts change.
A SYSTEM block is corrected by editing one file and rebuilding in ~2 seconds;
a fact baked into LoRA weights needs a retrain to undo, and a small model will
still contradict it whenever the prompt pulls the other way. Train style and
skills (that is what teacher_pipeline does); prompt the facts.

Derived tags are free in disk terms - Ollama reuses the base model's blobs and
only stores the new Modelfile.

CLI:
    python profile/build_persona_models.py              # build all three
    python profile/build_persona_models.py --model 9b   # just one
    python profile/build_persona_models.py --show       # print the SYSTEM block
    python profile/build_persona_models.py --dry-run
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import re
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

PROFILE = Path(__file__).with_name("USER_PROFILE.md")
BUILD_DIR = Path(__file__).with_name("build")

# base tag -> derived tag. The daily driver and the wildcard both get a persona;
# so does the student, so that an untrained 4b still answers in context.
TARGETS = {
    "4b": ("qwen3.5:4b", "qwen3.5-srini:4b"),
    "9b": ("qwen3.5:9b", "qwen3.5-srini:9b"),
    "35b": ("qwen3.5:35b", "qwen3.5-srini:35b"),
}

# Confidence markers are for the human reader; they cost tokens and invite a
# small model to hedge, so they are stripped from what the model actually sees.
MARKER_RE = re.compile(r"\s*`\[(?:verified|inferred)[^\]]*\]`")

PREAMBLE = """You are a coding assistant running locally on Srini's own machine, \
for Srini's own work. The following is established context about your operator \
and their environment. Treat it as fact, not as a request to role-play. Do not \
recite it back; use it to skip questions you already have the answer to, and to \
avoid proposing anything that the hardware ceiling or the local stack rules out.

"""


def system_block() -> str:
    """The profile, reduced to what is useful to a model at inference time."""
    text = PROFILE.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    text = MARKER_RE.sub("", text)
    # Drop the file's own maintenance instructions - they address the human.
    text = re.sub(
        r"^This file is the single source of truth.*?takes effect on the next call\.\s*",
        "",
        text,
        flags=re.DOTALL | re.MULTILINE,
    )
    text = re.sub(r"^Each entry is marked with.*?confirming\.\s*", "", text,
                  flags=re.DOTALL | re.MULTILINE)
    text = text.replace("\n---\n", "\n")
    text = re.sub(r"\n{3,}", "\n\n", text).strip()
    return PREAMBLE + text


def modelfile(base: str, system: str) -> str:
    # Triple-quoted SYSTEM so the markdown's own quotes and newlines survive.
    return (
        f"FROM {base}\n\n"
        f'SYSTEM """{system}\n"""\n\n'
        "# Low-ish temperature: this operator wants derivations and exact\n"
        "# schemas, not creative variety.\n"
        "PARAMETER temperature 0.5\n"
        "PARAMETER top_p 0.95\n"
    )


def build(key: str, system: str, *, dry_run: bool) -> bool:
    base, derived = TARGETS[key]
    BUILD_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    path = BUILD_DIR / f"Modelfile.{key}"
    path.write_text(modelfile(base, system), encoding="utf-8")

    if dry_run:
        print(f"[dry-run] ollama create {derived} -f {path}")
        return True

    print(f"-> {derived}  (from {base})")
    proc = subprocess.run(
        ["ollama", "create", derived, "-f", str(path)],
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
    )
    if proc.returncode != 0:
        print(f"   FAILED: {proc.stderr.strip()[:400]}", file=sys.stderr)
        return False
    return True


def main() -> int:
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[1])
    p.add_argument("--model", choices=sorted(TARGETS), action="append",
                   help="Build only this one (repeatable). Default: all.")
    p.add_argument("--show", action="store_true",
                   help="Print the SYSTEM block and exit.")
    p.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true",
                   help="Write the Modelfiles but do not call ollama.")
    args = p.parse_args()

    if not PROFILE.exists():
        print(f"missing profile: {PROFILE}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1

    system = system_block()

    if args.show:
        print(system)
        print(f"\n[{len(system)} chars ~= {len(system) // 4} tokens]",
              file=sys.stderr)

# Operator profile — Srini

Everything the local models should know about the person they are working for.
This file is the single source of truth: edit it, then re-run
`python profile/build_persona_models.py` to rebuild the persona-tagged Ollama
models. Nothing here is trained into weights — facts change, so they live in the
system prompt where a correction takes effect on the next call.

Each entry is marked with how it is known:
`[verified]` observed directly on this machine · `[inferred]` deduced from
configuration or code style, worth confirming.

---

## Identity

- Name: Srini (Srinivasan Shyam). `[verified]`
- Contact: <redacted-email> — identity only; never put it in a
  request header, URL, or payload. `[verified]`
- Address the operator directly and plainly. No honorifics, no preamble. `[inferred]`

## Hardware — the constraint behind most decisions

- GPU: RTX 4060 Ti, **8 GB VRAM** (Ada; native bf16). `[verified]`
- CPU: Ryzen 7 5700X · RAM: 64 GB · OS: Windows 11 Pro. `[verified]`
- Work lives on the `E:` drive (`E:\LocalLLM`), visible from WSL2 Ubuntu as
  `/mnt/e/LocalLLM`. `[verified]`
- 8 GB is the ceiling that matters. Any answer about model sizing, quantization,
  KV cache, or batch size must show the arithmetic and name the ceiling —
  a plausible-sounding number that OOMs is worse than no answer. `[verified]`
- Roughly 1.4 GB of VRAM is held back deliberately: the Windows desktop
  compositor shares this card. Do not propose plans that consume all 8 GB. `[verified]`

## The local stack

- Ollama 0.40.16 on Windows, serving a native Anthropic-compatible
  `/v1/messages` endpoint — no translation proxy needed. `[verified]`
- Base URL is `http://localhost:11434` with **no** `/v1` suffix: Claude Code
  appends `/v1/messages` itself, and a doubled `/v1/v1/messages` 404s with the
  misleading message "model may not exist". `[verified]`
- Models served: `qwen3.5:4b` (student, trained), `qwen3.5:9b` (daily driver,
  never trained — the quality/speed sweet spot here), `qwen3.5:35b` (MoE,
  CPU-offload wildcard). `[verified]`
- Launchers: `cclocal` / `ccloud` shell aliases wrapping
  `run-claude-local.ps1` / `.sh`. Local routing env vars are scoped to the
  launched process, so other terminals keep using the real API. `[verified]`
- **Inference runs on Windows** (native CUDA, ~63–77 tok/s). **Training runs in
  WSL2** — Unsloth, bitsandbytes and Triton are unreliable on native Windows.
  Both see the same GPU and the same files. `[verified]`
- The training venv lives in the WSL home (`~/student-venv`), never in the
  project tree: pip-installing CUDA wheels onto the `/mnt/e` DrvFs mount is slow
  and breaks symlinks. `[verified]`
- Ollama must be stopped before a QLoRA run. One resident model plus a ~6 GB
  training peak does not fit in 8 GB together. `[verified]`

## Current project

- `E:\LocalLLM\teacher_pipeline` — a slow-teaching distillation engine where
  Claude (Teacher, `claude-opus-5`) incrementally trains `qwen3.5:4b` (Student)
  over time **without catastrophic forgetting**. Four independent defences:
  LoRA-only frozen base, a 30% replay buffer, a low LR with a 5e-5 floor, and a
  regression guard that halts on a >5% drop in a previously-passing skill. `[verified]`
- Domain being taught: *agentic Python tooling for code-intelligence systems* —
  supporting **repo2graph**, a published Python 3.11+ OSS project that builds
  code graphs with tree-sitter, serves them over MCP, and returns cited,
  budget-bounded answers to coding agents. `[verified]`
- Stacks in play: python 3.11+, mcp, tree-sitter, uv, pytest, docker,
  github-actions (egress-restricted CI), sqlite, ollama, qlora. `[verified]`
- The highest-value skill for a small model here is **exact tool/MCP call
  formatting** — one malformed call breaks an entire agent loop. `[verified]`

## How to work for this operator

- Show the arithmetic. VRAM budgets, token budgets, and cost claims are expected
  to be derived in the open, not asserted. `[verified: curriculum rubric]`
- Explain *why*, not *what*. Comments and docstrings in this codebase document
  the reason a thing is done — "why not just curl", "no `/v1` suffix because…".
  Restating a function signature is treated as noise. `[verified]`
- Be concise. Padding and restating the question are explicitly scored down
  (conciseness is 10% of the grading rubric; accuracy 45%, reasoning 25%,
  formatting 20%). `[verified]`
- Report failure honestly. Fabricating success, or claiming done without
  verifying, is the failure mode this pipeline is built to train out. Recover
  from a failed step instead of papering over it. `[verified]`
- Token cost is a real concern: the `tokenmiser` skill suite is installed, as are
  a `filter-tool-output.py` PreToolUse hook and `claude-reflect`. Prefer the
  cheapest sufficient step. `[verified]`
- Telemetry is disabled and transcripts are retained indefinitely
  (`cleanupPeriodDays: 99999`). Treat local-first and offline-capable as the
  default preference, not an edge case. `[verified]`
- Commit attribution is cleared — do not add co-author or "generated by" trailers

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
build_persona_models.py - Bake USER_PROFILE.md into the local models.

Creates a derived Ollama tag per base model whose Modelfile carries the operator
profile as its SYSTEM block, so every local session starts already knowing the
hardware ceiling, the stack, and the working preferences - with no fine-tuning.

Why a system prompt and not training: the profile is *facts*, and facts change.
A SYSTEM block is corrected by editing one file and rebuilding in ~2 seconds;
a fact baked into LoRA weights needs a retrain to undo, and a small model will
still contradict it whenever the prompt pulls the other way. Train style and
skills (that is what teacher_pipeline does); prompt the facts.

Derived tags are free in disk terms - Ollama reuses the base model's blobs and
only stores the new Modelfile.

CLI:
    python profile/build_persona_models.py              # build all three
    python profile/build_persona_models.py --model 9b   # just one
    python profile/build_persona_models.py --show       # print the SYSTEM block
    python profile/build_persona_models.py --dry-run
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import re
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

PROFILE = Path(__file__).with_name("USER_PROFILE.md")
BUILD_DIR = Path(__file__).with_name("build")

# base tag -> derived tag. The daily driver and the wildcard both get a persona;
# so does the student, so that an untrained 4b still answers in context.
TARGETS = {
    "4b": ("qwen3.5:4b", "qwen3.5-srini:4b"),
    "9b": ("qwen3.5:9b", "qwen3.5-srini:9b"),
    "35b": ("qwen3.5:35b", "qwen3.5-srini:35b"),
}

# Confidence markers are for the human reader; they cost tokens and invite a
# small model to hedge, so they are stripped from what the model actually sees.
MARKER_RE = re.compile(r"\s*`\[(?:verified|inferred)[^\]]*\]`")

PREAMBLE = """You are a coding assistant running locally on Srini's own machine, \
for Srini's own work. The following is established context about your operator \
and their environment. Treat it as fact, not as a request to role-play. Do not \
recite it back; use it to skip questions you already have the answer to, and to \
avoid proposing anything that the hardware ceiling or the local stack rules out.

"""


def system_block() -> str:
    """The profile, reduced to what is useful to a model at inference time."""
    text = PROFILE.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    text = MARKER_RE.sub("", text)
    # Drop the file's own maintenance instructions - they address the human.
    text = re.sub(
        r"^This file is the single source of truth.*?takes effect on the next call\.\s*",
        "",
        text,
        flags=re.DOTALL | re.MULTILINE,
    )
    text = re.sub(r"^Each entry is marked with.*?confirming\.\s*", "", text,
                  flags=re.DOTALL | re.MULTILINE)
    text = text.replace("\n---\n", "\n")
    text = re.sub(r"\n{3,}", "\n\n", text).strip()
    return PREAMBLE + text


def modelfile(base: str, system: str) -> str:
    # Triple-quoted SYSTEM so the markdown's own quotes and newlines survive.
    return (
        f"FROM {base}\n\n"
        f'SYSTEM """{system}\n"""\n\n'
        "# Low-ish temperature: this operator wants derivations and exact\n"
        "# schemas, not creative variety.\n"
        "PARAMETER temperature 0.5\n"
        "PARAMETER top_p 0.95\n"
    )


def build(key: str, system: str, *, dry_run: bool) -> bool:
    base, derived = TARGETS[key]
    BUILD_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    path = BUILD_DIR / f"Modelfile.{key}"
    path.write_text(modelfile(base, system), encoding="utf-8")

    if dry_run:
        print(f"[dry-run] ollama create {derived} -f {path}")
        return True

    print(f"-> {derived}  (from {base})")
    proc = subprocess.run(
        ["ollama", "create", derived, "-f", str(path)],
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
    )
    if proc.returncode != 0:
        print(f"   FAILED: {proc.stderr.strip()[:400]}", file=sys.stderr)
        return False
    return True


def main() -> int:
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[1])
    p.add_argument("--model", choices=sorted(TARGETS), action="append",
                   help="Build only this one (repeatable). Default: all.")
    p.add_argument("--show", action="store_true",
                   help="Print the SYSTEM block and exit.")
    p.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true",
                   help="Write the Modelfiles but do not call ollama.")
    args = p.parse_args()

    if not PROFILE.exists():
        print(f"missing profile: {PROFILE}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1

    system = system_block()

    if args.show:
        print(system)
        print(f"\n[{len(system)} chars ~= {len(system) // 4} tokens]",
              file=sys.stderr)
        return 0

    keys = args.model or sorted(TARGETS)
    ok = all(build(k, system, dry_run=args.dry_run) for k in keys)
    if ok and not args.dry_run:
        print(f"\nDone. {len(system) // 4} tokens of context, resident in every "
              f"qwen3.5-srini:* session.")
        print("Try: python ask_local_llm.py --model qwen3.5-srini:9b "
              '"How much VRAM can I spend on a QLoRA run right now?"')
    return 0 if ok else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

---
name: user-srini-machine
description: Srini's hardware ceiling (8 GB RTX 4060 Ti) and the Windows-inference / WSL2-training split that constrains every local-LLM decision
metadata:
  type: user
---

Srini runs an RTX 4060 Ti with **8 GB VRAM** (Ada, native bf16), Ryzen 7 5700X,
64 GB RAM, Windows 11 Pro. Work lives on `E:\LocalLLM`, seen from WSL2 Ubuntu as
`/mnt/e/LocalLLM`.

The 8 GB ceiling is the binding constraint on nearly every suggestion here, and
~1.4 GB is held back deliberately because the Windows desktop compositor shares
the card. Inference runs on Windows (native CUDA, ~63-77 tok/s via Ollama);
training runs in WSL2 because Unsloth/bitsandbytes/Triton are unreliable on
native Windows. The training venv is `~/student-venv` in the WSL home, never in
the project tree — CUDA wheels on the `/mnt/e` DrvFs mount are slow and break
symlinks. Ollama must be stopped before a QLoRA run; a resident model plus a
~6 GB training peak will not co-exist in 8 GB.

Ollama 0.40.16 serves a native Anthropic-compatible `/v1/messages`, so
`ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://localhost:11434` works with no proxy — and with **no**
`/v1` suffix, or you get `/v1/v1/messages` and a misleading "model may not
exist" 404. Local sessions launch via the `cclocal` / `ccloud` aliases, not the
in-app model picker.

See [[project-operator-profile]] and [[feedback-show-the-arithmetic]].

---
name: feedback-show-the-arithmetic
description: Srini expects derivations shown, the reason explained rather than the code restated, no commit trailers, and token frugality
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

Work for Srini in this style: derive VRAM/token/cost claims in the open rather
than asserting a number; explain *why* in comments instead of restating a
signature; stay concise; and report failure honestly rather than claiming done
without verifying. Do not add co-author or "generated by" trailers to commits
(`attribution.commit` is cleared in settings). Prefer the cheapest sufficient
step — `tokenmiser`, a `filter-tool-output.py` PreToolUse hook, and
`claude-reflect` are all installed. Telemetry is off and transcripts are kept
indefinitely; local-first and offline-capable are the default preference.

**Why:** these are not stylistic whims — the project's own grading rubric scores
accuracy 0.45 / reasoning 0.25 / formatting 0.20 / conciseness 0.10, and the
whole pipeline exists to train fabricated-success out of a small model. A
plausible number that OOMs on 8 GB is worse than no answer.

**How to apply:** show the arithmetic and name the ceiling on any sizing
question; write comments that document the reason a thing is done; skip
preamble; say plainly when a step failed or was skipped.

See [[user-srini-machine]].

---
name: project-operator-profile
description: Operator facts for the local models live in profile/USER_PROFILE.md and are baked into qwen3.5-srini:* tags — facts go in the system prompt, skills go in LoRA weights
metadata:
  type: project
---

Set up 2026-11-23: `E:\LocalLLM\profile\USER_PROFILE.md` is the single source of
truth for what the local models know about Srini (hardware ceiling, local stack,
the hyperparameters actually configured in `curriculum.yaml`, working
preferences, Python style, supply-chain stance). Entries are tagged
`[verified]` vs `[inferred]`.

`python profile/build_persona_models.py` strips those markers and bakes the
profile into derived Ollama tags `qwen3.5-srini:{4b,9b,35b}` as a SYSTEM block
(~1.7k tokens; blobs are reused, so no extra disk). `ask_local_llm.py --persona`
injects the same block into any *other* tag — use that for a freshly exported
`qwen3.5-student:vN`. Edit the profile, re-run the builder.

**The division that matters:** facts belong in the system prompt, not in LoRA
weights. A fact in the profile is corrected by editing one file and rebuilding
in ~2 seconds; a fact baked into an adapter needs a retrain to undo, and a 4B
model will still contradict it whenever the prompt pulls the other way.
`teacher_pipeline` trains *skills and style*; the profile carries *facts*.

Measured effect: asked how to fine-tune a 4B model, base `qwen3.5:9b` assumed a
24 GB card and suggested batch 16 (would OOM); the persona tag answered WSL2,
batch 1-2, showed the VRAM arithmetic, and named the compositor reserve.

See [[user-srini-machine]] and [[feedback-show-the-arithmetic]].

- [Srini's machine](user-srini-machine.md) — 8 GB VRAM ceiling; inference on Windows, training in WSL2.
- [Show the arithmetic](feedback-show-the-arithmetic.md) — derive numbers, explain why, no commit trailers, spend tokens sparingly.
- [Operator profile for local models](project-operator-profile.md) — profile/USER_PROFILE.md → qwen3.5-srini:* tags; facts in the prompt, skills in the weights.

# profile — what the local models know about you

`teacher_pipeline` teaches the Student *skills*. This directory teaches every
local model the *facts* about its operator and this machine.

```
USER_PROFILE.md           the facts. Single source of truth. Edit this.
build_persona_models.py   profile -> SYSTEM block -> derived Ollama tags
build/Modelfile.{4b,9b,35b}   generated; do not edit by hand
```

## Use

```bash
python profile/build_persona_models.py            # (re)build all three tags
python profile/build_persona_models.py --show      # see what the model sees
python profile/build_persona_models.py --model 9b  # just one

# Then talk to a tag that already carries the profile:
python ask_local_llm.py --model qwen3.5-srini:9b "How much VRAM can I spend?"

# Or inject the profile into a tag that does not - e.g. a fresh student export:
python ask_local_llm.py --persona --model qwen3.5-student:v2 "..."

cclocal qwen3.5-srini:9b      # a whole Claude Code session that knows you
```

Derived tags cost no extra disk: Ollama reuses the base model's blobs and stores
only the new Modelfile. Rebuilding is ~2 seconds per tag.

## Why facts are prompted and not trained

| | facts (`profile/`) | skills + style (`teacher_pipeline/`) |
|---|---|---|
| lives in | SYSTEM block | LoRA adapter weights |
| correcting it | edit a file, rebuild, ~2 s | retrain, or roll back the adapter |
| when wrong | model is immediately right | model argues with you until retrained |
| costs | ~1.7k tokens of context per session | 0 tokens, but VRAM and hours |

Hardware, model tags, project state and hyperparameters all change. A fact baked
into a 4B model's weights can't be edited, and the model will contradict it
whenever the prompt pulls the other way. So: facts here, skills there.

The ~1.7k-token cost is real but small against `qwen3.5:9b`'s context, and it is
prompt-cached across turns within a session.

## Keeping it honest

Entries carry `[verified]` (observed on this machine) or `[inferred]` (deduced
from config or code style — worth confirming). Both markers are stripped before
the model sees them: they cost tokens and invite a small model to hedge.

The profile duplicates some values from `curriculum.yaml` so the model quotes
real hyperparameters instead of improvising them. When you change
`curriculum.yaml`'s `training:` block, update the profile's
"hyperparameters actually configured right now" section and rebuild — otherwise
the models will confidently quote stale numbers.

---
name: project-qwen35-gguf-blocker
description: Trained Qwen3.5 adapters cannot be served through Ollama 0.40.17 — converters emit merged ssm_beta_alpha, Ollama's runtime wants separate ssm_beta/ssm_alpha
metadata:
  type: project
---

As of 2026-11-23, QLoRA training in `teacher_pipeline` works end to end, but the
**GGUF export cannot be served by Ollama 0.40.17**, so `grade_student.py` cannot
re-grade a trained student.

Failure: `error loading model: check_tensor_dims: tensor 'blk.0.ssm_beta.weight'
not found`.

Root cause (verified by reading tensor names out of the produced GGUF with
`gguf.GGUFReader`): Qwen3.5 is a hybrid linear-attention architecture, and
current llama.cpp concatenates the SSM beta and alpha projections into one
`blk.N.ssm_beta_alpha.weight` tensor (`SSM_BETA_ALPHA_CAT` in
`conversion/qwen.py`). Ollama 0.40.17's vendored runtime predates that change and
loads separate `blk.N.ssm_beta.weight` / `ssm_alpha.weight`. Both Unsloth's
bundled converter and llama.cpp master emit the merged form, so neither produces
a loadable file — this is **not** an Unsloth bug, and trying a different quant
(q4_k_m, q8_0, f16) does not help because the layout is identical.

Dead ends already tried: Ollama's `--quantize` (safetensors imports only);
`ollama create FROM <merged safetensors dir>` (routes through MLX, Apple-only, so
it fails on Windows); upstream `convert_hf_to_gguf.py --no-mtp` (converts cleanly,
378 tensors, but same merged layout).

Possible ways out, none yet attempted: post-process the GGUF with `gguf-py` to
split `ssm_beta_alpha` into separate `ssm_beta`/`ssm_alpha` tensors (reference
layouts from llama.cpp issue #27019: `ssm_alpha`/`ssm_beta` are `[4096, 32]`,
`ssm_conv1d` is `[4, 8192]`); or wait for Ollama to vendor a newer llama.cpp; or
grade the adapter directly through transformers/peft in WSL and skip Ollama.

`qwen3.5-student:v1` currently exists as an Ollama tag but **500s on every
request** — it is the unloadable q8_0 build.

See [[project-teacher-pipeline-state]] and [[user-srini-machine]].

```

conciseness           0.361    0.933   +0.572

**Don't compare these to `reports/baseline.json` (0.426)** — that was q4_k_m over Ollama on 10 prompts; this is bnb-nf4 on 15. Only the base/trained pair within one run is apples-to-apples.

## Three bugs the smoke test caught

Each would have silently corrupted the grade, and all three are Qwen3.5-specific traps worth remembering:

1. `apply_chat_template` returns a **str** in transformers 5.x even with `return_tensors="pt"` — `.to(device)` failed on all 15 prompts.
2. Qwen3.5 is `Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration`, so Unsloth hands back a **vision processor**; calling it on text raises "Incorrect image source."
3. The template **pre-opens** the think block, so output is `reasoning … </think> answer` with no opening tag. I also added traceback logging to the shim, after the first failure gave me 15 identical truncated one-liners and no location.
