input.content:
@echo off
REM Immich control script.  Usage:  immich [start|stop|status|logs|update|open]
REM Double-clicking this file runs "status".

setlocal
set DOCKER="%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\DockerDesktop\Docker Desktop.exe"
set COMPOSE=docker compose
cd /d "%~dp0"

set CMD=%1
if "%CMD%"=="" set CMD=status

REM --- make sure the Docker engine is running before doing anything ---
docker info >nul 2>&1
if errorlevel 1 (
  echo Docker engine is not running. Starting Docker Desktop...
  start "" %DOCKER%
  echo Waiting for the engine ^(this can take a minute^)...
  for /l %%i in (1,1,60) do (
    timeout /t 5 /nobreak >nul
    docker info >nul 2>&1 && goto :engine_up
  )
  echo.
  echo ERROR: Docker engine did not come up. Open Docker Desktop manually and retry.
  goto :end
)
:engine_up

if /i "%CMD%"=="start"  goto :start
if /i "%CMD%"=="stop"   goto :stop
if /i "%CMD%"=="status" goto :status
if /i "%CMD%"=="logs"   goto :logs
if /i "%CMD%"=="update" goto :update
if /i "%CMD%"=="open"   goto :open
echo Unknown command "%CMD%".  Use: start ^| stop ^| status ^| logs ^| update ^| open
goto :end

:start
echo Starting Immich...
%COMPOSE% up -d
echo.
echo Immich is at http://localhost:2283
goto :end

:stop
echo Stopping Immich ^(data is kept^)...
%COMPOSE% stop
goto :end

:status
%COMPOSE% ps
echo.
echo --- reachability ---
curl -s -m 10 -o nul -w "  http://localhost:2283 -> HTTP %%{http_code}\n" http://localhost:2283/ 2>nul
if errorlevel 1 echo   could not reach http://localhost:2283
goto :end

:logs
echo Showing logs. Press Ctrl+C to exit.
%COMPOSE% logs -f --tail=100
goto :end

:update
REM Image pulls happen on the HOST, which does have internet. The containers
REM themselves stay sealed. New ML models are the exception -- see the comments
REM at the bottom of docker-compose.yml.
echo Pulling new images...
%COMPOSE% pull
echo Recreating containers...
%COMPOSE% up -d
echo.
echo Done. Old images can be cleaned up with:  docker image prune
goto :end

:open
start "" http://localhost:2283
goto :end

:end
echo.
if "%1"=="" pause
endlocal

options.label: External library, read-only (Recommended)
options.description: Immich indexes the files where they sit. No copying, no duplicate disk use, and a read-only mount means Immich physically cannot alter or delete your originals. Your year-folder structure stays exactly as it is. Best when you want Immich as a fast viewer/search layer over an archive you keep managing yourself.

- can't delete or move photos from inside Immich
- you add new photos by dropping them in the folder

options.label: Upload into Immich's own library
options.description: Files are copied into E:\immich-library and Immich fully owns them. You can delete, move and organize from inside the app, and it behaves like Google Photos. Costs a second copy on disk and your year-folders are no longer the source of truth.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Immich indexing progress. Usage: bash progress.sh [seconds_between_samples]
# Run with no args for a one-shot snapshot, or e.g. "bash progress.sh 60" to watch.

Q() { docker exec immich_postgres psql -U postgres -d immich -tAc "$1" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' \r'; }

snapshot() {
  TOTAL=$(Q "select count(*) from asset;")
  META=$(Q  "select count(*) from asset_job_status where \"metadataExtractedAt\" is not null;")
  THUMB=$(Q "select count(*) from asset_file where type='thumbnail';")
  FACES=$(Q "select count(*) from asset_job_status where \"facesRecognizedAt\" is not null;")
  SMART=$(Q "select count(*) from smart_search;")
  PEOPLE=$(Q "select count(*) from person;")
  OCR=$(Q   "select count(*) from asset_job_status where \"ocrAt\" is not null;")
}

bar() { # bar <done> <total>
  local d=$1 t=$2 w=32
  [ "${t:-0}" -eq 0 ] && { printf "n/a"; return; }
  local f=$(( d * w / t )) p=$(( d * 100 / t ))
  printf "["
  for ((i=0;i<w;i++)); do [ $i -lt $f ] && printf "#" || printf "."; done
  printf "] %3d%%  %s/%s" "$p" "$d" "$t"
}

show() {
  echo "  metadata     $(bar "${META:-0}"  "$TOTAL")"
  echo "  thumbnails   $(bar "${THUMB:-0}" "$TOTAL")"
  echo "  faces        $(bar "${FACES:-0}" "$TOTAL")"
  echo "  smart search $(bar "${SMART:-0}" "$TOTAL")"
  echo "  ocr          $(bar "${OCR:-0}"   "$TOTAL")"
  echo "  people found: ${PEOPLE:-0}"
}

INTERVAL=${1:-0}

snapshot
echo "=== Immich indexing progress  ($(date '+%H:%M:%S')) ==="
show

if [ "$INTERVAL" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
  while true; do
    P_META=$META; P_THUMB=$THUMB; P_FACES=$FACES; P_SMART=$SMART
    sleep "$INTERVAL"
    snapshot
    echo
    echo "=== $(date '+%H:%M:%S')  (last ${INTERVAL}s) ==="
    show
    RATE=$(( (THUMB - P_THUMB) ))
    if [ "$RATE" -gt 0 ]; then
      LEFT=$(( TOTAL - THUMB ))
      ETA=$(( LEFT * INTERVAL / RATE / 60 ))
      echo "  rate: ${RATE} thumbs/${INTERVAL}s  ->  ~${ETA} min remaining for thumbnails"
    fi
    if [ "${THUMB:-0}" -ge "${TOTAL:-1}" ] && [ "${SMART:-0}" -ge "${TOTAL:-1}" ]; then
      echo "  ALL DONE"; break
    fi
  done
fi

echo
echo "=== GPU ==="
docker exec immich_machine_learning nvidia-smi \
  --query-gpu=utilization.gpu,utilization.encoder,memory.used \
  --format=csv,noheader 2>/dev/null | sed 's/^/  compute\/encoder\/vram: /'

def ini_set(path, key, old, new):

# Blocks Actual Budget from all network access via Windows Firewall.
# MUST be run as Administrator.  Re-running is safe (rules are recreated).

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'

$exe = "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\desktop-electron\Actual.exe"

if (-not (Test-Path $exe)) {
    Write-Error "Actual.exe not found at $exe - is Actual Budget installed?"
}

$rules = @(
    @{ Name = 'Actual Budget - Block Outbound'; Direction = 'Outbound' },
    @{ Name = 'Actual Budget - Block Inbound';  Direction = 'Inbound'  }
)

foreach ($r in $rules) {
    Get-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName $r.Name -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
        Remove-NetFirewallRule -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

    New-NetFirewallRule `
        -DisplayName $r.Name `
        -Description 'Keeps Actual Budget fully offline (local-only finances).' `
        -Program $exe `
        -Direction $r.Direction `
        -Action Block `
        -Profile Any `
        -Enabled True | Out-Null

    Write-Host "Created: $($r.Name)" -ForegroundColor Green
}

Write-Host ""
Write-Host "Actual Budget is now blocked from all inbound and outbound network traffic." -ForegroundColor Cyan
Write-Host "Program: $exe"

# Zips every Actual Budget file into a timestamped local backup.
# No admin required.  Nothing leaves this machine.

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'

$docDir    = "$env:USERPROFILE\Documents\Actual"
$backupDir = 'E:\LocalLLM\actual-budget\backups'
$keep      = 30   # number of backups to retain

if (-not (Test-Path $docDir)) { Write-Error "No budget directory at $docDir" }
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $backupDir | Out-Null

$stamp = Get-Date -Format 'yyyy-MM-dd_HHmmss'
$dest  = Join-Path $backupDir "actual-backup_$stamp.zip"

Compress-Archive -Path "$docDir\*" -DestinationPath $dest -CompressionLevel Optimal

$size = "{0:N1} MB" -f ((Get-Item $dest).Length / 1MB)
Write-Host "Backup written: $dest ($size)" -ForegroundColor Green

# Prune old backups
$old = Get-ChildItem $backupDir -Filter 'actual-backup_*.zip' |
       Sort-Object LastWriteTime -Descending | Select-Object -Skip $keep
if ($old) {
    $old | Remove-Item -Force
    Write-Host "Pruned $($old.Count) old backup(s), keeping the newest $keep." -ForegroundColor DarkGray
}

| Backups | `backups\actual-backup_<timestamp>.zip` |

Installer SHA-256 verified against the GitHub release:
`57fec4fd4484fa4fb9ac2dd015b9af581b60a00cd798679921b418bfee118cc2`

## Why it's offline

1. **No sync server.** Actual only talks to a network when you configure a sync
   server. `server-url` is `null`, so the app runs in local-file mode and all
   data lives in the SQLite file above.
2. **Firewall block.** Two Windows Firewall rules deny Actual.exe all inbound
   and outbound traffic on every profile. This also kills update checks and
   any bank-sync (SimpleFIN / GoCardless) attempt.

## Scripts

```powershell
# One-time, run as Administrator — creates the firewall block rules
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File E:\LocalLLM\actual-budget\block-actual-internet.ps1

# Any time — confirms app, local-only mode, and firewall rules are all in place
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File E:\LocalLLM\actual-budget\verify-offline.ps1

# Any time — zips all budgets to backups\, keeps the newest 30
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File E:\LocalLLM\actual-budget\backup-budget.ps1
```

## Day-to-day

- Launch from the Start menu ("Actual").
- Enter transactions manually, or import OFX/QFX/CSV files you download from
  your bank yourself (**Import** on an account page). Bank auto-sync is
  deliberately unavailable here — it requires internet.
- Back up before anything risky: run `backup-budget.ps1`. Actual's own
  **Settings → Export** also writes a self-contained `.zip` you can restore
  on any machine.

## Updating later

Updates require internet, so they're a deliberate act:

1. Download the new `Actual-windows-x64.exe` from
   <https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/releases> and verify its SHA-256
   against the digest on that release page.
2. Run `backup-budget.ps1`.
3. Run the installer.
4. Re-run `block-actual-internet.ps1` as Administrator, then `verify-offline.ps1`.

The install path doesn't change between versions, so the firewall rules keep
matching — but re-run the verify script to be sure.

instruction:
Act as an autonomous AI Systems Architect and ML Engineer. Execute the following 4-phase pipeline step-by-step on my machine. Pause and ask for my explicit approval before downloading multi-gigabyte model weights or running long training jobs.

### PHASE 1: Hardware & Environment Audit
1. Run terminal commands to scan my exact system specifications:
   - OS, Architecture (x86_64 vs Apple Silicon), and CPU cores/threads.
   - Total System RAM and currently available RAM.
   - GPU vendor, model, driver/CUDA/Metal/ROCm version, and exact VRAM capacity.
   - Available disk space on the primary drive.
   - Existing AI runtimes already installed (Python, uv, Conda, Ollama, llama.cpp, LM Studio, vLLM, Unsloth, Docker).
2. Output a clean Markdown hardware summary table. Based on my exact VRAM/RAM ceiling and memory bandwidth, recommend:
   - **Best Daily-Driver Inference Model** (quantized GGUF, e.g., Q4_K_M / UD-Q4_K_XL, that fits comfortably in VRAM/unified memory with room for at least a 16k–32k context window).
   - **Best Trainable Student Model** (base/instruct weights that can be fine-tuned locally using QLoRA/Unsloth within my VRAM limits, or fallback to CPU/cloud if VRAM < 8GB).

### PHASE 2: Local Runtime Setup & Claude Integration
1. Once I approve your model picks, install/configure the optimal local inference server (`llama.cpp`, Ollama, or Unsloth) with full GPU acceleration enabled.
2. Download the approved inference model and verify it responds over a local OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible API (`http://localhost:11434` or `http://localhost:8888`).
3. Create a bridge so you (Claude) and I can interact with the local model directly:
   - Configure a local tool/MCP script (`ask_local_llm.py`) or shell wrapper so you can send prompts to the local model, inspect its outputs, and grade its responses programmatically.
   - Also generate a helper launch script (`run-claude-local.sh` / `.ps1`) showing how I can point Claude Code directly at the local model endpoint (`ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`) whenever I want zero-cost offline execution.

### PHASE 3: Build the "Slow-Teaching" Distillation & Learning Engine
Build a structured project directory (`./teacher_pipeline/`) that allows you (Claude, acting as the Teacher) to gradually train and improve the local model (the Student) over time without catastrophic forgetting:
1. **Curriculum & Domain Spec (`curriculum.yaml`)**: Ask me what specific skills, coding stacks, workflows, or reasoning tasks I want the local LLM to learn from you.
2. **Interaction Logger & Synthetic Data Generator (`generate_lessons.py`)**:
   - Create a pipeline that captures high-value prompt/response pairs from our sessions—specifically preserving your step-by-step reasoning traces (`<thinking>` / Chain-of-Thought) and exact tool-call formatting.
   - Include a deduplication and quality-filtering step so only verified, high-signal examples enter `./teacher_pipeline/dataset/train.jsonl`.
3. **Evaluation & Grading Harness (`grade_student.py`)**:
   - Write a benchmark script where you give the local student model unseen test prompts from the curriculum, grade its answers against your own reference outputs (scoring accuracy, formatting, and reasoning), and log weak areas to target in the next lesson batch.
4. **Incremental QLoRA Fine-Tuning Script (`train_student.py`)**:
   - Set up an Unsloth / Hugging Face `trl` (SFTTrainer) QLoRA training script calibrated to my exact GPU VRAM (configured with safe batch sizes, gradient accumulation, low learning rate `2e-4` -> `5e-5` cosine decay, and checkpointing) so I can run periodic incremental updates ("micro-epochs") as the dataset grows, then automatically export/merge the updated LoRA adapter back into GGUF for local serving.

### PHASE 4: Initialize First Lesson
Once the infrastructure is verified:
1. Ask me for my primary target domain/use case.
2. Generate the first batch of 25 curated training examples with Chain-of-Thought reasoning, run a baseline evaluation on the un-tuned local model, and show me the exact command to kick off Lesson 1.

# start-ollama.ps1 - Launch the Ollama server tuned for an RTX 4060 Ti (8 GB VRAM).
#
# Why this script exists: the Ollama desktop tray app ignores OLLAMA_MODELS and
# stores models on C:. Running `ollama serve` ourselves keeps the store on E: and
# lets us set the flags that make a 9B model fit in 8 GB at 32k context.
#
# Usage:  powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File E:\LocalLLM\start-ollama.ps1

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'

$env:OLLAMA_MODELS = 'E:\LocalLLM\models'
$env:OLLAMA_HOST   = '127.0.0.1:11434'

# --- 8 GB VRAM tuning -------------------------------------------------------
# Flash attention cuts KV-cache memory and speeds up prompt processing.
$env:OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION = '1'
# q8_0 KV cache ~halves context memory vs fp16. This is what buys us 32k on a
# 5.7 GB model inside a 7.2 GiB usable budget.
$env:OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE   = 'q8_0'
# Default context for all models unless a request overrides it.
$env:OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH  = '32768'
# Only one model resident at a time - two would blow the VRAM ceiling.
$env:OLLAMA_MAX_LOADED_MODELS = '1'
# Keep weights warm between prompts so we don't pay reload cost each call.
$env:OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE      = '30m'

$exe = 'C:\Users\Srini\AppData\Local\Programs\Ollama\ollama.exe'

# If a server is already up, don't start a second one.
try {
    $null = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri 'http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/version' -TimeoutSec 3
    Write-Host 'Ollama already running on 127.0.0.1:11434' -ForegroundColor Yellow
    exit 0
} catch { }

Write-Host "Starting Ollama (models: $env:OLLAMA_MODELS)" -ForegroundColor Cyan
Start-Process -FilePath $exe -ArgumentList 'serve' -WindowStyle Hidden

# Wait for the API to answer rather than guessing with a fixed sleep.
for ($i = 0; $i -lt 30; $i++) {
    Start-Sleep -Seconds 1
    try {
        $v = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri 'http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/version' -TimeoutSec 2
        Write-Host "Ollama $($v.version) ready on http://127.0.0.1:11434" -ForegroundColor Green
        exit 0
    } catch { }
}

Write-Error 'Ollama did not come up within 30s.'
exit 1

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
ask_local_llm.py - Bridge between Claude (the Teacher) and the local model (the Student).

Claude calls this to send prompts to the local Ollama server, inspect the
Student's reasoning, and grade it programmatically. It is also imported as a
module by teacher_pipeline/grade_student.py.

Why not just curl: Qwen3.5 is a hybrid-reasoning model. Ollama returns its
chain-of-thought in a separate `thinking` field, and `num_predict` is shared
between thinking and the final answer - so a small token budget yields an empty
`content`. This wrapper handles that, separates the two channels, and reports
timing so we can see the real cost of each call.

CLI:
    python ask_local_llm.py "What is a LoRA adapter?"
    python ask_local_llm.py --think "Bat and ball cost $1.10..." --max-tokens 2000
    python ask_local_llm.py --model qwen3.5:9b --json "Write a Python LRU cache"
    echo "long prompt" | python ask_local_llm.py --stdin --json

Module:
    from ask_local_llm import ask
    r = ask("prompt", model="qwen3.5:4b", think=True)
    r.content, r.thinking, r.tokens_per_sec
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import os
import sys
import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.request
from dataclasses import dataclass, asdict, field

OLLAMA_HOST = os.environ.get("OLLAMA_HOST", "127.0.0.1:11434")
if not OLLAMA_HOST.startswith("http"):
    OLLAMA_HOST = f"http://{OLLAMA_HOST}"

DEFAULT_MODEL = os.environ.get("LOCAL_LLM_MODEL", "qwen3.5:4b")

# In thinking mode the model routinely spends 500-1500 tokens reasoning before
# emitting a single token of answer. Budget for that or `content` comes back "".
DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS_THINK = 2048
DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS_PLAIN = 1024


@dataclass
class LocalReply:
    """One response from the Student, with both channels kept separate."""

    content: str
    thinking: str
    model: str
    prompt_tokens: int = 0
    completion_tokens: int = 0
    wall_seconds: float = 0.0
    tokens_per_sec: float = 0.0
    truncated: bool = False
    error: str | None = None
    messages: list = field(default_factory=list)

    def to_json(self, indent: int = 2) -> str:
        return json.dumps(asdict(self), indent=indent, ensure_ascii=False)


def _post(path: str, payload: dict, timeout: int) -> dict:
    req = urllib.request.Request(
        f"{OLLAMA_HOST}{path}",
        data=json.dumps(payload).encode("utf-8"),
        headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"},
        method="POST",
    )
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=timeout) as resp:
        return json.loads(resp.read().decode("utf-8"))


def ask(
    prompt: str,
    *,
    model: str = DEFAULT_MODEL,
    system: str | None = None,
    think: bool = False,
    max_tokens: int | None = None,
    temperature: float = 0.6,
    top_p: float = 0.95,
    num_ctx: int | None = None,
    timeout: int = 900,
    history: list | None = None,
) -> LocalReply:
    """Send one prompt to the local model and return both channels separately.

    `think=False` disables the reasoning channel, which is what you want for
    fast deterministic checks. `think=True` exposes the chain-of-thought in
    `.thinking` - that trace is the raw material for distillation.
    """
    if max_tokens is None:
        max_tokens = DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS_THINK if think else DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS_PLAIN

    messages = list(history or [])
    if system:
        messages.insert(0, {"role": "system", "content": system})
    messages.append({"role": "user", "content": prompt})

    options = {
        "num_predict": max_tokens,
        "temperature": temperature,
        "top_p": top_p,
    }
    if num_ctx:
        options["num_ctx"] = num_ctx

    payload = {
        "model": model,
        "messages": messages,
        "think": think,
        "stream": False,
        "options": options,
    }

    started = time.time()
    try:
        data = _post("/api/chat", payload, timeout)
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
        body = e.read().decode("utf-8", "replace")[:500]
        return LocalReply("", "", model, error=f"HTTP {e.code}: {body}",
                          wall_seconds=round(time.time() - started, 2))
    except Exception as e:  # connection refused, timeout, ...
        return LocalReply("", "", model, error=f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}",
                          wall_seconds=round(time.time() - started, 2))

    wall = time.time() - started
    msg = data.get("message", {}) or {}
    content = (msg.get("content") or "").strip()
    thinking = (msg.get("thinking") or "").strip()

    eval_count = data.get("eval_count", 0) or 0
    eval_dur = data.get("eval_duration", 0) or 0
    tps = round(eval_count / (eval_dur / 1e9), 1) if eval_dur else 0.0

    # If we hit the ceiling and produced only reasoning, the answer was cut off.
    truncated = eval_count >= max_tokens and not content

    messages.append({"role": "assistant", "content": content})

    return LocalReply(
        content=content,
        thinking=thinking,
        model=data.get("model", model),
        prompt_tokens=data.get("prompt_eval_count", 0) or 0,
        completion_tokens=eval_count,
        wall_seconds=round(wall, 2),
        tokens_per_sec=tps,
        truncated=truncated,
        messages=messages,
    )


def health() -> dict:
    """Server reachability plus which models are available and resident."""
    out = {"host": OLLAMA_HOST, "up": False, "version": None, "models": [], "loaded": []}
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(f"{OLLAMA_HOST}/api/version", timeout=5) as r:
            out["version"] = json.loads(r.read())["version"]
            out["up"] = True
    except Exception as e:
        out["error"] = f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"
        return out
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(f"{OLLAMA_HOST}/api/tags", timeout=10) as r:
            out["models"] = [m["name"] for m in json.loads(r.read()).get("models", [])]
        with urllib.request.urlopen(f"{OLLAMA_HOST}/api/ps", timeout=10) as r:
            out["loaded"] = [
                {"name": m["name"], "size_gb": round(m.get("size", 0) / 1e9, 2),
                 "ctx": m.get("context_length")}
                for m in json.loads(r.read()).get("models", [])
            ]
    except Exception as e:
        out["error"] = f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"
    return out


def main() -> int:
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Ask the local LLM (Ollama) a question.")
    p.add_argument("prompt", nargs="*", help="Prompt text.")
    p.add_argument("--stdin", action="store_true", help="Read the prompt from stdin.")
    p.add_argument("--model", default=DEFAULT_MODEL)
    p.add_argument("--system", default=None, help="Optional system prompt.")
    p.add_argument("--think", action="store_true", help="Enable the reasoning channel.")
    p.add_argument("--max-tokens", type=int, default=None)
    p.add_argument("--temperature", type=float, default=0.6)
    p.add_argument("--num-ctx", type=int, default=None)
    p.add_argument("--timeout", type=int, default=900)
    p.add_argument("--json", action="store_true", dest="as_json",
                   help="Emit the full structured reply (for programmatic grading).")
    p.add_argument("--health", action="store_true", help="Probe the server and exit.")
    args = p.parse_args()

    if args.health:
        print(json.dumps(health(), indent=2))
        return 0

    prompt = sys.stdin.read() if args.stdin else " ".join(args.prompt)
    if not prompt.strip():
        p.error("no prompt given (pass text, or use --stdin)")

    r = ask(
        prompt,
        model=args.model,
        system=args.system,
        think=args.think,
        max_tokens=args.max_tokens,
        temperature=args.temperature,
        num_ctx=args.num_ctx,
        timeout=args.timeout,
    )

    if args.as_json:
        print(r.to_json())
        return 1 if r.error else 0

    if r.error:
        print(f"ERROR: {r.error}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    if r.thinking:
        print(f"--- thinking ({len(r.thinking)} chars) ---\n{r.thinking}\n--- answer ---")
    print(r.content or "(empty - the token budget was spent on reasoning; raise --max-tokens)")
    print(
        f"\n[{r.model} | {r.completion_tokens} tok | {r.tokens_per_sec} tok/s | {r.wall_seconds}s"
        + (" | TRUNCATED" if r.truncated else "") + "]",
        file=sys.stderr,
    )
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# curriculum.yaml - What the Student must learn from the Teacher.
#
# This file is the single source of truth for the whole pipeline:
#   generate_lessons.py  reads `skills` to know what examples to synthesize
#   grade_student.py     reads `rubric` + `eval` to know how to score
#   train_student.py     reads `training` for the VRAM-calibrated hyperparameters
#
# Calibrated for: RTX 4060 Ti 8 GB | Ryzen 7 5700X | 64 GB RAM | WSL2 Ubuntu

meta:
  student_model: qwen3.5:4b                      # served (Ollama tag)
  student_hf_repo: unsloth/Qwen3.5-4B            # trained (HF repo, 4-bit QLoRA)
  teacher: claude-opus-5                          # Claude, acting as Teacher
  daily_driver: qwen3.5:9b                        # untouched by training
  created: 2026-11-22
  version: 1

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# DOMAIN - set during Phase 4. Everything downstream keys off this.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
domain:
  name: "TBD"
  description: "TBD - set in Phase 4"
  # Stacks/tools the Student is expected to be fluent in.
  stacks: []

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# SKILLS - one block per competency. `weight` controls how many examples
# generate_lessons.py synthesizes for it (relative share of the batch).
# `difficulty` ladders: lessons start easy and escalate across micro-epochs.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
skills: []
#  - id: tool_call_format
#    name: "Exact tool-call formatting"
#    weight: 3
#    difficulty: [easy, medium, hard]
#    description: >
#      Emit tool calls with precise JSON schema adherence - correct names,
#      no invented parameters, no prose wrapped around the call.
#    must_include: ["valid JSON", "no hallucinated params"]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# RUBRIC - how grade_student.py scores an answer. Weights must sum to 1.0.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
rubric:
  weights:
    accuracy: 0.45      # is the substance correct?
    reasoning: 0.25     # is the chain-of-thought sound, not just the answer?
    formatting: 0.20    # does it match the required output shape exactly?
    conciseness: 0.10   # no padding, no restating the question
  pass_threshold: 0.70  # below this, the skill is logged as weak
  scale: 5              # per-criterion scoring is 0-5, normalized to 0-1

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# DATA GENERATION
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
generation:
  batch_size: 25                 # examples per lesson batch
  include_thinking: true         # preserve the Teacher's CoT in the target
  thinking_tag: "think"          # wrapped as <think>...</think> in training text
  min_chars: 120                 # reject stubs
  max_chars: 12000               # reject runaway outputs
  dedupe:
    method: minhash_jaccard      # near-duplicate detection, not just exact
    threshold: 0.85              # >= this Jaccard similarity = duplicate
    shingle_size: 5              # word n-gram size for shingling
  quality_filters:
    require_thinking: true       # a target with no CoT is low-signal
    reject_refusals: true
    reject_placeholders: true    # "TODO", "...", "your code here"
    max_per_skill_ratio: 0.40    # no single skill may dominate the batch

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# EVALUATION
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
eval:
  holdout_ratio: 0.20            # fraction of generated examples kept unseen
  n_eval_prompts: 20             # per grading run
  temperature: 0.3               # low, for score stability across runs
  think: true                    # grade the reasoning channel too
  max_tokens: 2048
  # Compare each run against the previous to catch regression / forgetting.
  regression_guard:
    enabled: true
    max_drop: 0.05               # >5% score drop on a previously-passing skill
                                 # = likely catastrophic forgetting; halt.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# TRAINING - QLoRA hyperparameters calibrated to 8 GB VRAM.
# These numbers are deliberately conservative; peak usage ~6 GB leaves
# headroom for the Windows desktop compositor sharing the card.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
training:
  max_seq_length: 2048           # 4096 will OOM at batch 2 on 8 GB
  load_in_4bit: true             # QLoRA - the base stays quantized
  dtype: bfloat16                # Ada (RTX 4060 Ti) supports bf16 natively

  lora:
    r: 16                        # 16 is the sweet spot for small incremental runs
    alpha: 32                    # 2x r
    dropout: 0.0                 # Unsloth's fast path requires 0
    bias: none
    target_modules:
      - q_proj
      - k_proj
      - v_proj
      - o_proj
      - gate_proj
      - up_proj
      - down_proj
    use_rslora: true             # rank-stabilized: steadier at low LR
    use_gradient_checkpointing: unsloth

  batch:
    per_device_train_batch_size: 2
    gradient_accumulation_steps: 8   # effective batch = 16
    dataloader_num_workers: 2

  optim:
    optimizer: adamw_8bit        # paged 8-bit optimizer; saves ~1 GB
    learning_rate: 2.0e-4        # start of the cosine ramp-down
    min_learning_rate: 5.0e-5    # floor - the cosine decays to this
    lr_scheduler_type: cosine
    warmup_ratio: 0.03
    weight_decay: 0.01
    max_grad_norm: 0.3           # low clip: guards against loss spikes
    num_train_epochs: 2          # a "micro-epoch" pass over the new batch
    seed: 3407

  # --- anti-catastrophic-forgetting -----------------------------------------
  # The core defence is structural: LoRA only (base weights frozen), a low LR
  # floor, and replaying old examples alongside new ones.
  forgetting_guard:
    replay_ratio: 0.30           # 30% of each batch is resampled older data
    train_on_responses_only: true  # mask the prompt; don't train on user turns
    resume_from_last_adapter: true # stack lessons rather than restarting
    eval_before_and_after: true    # grade_student.py runs on both sides

  checkpointing:
    save_steps: 25
    save_total_limit: 4
    output_dir: ./adapters

  export:
    merge_to_16bit: true
    gguf_quant: q4_k_m           # matches the served daily-driver quant
    gguf_dir: ./gguf
    ollama_tag: qwen3.5-student  # :v1, :v2, ... per lesson

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
generate_lessons.py - Turn Teacher output into a clean training set.

Two ways in:

  1. HARVEST - scrape real Claude Code sessions off disk. These are the
     highest-signal examples you have, because they are the Teacher solving
     *your* actual problems, with real tool calls.
         python generate_lessons.py harvest --limit 200

  2. INGEST - load a batch of curated examples Claude authored directly
     (Phase 4 writes lessons_batch_01.json this way).
         python generate_lessons.py ingest --file lessons/lesson_01.json

Both paths run the same pipeline:
     normalize -> quality filter -> near-duplicate dedupe -> train/eval split

Output:
     dataset/train.jsonl   dataset/eval.jsonl   dataset/rejected.jsonl

Every record keeps the Teacher's reasoning trace and exact tool-call JSON -
that formatting fidelity is most of what the Student needs to learn.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import os
import random
import re
import sys
from collections import Counter
from dataclasses import dataclass, field, asdict
from pathlib import Path

try:
    import yaml
except ImportError:
    sys.exit("Missing dependency: pip install pyyaml")

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
CURRICULUM = HERE / "curriculum.yaml"
DATASET = HERE / "dataset"
RAW = HERE / "raw_sessions"

# Where Claude Code keeps its session transcripts on this machine.
CLAUDE_PROJECTS = Path(os.path.expanduser("~")) / ".claude" / "projects"

PLACEHOLDER_PAT = re.compile(
    r"\b(TODO|FIXME|your code here|insert .{0,20} here|\.\.\.\s*$|<placeholder>)",
    re.IGNORECASE | re.MULTILINE,
)
REFUSAL_PAT = re.compile(
    r"\b(I can'?t help with|I'm (unable|not able) to|I won'?t|I cannot assist|"
    r"As an AI language model)\b",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data model
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
@dataclass
class Example:
    """One Teacher->Student training example."""

    instruction: str
    output: str
    thinking: str = ""
    system: str = ""
    skill: str = "general"
    difficulty: str = "medium"
    tool_calls: list = field(default_factory=list)
    source: str = "synthetic"
    tags: list = field(default_factory=list)

    def fingerprint(self) -> str:
        """Stable id for exact-duplicate detection."""
        return hashlib.sha256(
            (self.instruction.strip() + "||" + self.output.strip()).encode("utf-8")
        ).hexdigest()[:16]

    def to_record(self, thinking_tag: str = "think") -> dict:
        """Chat-format record. The CoT is embedded so SFT learns to produce it."""
        target = self.output.strip()
        if self.thinking.strip():
            target = (
                f"<{thinking_tag}>\n{self.thinking.strip()}\n</{thinking_tag}>\n\n"
                + target
            )
        messages = []
        if self.system.strip():
            messages.append({"role": "system", "content": self.system.strip()})
        messages.append({"role": "user", "content": self.instruction.strip()})
        messages.append({"role": "assistant", "content": target})
        return {
            "messages": messages,
            "meta": {
                "skill": self.skill,
                "difficulty": self.difficulty,
                "source": self.source,
                "has_thinking": bool(self.thinking.strip()),
                "has_tool_calls": bool(self.tool_calls),
                "fingerprint": self.fingerprint(),
                "tags": self.tags,
            },
        }


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Near-duplicate detection (MinHash-free Jaccard over word shingles)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def shingles(text: str, k: int) -> set[str]:
    words = re.findall(r"\w+", text.lower())
    if len(words) < k:
        return {" ".join(words)} if words else set()
    return {" ".join(words[i : i + k]) for i in range(len(words) - k + 1)}


def jaccard(a: set[str], b: set[str]) -> float:
    if not a or not b:
        return 0.0
    inter = len(a & b)
    return inter / (len(a) + len(b) - inter)


def dedupe(examples: list[Example], threshold: float, k: int) -> tuple[list, list]:
    """Drop exact and near-duplicates. Keeps the first occurrence.

    O(n^2) over shingle sets. Fine for the batch sizes here (hundreds);
    swap in datasketch MinHashLSH if the set ever reaches tens of thousands.
    """
    kept: list[Example] = []
    kept_shingles: list[set[str]] = []
    seen_fp: set[str] = set()
    rejected: list[tuple[Example, str]] = []

    for ex in examples:
        fp = ex.fingerprint()
        if fp in seen_fp:
            rejected.append((ex, "exact_duplicate"))
            continue
        sh = shingles(ex.instruction + " " + ex.output, k)
        dup_of = None
        for i, prev in enumerate(kept_shingles):
            if jaccard(sh, prev) >= threshold:
                dup_of = i
                break
        if dup_of is not None:
            rejected.append((ex, f"near_duplicate_of_{dup_of}"))
            continue
        seen_fp.add(fp)
        kept.append(ex)
        kept_shingles.append(sh)

    return kept, rejected


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Quality filtering
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def quality_check(ex: Example, cfg: dict) -> str | None:
    """Return a rejection reason, or None if the example passes."""
    g = cfg["generation"]
    q = g["quality_filters"]
    body = ex.output.strip()

    if len(body) < g["min_chars"]:
        return f"too_short({len(body)}<{g['min_chars']})"
    if len(body) > g["max_chars"]:
        return f"too_long({len(body)}>{g['max_chars']})"
    if not ex.instruction.strip():
        return "empty_instruction"
    if q.get("require_thinking") and not ex.thinking.strip():
        return "missing_thinking"
    if q.get("reject_refusals") and REFUSAL_PAT.search(body):
        return "refusal"
    if q.get("reject_placeholders") and PLACEHOLDER_PAT.search(body):
        return "placeholder"
    # Any fenced JSON that claims to be a tool call must actually parse.
    for block in re.findall(r"```json\s*(.*?)```", body, re.DOTALL):
        try:
            json.loads(block)
        except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
            return f"invalid_json_block({e.msg})"
    return None


def enforce_skill_balance(examples: list[Example], max_ratio: float) -> tuple[list, list]:
    """Stop one skill from swamping the batch, which skews the LoRA."""
    if not examples:
        return [], []
    cap = max(1, int(len(examples) * max_ratio))
    counts: Counter = Counter()
    kept, rejected = [], []
    for ex in examples:
        if counts[ex.skill] >= cap:
            rejected.append((ex, f"skill_over_cap({ex.skill}>{cap})"))
            continue
        counts[ex.skill] += 1
        kept.append(ex)
    return kept, rejected


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Source 1: harvest real Claude Code transcripts
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def harvest_sessions(limit: int, min_output_chars: int = 400) -> list[Example]:
    """Mine ~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl for Teacher turns worth learning from.

    Claude Code writes one JSONL per session: each line is an event with a
    `message` holding role + content blocks. We pair each user turn with the
    assistant turn that answered it, preserving thinking blocks and tool_use
    blocks verbatim.
    """
    if not CLAUDE_PROJECTS.exists():
        print(f"  no transcripts at {CLAUDE_PROJECTS}", file=sys.stderr)
        return []

    files = sorted(
        CLAUDE_PROJECTS.rglob("*.jsonl"), key=lambda p: p.stat().st_mtime, reverse=True
    )
    print(f"  scanning {len(files)} transcript file(s)")
    out: list[Example] = []

    for fp in files:
        if len(out) >= limit:
            break
        try:
            lines = fp.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").splitlines()
        except OSError:
            continue

        pending_user: str | None = None
        for line in lines:
            if len(out) >= limit:
                break
            line = line.strip()
            if not line:
                continue
            try:
                ev = json.loads(line)
            except json.JSONDecodeError:
                continue

            msg = ev.get("message")
            if not isinstance(msg, dict):
                continue
            role = msg.get("role")
            content = msg.get("content")

            text_parts, think_parts, tool_calls = [], [], []
            if isinstance(content, str):
                text_parts.append(content)
            elif isinstance(content, list):
                for blk in content:
                    if not isinstance(blk, dict):
                        continue
                    btype = blk.get("type")
                    if btype == "text":
                        text_parts.append(blk.get("text", ""))
                    elif btype == "thinking":
                        think_parts.append(blk.get("thinking", ""))
                    elif btype == "tool_use":
                        tool_calls.append(
                            {"name": blk.get("name"), "input": blk.get("input")}
                        )
                    # tool_result blocks are deliberately skipped: they are
                    # environment output, not Teacher behaviour to imitate.

            text = "\n".join(t for t in text_parts if t).strip()

            if role == "user":
                # Skip tool-result-only turns and system reminders.
                if text and "<system-reminder>" not in text:
                    pending_user = text
                continue

            if role == "assistant" and pending_user:
                thinking = "\n".join(think_parts).strip()
                # Render tool calls into the target so formatting is learned.
                body = text
                if tool_calls:
                    rendered = "\n\n".join(
                        f"```json\n{json.dumps(tc, indent=2)}\n```" for tc in tool_calls
                    )
                    body = (body + "\n\n" + rendered).strip()
                if len(body) >= min_output_chars:
                    out.append(
                        Example(
                            instruction=pending_user,
                            output=body,
                            thinking=thinking,
                            skill="harvested_session",
                            source=f"session:{fp.stem[:8]}",
                            tool_calls=tool_calls,
                            tags=["real_session"],
                        )
                    )
                pending_user = None

    print(f"  harvested {len(out)} candidate pair(s)")
    return out


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Source 2: ingest a curated JSON batch
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def load_batch(path: Path) -> list[Example]:
    data = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    items = data["examples"] if isinstance(data, dict) else data
    out = []
    for d in items:
        out.append(
            Example(
                instruction=d.get("instruction") or d.get("prompt", ""),
                output=d.get("output") or d.get("response", ""),
                thinking=d.get("thinking", ""),
                system=d.get("system", ""),
                skill=d.get("skill", "general"),
                difficulty=d.get("difficulty", "medium"),
                tool_calls=d.get("tool_calls", []),
                source=d.get("source", f"curated:{path.stem}"),
                tags=d.get("tags", []),
            )
        )
    print(f"  loaded {len(out)} curated example(s) from {path.name}")
    return out


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Pipeline
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def write_jsonl(path: Path, records: list[dict], append: bool) -> int:
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    mode = "a" if (append and path.exists()) else "w"
    with path.open(mode, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        for r in records:
            f.write(json.dumps(r, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
    with path.open(encoding="utf-8") as f:
        return sum(1 for _ in f)


def existing_fingerprints(path: Path) -> set[str]:
    """So repeated runs never re-add examples already in the training set."""
    fps: set[str] = set()
    if not path.exists():
        return fps
    with path.open(encoding="utf-8") as f:
        for line in f:
            try:
                fps.add(json.loads(line)["meta"]["fingerprint"])
            except Exception:
                continue
    return fps


def run(examples: list[Example], cfg: dict, append: bool, dry_run: bool) -> dict:
    gen = cfg["generation"]
    stats: Counter = Counter()
    rejected_all: list[tuple[Example, str]] = []

    print(f"\n[1/4] quality filtering {len(examples)} example(s)")
    passed = []
    for ex in examples:
        reason = quality_check(ex, cfg)
        if reason:
            rejected_all.append((ex, reason))
            stats[f"reject:{reason.split('(')[0]}"] += 1
        else:
            passed.append(ex)
    print(f"      {len(passed)} passed, {len(examples) - len(passed)} rejected")

    print(f"[2/4] deduplicating (jaccard >= {gen['dedupe']['threshold']})")
    deduped, dup_rejects = dedupe(
        passed, gen["dedupe"]["threshold"], gen["dedupe"]["shingle_size"]
    )
    rejected_all += dup_rejects
    print(f"      {len(deduped)} unique, {len(dup_rejects)} duplicate(s) dropped")

    # Drop anything already present in train.jsonl from earlier lessons.
    known = existing_fingerprints(DATASET / "train.jsonl") | existing_fingerprints(
        DATASET / "eval.jsonl"
    )
    if known:
        before = len(deduped)
        fresh, stale = [], []
        for ex in deduped:
            (fresh if ex.fingerprint() not in known else stale).append(ex)
        rejected_all += [(e, "already_in_dataset") for e in stale]
        deduped = fresh
        print(f"      {before - len(deduped)} already in dataset, {len(deduped)} new")

    print(f"[3/4] enforcing skill balance (max {gen['quality_filters']['max_per_skill_ratio']:.0%}/skill)")
    balanced, bal_rejects = enforce_skill_balance(
        deduped, gen["quality_filters"]["max_per_skill_ratio"]
    )
    rejected_all += bal_rejects
    print(f"      {len(balanced)} kept, {len(bal_rejects)} over cap")

    print(f"[4/4] splitting (holdout {cfg['eval']['holdout_ratio']:.0%})")
    random.seed(cfg["training"]["optim"]["seed"])
    random.shuffle(balanced)
    n_eval = int(len(balanced) * cfg["eval"]["holdout_ratio"])
    eval_set, train_set = balanced[:n_eval], balanced[n_eval:]

    tag = gen["thinking_tag"]
    if dry_run:
        print("\n(dry run - nothing written)")
    else:
        n_tr = write_jsonl(DATASET / "train.jsonl",
                           [e.to_record(tag) for e in train_set], append)
        n_ev = write_jsonl(DATASET / "eval.jsonl",
                           [e.to_record(tag) for e in eval_set], append)
        write_jsonl(
            DATASET / "rejected.jsonl",
            [{"reason": r, **asdict(e)} for e, r in rejected_all],
            append,
        )
        print(f"\n  dataset/train.jsonl  +{len(train_set):4d}  (total {n_tr})")
        print(f"  dataset/eval.jsonl   +{len(eval_set):4d}  (total {n_ev})")
        print(f"  dataset/rejected.jsonl +{len(rejected_all):2d}  (audit trail)")

    by_skill = Counter(e.skill for e in balanced)
    with_cot = sum(1 for e in balanced if e.thinking.strip())
    print(f"\n  with reasoning traces: {with_cot}/{len(balanced)}")
    print(f"  by skill: {dict(by_skill)}")
    if rejected_all:
        print(f"  top rejection reasons: {dict(Counter(r.split('(')[0] for _, r in rejected_all).most_common(5))}")

    return {"train": len(train_set), "eval": len(eval_set), "rejected": len(rejected_all)}


def main() -> int:
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__,
                                formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    sub = p.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)

    h = sub.add_parser("harvest", help="Mine real Claude Code sessions.")
    h.add_argument("--limit", type=int, default=200)
    h.add_argument("--min-chars", type=int, default=400)

    i = sub.add_parser("ingest", help="Load a curated JSON batch.")
    i.add_argument("--file", required=True, type=Path)

    s = sub.add_parser("stats", help="Summarize the current dataset.")

    for sp in (h, i):
        sp.add_argument("--no-append", action="store_true",
                        help="Overwrite the dataset instead of appending.")
        sp.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true")

    args = p.parse_args()
    cfg = yaml.safe_load(CURRICULUM.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))

    if args.cmd == "stats":
        for name in ("train", "eval", "rejected"):
            fp = DATASET / f"{name}.jsonl"
            if not fp.exists():
                print(f"{name:9s}: (none)")
                continue
            rows = [json.loads(l) for l in fp.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines() if l.strip()]
            print(f"{name:9s}: {len(rows)} rows")
            if name != "rejected" and rows:
                sk = Counter(r.get("meta", {}).get("skill", "?") for r in rows)
                cot = sum(1 for r in rows if r.get("meta", {}).get("has_thinking"))
                print(f"           skills={dict(sk)}  with_cot={cot}")
        return 0

    if args.cmd == "harvest":
        print("Harvesting real Claude Code sessions...")
        examples = harvest_sessions(args.limit, args.min_chars)
    else:
        path = args.file if args.file.is_absolute() else HERE / args.file
        if not path.exists():
            sys.exit(f"no such file: {path}")
        examples = load_batch(path)

    if not examples:
        print("No examples found. Nothing to do.")
        return 1

    run(examples, cfg, append=not args.no_append, dry_run=args.dry_run)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
grade_student.py - Benchmark the Student against the Teacher's reference answers.

The Teacher (Claude) writes reference outputs into the eval set. This script
replays those prompts against the local model and scores each answer on four
axes from curriculum.yaml's rubric, then logs which skills are weak so the next
lesson batch can target them.

Scoring is deterministic and offline by default - no Teacher API call needed:
  accuracy     keyword/содержание overlap with the reference, plus code-block
               and numeric-fact agreement
  reasoning    did it produce a usable chain-of-thought, and does that CoT
               mention the key concepts the reference reasoning does
  formatting   structural match: code fences, JSON validity, required markers
  conciseness  length ratio against the reference, penalising padding

With --judge, Claude grades the same answers qualitatively instead (pass the
generated report back to Claude and have it fill in the `judge` block).

Usage:
    python grade_student.py                          # grade qwen3.5:4b on eval.jsonl
    python grade_student.py --model qwen3.5:9b       # baseline a different model
    python grade_student.py --baseline               # tag this run as the pre-training baseline
    python grade_student.py --compare reports/baseline.json
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import re
import statistics
import sys
import time
from collections import defaultdict
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

try:
    import yaml
except ImportError:
    sys.exit("Missing dependency: pip install pyyaml")

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(HERE.parent))  # so we can import ask_local_llm

try:
    from ask_local_llm import ask, health
except ImportError:
    sys.exit("Cannot import ask_local_llm.py - expected at E:\\LocalLLM\\ask_local_llm.py")

CURRICULUM = HERE / "curriculum.yaml"
DATASET = HERE / "dataset"
REPORTS = HERE / "reports"

STOPWORDS = {
    "the", "a", "an", "and", "or", "but", "if", "then", "to", "of", "in", "on",
    "for", "with", "is", "are", "was", "were", "be", "been", "it", "this",
    "that", "these", "those", "as", "at", "by", "from", "you", "your", "we",
    "can", "will", "would", "should", "not", "no", "do", "does", "so", "into",
}

THINK_RE = re.compile(r"<think>(.*?)</think>", re.DOTALL | re.IGNORECASE)
CODE_RE = re.compile(r"```(\w+)?\s*(.*?)```", re.DOTALL)
NUM_RE = re.compile(r"-?\d+(?:\.\d+)?")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Scoring primitives
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def content_words(text: str) -> set[str]:
    return {w for w in re.findall(r"[a-z_][a-z0-9_]{2,}", text.lower()) if w not in STOPWORDS}


def split_reference(target: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
    """Separate the Teacher's <think> trace from the final answer."""
    m = THINK_RE.search(target)
    if not m:
        return "", target.strip()
    return m.group(1).strip(), THINK_RE.sub("", target).strip()


def score_accuracy(student: str, ref: str) -> tuple[float, str]:
    """Recall of the reference's content words, plus agreement on numbers."""
    ref_w, stu_w = content_words(ref), content_words(student)
    if not ref_w:
        return 1.0, "empty reference"
    recall = len(ref_w & stu_w) / len(ref_w)

    # Numeric facts are high-signal: a wrong number is a wrong answer.
    ref_nums = set(NUM_RE.findall(ref))
    num_score = 1.0
    if ref_nums:
        stu_nums = set(NUM_RE.findall(student))
        num_score = len(ref_nums & stu_nums) / len(ref_nums)

    score = 0.7 * recall + 0.3 * num_score
    return min(1.0, score), f"recall={recall:.2f} nums={num_score:.2f}"


def score_reasoning(student_think: str, ref_think: str, student_answer: str) -> tuple[float, str]:
    """Reward a real CoT that covers the reference reasoning's concepts."""
    if not ref_think:
        # Nothing to compare against; credit any visible reasoning.
        return (0.8 if student_think else 0.5), "no reference CoT"
    if not student_think:
        return 0.0, "student produced no CoT"

    ref_w, stu_w = content_words(ref_think), content_words(student_think)
    coverage = len(ref_w & stu_w) / len(ref_w) if ref_w else 0.0

    # A CoT that is pure restatement of the answer is not reasoning.
    answer_w = content_words(student_answer)
    novelty = len(stu_w - answer_w) / len(stu_w) if stu_w else 0.0

    # Multi-step structure (numbered/bulleted steps) is a good proxy for depth.
    steps = len(re.findall(r"(?m)^\s*(?:\d+[.)]|[-*])\s+", student_think))
    structure = min(1.0, steps / 4.0)

    score = 0.55 * coverage + 0.25 * novelty + 0.20 * structure
    return min(1.0, score), f"cov={coverage:.2f} nov={novelty:.2f} steps={steps}"


def score_formatting(student: str, ref: str) -> tuple[float, str]:
    """Structural fidelity: code fences, language tags, JSON validity."""
    checks, notes = [], []

    ref_blocks, stu_blocks = CODE_RE.findall(ref), CODE_RE.findall(student)
    if ref_blocks:
        if not stu_blocks:
            checks.append(0.0)
            notes.append("missing code block")
        else:
            checks.append(1.0)
            ref_langs = {l for l, _ in ref_blocks if l}
            stu_langs = {l for l, _ in stu_blocks if l}
            if ref_langs:
                checks.append(1.0 if ref_langs & stu_langs else 0.3)
                if not ref_langs & stu_langs:
                    notes.append(f"lang tag {ref_langs}!={stu_langs}")
    else:
        # Reference has no code: punish gratuitous code dumps.
        checks.append(0.6 if stu_blocks else 1.0)
        if stu_blocks:
            notes.append("unrequested code block")

    # Every JSON block the Student emits must actually parse - this is the
    # single most important property for tool calling.
    json_blocks = [b for l, b in stu_blocks if (l or "").lower() == "json"]
    for b in json_blocks:
        try:
            json.loads(b)
            checks.append(1.0)
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            checks.append(0.0)
            notes.append("invalid JSON")

    # Mirror the reference's use of markdown headings / bullets.
    for pat, label in ((r"(?m)^#{1,6}\s", "headings"), (r"(?m)^\s*[-*]\s", "bullets")):
        if re.search(pat, ref):
            checks.append(1.0 if re.search(pat, student) else 0.5)
            if not re.search(pat, student):
                notes.append(f"missing {label}")

    if not checks:
        return 1.0, "no structure required"
    return sum(checks) / len(checks), ", ".join(notes) or "ok"


def score_conciseness(student: str, ref: str) -> tuple[float, str]:
    """Penalise both padding and truncation, relative to the reference."""
    if not ref.strip():
        return 1.0, "empty reference"
    ratio = len(student) / len(ref)
    if ratio < 0.3:
        return max(0.0, ratio / 0.3), f"too short ({ratio:.2f}x)"
    if ratio <= 1.6:
        return 1.0, f"{ratio:.2f}x"
    # Degrade gradually past 1.6x rather than falling off a cliff.
    return max(0.0, 1.0 - (ratio - 1.6) / 2.4), f"padded ({ratio:.2f}x)"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Harness
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def load_eval(path: Path, limit: int | None) -> list[dict]:
    if not path.exists():
        sys.exit(f"No eval set at {path}. Run generate_lessons.py first.")
    rows = []
    for line in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
        if not line.strip():
            continue
        r = json.loads(line)
        msgs = r.get("messages", [])
        prompt = next((m["content"] for m in msgs if m["role"] == "user"), None)
        target = next((m["content"] for m in msgs if m["role"] == "assistant"), None)
        if not prompt or not target:
            continue
        system = next((m["content"] for m in msgs if m["role"] == "system"), "")
        rows.append({
            "prompt": prompt,
            "target": target,
            "system": system,
            "skill": r.get("meta", {}).get("skill", "general"),
            "difficulty": r.get("meta", {}).get("difficulty", "medium"),
        })
    return rows[:limit] if limit else rows


def grade_one(row: dict, cfg: dict, model: str) -> dict:
    ev = cfg["eval"]
    w = cfg["rubric"]["weights"]
    ref_think, ref_answer = split_reference(row["target"])

    r = ask(
        row["prompt"],
        model=model,
        system=row["system"] or None,
        think=ev["think"],
        max_tokens=ev["max_tokens"],
        temperature=ev["temperature"],
    )
    if r.error:
        return {"skill": row["skill"], "error": r.error, "total": 0.0,
                "prompt": row["prompt"][:160]}

    stu_answer = r.content
    stu_think = r.thinking or (THINK_RE.search(stu_answer).group(1)
                               if THINK_RE.search(stu_answer) else "")
    stu_answer_clean = THINK_RE.sub("", stu_answer).strip()

    acc, acc_n = score_accuracy(stu_answer_clean, ref_answer)
    rea, rea_n = score_reasoning(stu_think, ref_think, stu_answer_clean)
    fmt, fmt_n = score_formatting(stu_answer_clean, ref_answer)
    con, con_n = score_conciseness(stu_answer_clean, ref_answer)

    total = acc * w["accuracy"] + rea * w["reasoning"] + fmt * w["formatting"] + con * w["conciseness"]

    return {
        "skill": row["skill"],
        "difficulty": row["difficulty"],
        "prompt": row["prompt"][:160],
        "scores": {"accuracy": round(acc, 3), "reasoning": round(rea, 3),
                   "formatting": round(fmt, 3), "conciseness": round(con, 3)},
        "notes": {"accuracy": acc_n, "reasoning": rea_n,
                  "formatting": fmt_n, "conciseness": con_n},
        "total": round(total, 3),
        "passed": total >= cfg["rubric"]["pass_threshold"],
        "truncated": r.truncated,
        "tokens_per_sec": r.tokens_per_sec,
        "student_answer": stu_answer_clean[:2000],
        "student_thinking": stu_think[:1500],
    }


def main() -> int:
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__,
                                formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    p.add_argument("--model", default=None, help="Ollama tag to grade (default: curriculum student_model).")
    p.add_argument("--eval-file", type=Path, default=None)
    p.add_argument("--limit", type=int, default=None)
    p.add_argument("--baseline", action="store_true",
                   help="Also write reports/baseline.json for later comparison.")
    p.add_argument("--compare", type=Path, default=None,
                   help="Diff against a previous report; flags regressions.")
    p.add_argument("--out", type=Path, default=None)
    args = p.parse_args()

    cfg = yaml.safe_load(CURRICULUM.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    model = args.model or cfg["meta"]["student_model"]

    h = health()
    if not h["up"]:
        sys.exit(f"Ollama is not reachable at {h['host']}: {h.get('error')}\n"
                 f"Start it: powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File E:\\LocalLLM\\start-ollama.ps1")
    if model not in h["models"]:
        sys.exit(f"Model '{model}' not installed. Have: {h['models']}")

    eval_path = args.eval_file or (DATASET / "eval.jsonl")
    rows = load_eval(eval_path, args.limit or cfg["eval"]["n_eval_prompts"])
    if not rows:
        sys.exit(f"{eval_path} has no usable rows.")

    print(f"Grading {model} on {len(rows)} prompt(s) from {eval_path.name}\n")
    started = time.time()
    results = []
    for i, row in enumerate(rows, 1):
        print(f"  [{i:>3}/{len(rows)}] {row['skill']:<24} ", end="", flush=True)
        res = grade_one(row, cfg, model)
        results.append(res)
        if "error" in res:
            print(f"ERROR {res['error'][:60]}")
        else:
            flag = "PASS" if res["passed"] else "FAIL"
            print(f"{res['total']:.3f} {flag}  ({res['tokens_per_sec']} tok/s)")

    scored = [r for r in results if "error" not in r]
    if not scored:
        sys.exit("Every prompt errored - nothing to report.")

    overall = statistics.mean(r["total"] for r in scored)
    by_crit = {
        c: round(statistics.mean(r["scores"][c] for r in scored), 3)
        for c in ("accuracy", "reasoning", "formatting", "conciseness")
    }
    by_skill: dict[str, list[float]] = defaultdict(list)
    for r in scored:
        by_skill[r["skill"]].append(r["total"])
    skill_avg = {k: round(statistics.mean(v), 3) for k, v in sorted(by_skill.items())}

    thresh = cfg["rubric"]["pass_threshold"]
    weak = sorted([k for k, v in skill_avg.items() if v < thresh], key=lambda k: skill_avg[k])

    report = {
        "timestamp": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
        "model": model,
        "eval_file": str(eval_path),
        "n_prompts": len(rows),
        "n_errors": len(results) - len(scored),
        "overall_score": round(overall, 3),
        "pass_rate": round(sum(1 for r in scored if r["passed"]) / len(scored), 3),
        "by_criterion": by_crit,
        "by_skill": skill_avg,
        "weak_skills": weak,
        "mean_tokens_per_sec": round(statistics.mean(r["tokens_per_sec"] for r in scored), 1),
        "wall_seconds": round(time.time() - started, 1),
        "results": results,
    }

    print("\n" + "=" * 62)
    print(f"  {model}  overall {overall:.3f}   pass rate {report['pass_rate']:.0%}")
    print("=" * 62)
    for c, v in by_crit.items():
        bar = "#" * int(v * 30)
        print(f"  {c:<13} {v:.3f}  {bar}")
    print(f"\n  by skill:")
    for k, v in skill_avg.items():
        print(f"    {'WEAK' if v < thresh else '  ok'}  {k:<28} {v:.3f}")
    if weak:
        print(f"\n  -> target next lesson batch at: {', '.join(weak)}")
    print(f"\n  {report['mean_tokens_per_sec']} tok/s mean, {report['wall_seconds']}s total")

    REPORTS.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    stamp = datetime.now().strftime("%Y%m%d_%H%M%S")
    out = args.out or REPORTS / f"grade_{model.replace(':', '-')}_{stamp}.json"
    out.write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"\n  report: {out}")
    if args.baseline:
        bl = REPORTS / "baseline.json"
        bl.write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")
        print(f"  baseline: {bl}")

    # --- regression guard: catch catastrophic forgetting --------------------
    if args.compare:
        if not args.compare.exists():
            print(f"\n  (no comparison file at {args.compare})")
            return 0
        prev = json.loads(args.compare.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        guard = cfg["eval"]["regression_guard"]
        delta = overall - prev["overall_score"]
        print(f"\n  vs {args.compare.name}: {prev['overall_score']:.3f} -> {overall:.3f} "
              f"({delta:+.3f})")
        regressed = []
        for skill, prev_v in prev.get("by_skill", {}).items():
            now_v = skill_avg.get(skill)
            if now_v is None:
                continue
            drop = prev_v - now_v
            if prev_v >= thresh and drop > guard["max_drop"]:
                regressed.append((skill, prev_v, now_v, drop))
        if regressed:
            print(f"\n  !! REGRESSION on {len(regressed)} previously-passing skill(s):")
            for s, pv, nv, d in regressed:
                print(f"       {s:<28} {pv:.3f} -> {nv:.3f}  (-{d:.3f})")
            print("     Likely catastrophic forgetting. Lower the learning rate,")
            print("     raise forgetting_guard.replay_ratio, or roll back the adapter.")
            if guard.get("enabled"):
                return 2
        else:
            print("  no regression on previously-passing skills.")

    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
