input.command:
cd "$APPDATA/obs-studio" && (python -c "import json;json.load(open('basic/scenes/Main.json'));print('JSON valid')" 2>/dev/null || node -e "JSON.parse(require('fs').readFileSync('basic/scenes/Main.json'));console.log('JSON valid')" 2>/dev/null || echo "no validator available")
printf '
[Basic]
Profile=Stream and Record
ProfileDir=Stream and Record
SceneCollection=Main
SceneCollectionFile=Main
' >> "$APPDATA/obs-studio/global.ini"
tail -8 "$APPDATA/obs-studio/global.ini"
input.description: Validate scene JSON and set active profile/scene collection

input.command: cd "/c/Program Files/obs-studio/bin/64bit" && (./obs64.exe --disable-updater >/dev/null 2>&1 &) ; sleep 25; LOG=$(ls -t "$APPDATA/obs-studio/logs"/*.txt | head -1); echo "LOG: $LOG"; grep -iE "error|fail|warn|nvenc|monitor_capture|game_capture|Scene Collection|Profile|Encoder|Output resol|fps|Audio Device|Filter" "$LOG" | head -45
input.description: Launch OBS and inspect startup log

input.command: LOG=$(ls -t "$APPDATA/obs-studio/logs"/*.txt | head -1); echo "=== video/profile ==="; grep -iE "base resolution|output resolution|fps:|Current Profile|Current Scene Collection|Loaded scenes|- scene|Settings:" "$LOG" | head -25; echo "=== DISPLAY MODES (top) ==="; powershell -NoProfile -c "Get-CimInstance -ClassName CIM_VideoControllerResolution | Select-Object -ExpandProperty Caption -Unique | Sort-Object -Unique | Select-Object -Last 8; '--- monitor ---'; Get-CimInstance -Namespace root\wmi -ClassName WmiMonitorListedSupportedSourceModes -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | ForEach-Object { \$_.MonitorSourceModes | Sort-Object HorizontalActivePixels -Descending | Select-Object -First 3 | ForEach-Object { \"\$(\$_.HorizontalActivePixels)x\$(\$_.VerticalActivePixels)\" } }" 2>/dev/null
input.description: Check OBS loaded config and max display resolution

input.command: taskkill //F //IM obs64.exe 2>/dev/null | head -2; sleep 3; echo "=== scenes dir ==="; ls "$APPDATA/obs-studio/basic/scenes/"; echo "=== profiles dir ==="; ls "$APPDATA/obs-studio/basic/profiles/"; echo "=== user.ini ==="; cat "$APPDATA/obs-studio/user.ini"
input.description: Stop OBS and inspect user.ini and config dirs

input.command:
cd "$APPDATA/obs-studio" && python - <<'PY'
import io,re
p='user.ini'
s=io.open(p,encoding='utf-8-sig').read()
s=s.replace('FirstRun=true','FirstRun=false')
s=s.replace('RecordWhenStreaming=false','RecordWhenStreaming=true')
s=s.replace('KeepRecordingWhenStreamStops=false','KeepRecordingWhenStreamStops=true')
s=re.sub(r'Profile=Untitled','Profile=Stream and Record',s)
s=re.sub(r'ProfileDir=Untitled','ProfileDir=Stream and Record',s)
s=re.sub(r'SceneCollection=Untitled','SceneCollection=Main',s)
s=re.sub(r'SceneCollectionFile=Untitled\.json','SceneCollectionFile=Main.json',s)
io.open(p,'w',encoding='utf-8-sig',newline='').write(s)
# strip the [Basic] block I wrongly appended to global.ini
g='global.ini'
t=io.open(g,encoding='utf-8-sig').read()
t=t.split('\n[Basic]')[0].rstrip()+'\n'
io.open(g,'w',encoding='utf-8-sig',newline='').write(t)
print('user.ini [Basic] + flags updated; global.ini cleaned')
PY
grep -A6 "^\[Basic\]" user.ini; grep -E "FirstRun|RecordWhenStreaming|KeepRecording" user.ini
input.description: Point user.ini at new profile, enable record-while-streaming

questions.question: Your only display maxes out at 1920x1080, so a 4K recording would be an upscale of a 1080p source. How do you want the recording configured?

options.label: 1080p60 near-lossless (Recommended)

I can do the OBS side of this, but part of it is account-gated — let me confirm exactly what the theme contains before I build the scenes.

Fetched — it's free, includes 5 scenes (Starting Soon, In Game, Talk, Be Right Back, Stream Ended) plus Alert Box, Labels, and a 16:9 Cambox.

One hard limit up front: **I can't install the theme itself.** Installing it creates overlays inside *your* StreamElements account and each one gets a private URL containing your account token (`streamelements.com/overlay/<id>/<token>`). That needs your Twitch/YouTube login, which I don't have and shouldn't. What I can do is build the entire OBS side so that part is pure copy-paste.

Let me verify OBS is closed, then extend the scene collection programmatically rather than hand-editing the file OBS just rewrote:

OBS is closed and I've backed up the collection. Building the scenes:

Now verifying OBS actually accepts it, since a hand-built scene file is only as good as OBS's parse of it:

Verified — all 8 scenes load, all 6 browser sources instantiate, no CEF errors. (The `libcef.dll` "not an OBS plugin" line is normal; that's the Chromium runtime, not a plugin.)

## What's built in OBS

| OBS scene | Contents |
|---|---|
| **Starting Soon** | `SE Starting Soon` |
| **In Game** | `SE In Game` → `Alerts` (hidden) → Game Capture → Window Capture |
| **Talk** | `SE Talk` → `Alerts` (hidden) → Display Capture |
| **BRB** | `SE Be Right Back` |
| **Stream Ended** | `SE Stream Ended` |
| **Alerts** | `SE Alert Box` — nested into In Game and Talk |
| Desktop / Audio Only | your originals, untouched |

Every browser source is 1920x1080 with the transparent-background CSS, pointed at `about:blank` as a placeholder. I renamed your old `Game` scene to `In Game` to match the theme and layered the overlay on top of the capture already in it.

Three deliberate choices worth knowing:
- **`reroute_audio` is on** for all six, so alert and BRB-music audio shows up as its own Audio Mixer channel — it lands in both the stream and the recording, with independent volume. This is the usual reason people's alerts are missing from their VODs.
- **Alert Box unloads nothing** (`shutdown` off) so alerts never reconnect on a scene switch. The idle screens *do* unload when hidden, to save CPU.
- **The nested `Alerts` layer is hidden by default** — see the caveat below.

## Your part (~3 minutes)

1. Open https://widgets.streamelements.com/theme/japan-ink-package and click **Use Theme Package**, logging in with Twitch/YouTube. This installs the 5 overlays into your SE account.
2. Go to **streamelements.com → My Overlays**, and for each one use **⋮ → Copy Overlay URL**.
3. In OBS, double-click the matching `SE <name>` source and paste into the URL field. The names map one-to-one. Leave width, height, and CSS alone.

**Caveat on alerts:** StreamElements usually bakes the Alert Box *into* the In Game and Talk overlays. That's why I left the nested `Alerts` layer unchecked — enabling it when the overlay already contains alerts gives you every alert twice. Only tick it in a scene if the Alert Box arrived as its own separate overlay in your SE dashboard.

**Treat the overlay URLs as secrets.** They contain your account token — anyone who has one can view or trigger your overlay, so don't show that field on stream.

- **Stream key** — Settings → Stream. Still not set from earlier, so the streaming path remains untested end to end.
- **Webcam** — the theme has a 16:9 Cambox frame but there's no camera source, matching your earlier "just audio for now". When you want it: add a Video Capture Device to In Game and Talk and size it into the frame.

`Ctrl+M` toggles mic mute. Function keys were chosen because they rarely collide with game bindings. Each game gets its **own** Game Capture source so you can point each at its specific window independently.

The `Overlay` scene is nested into all four live scenes — edit the cambox once and it propagates everywhere, instead of maintaining four copies.

## Two research-driven, game-specific points

**Valorant** — Vanguard has a documented history of breaking OBS Game Capture to a black screen (an outage this July forced OBS to recommend Window Capture as the workaround). That's why the Valorant scene ships a pre-built `Window Capture` fallback, unchecked. If you go black: tick it, or run OBS as admin. Re-adding Game Capture also has an order dependency — remove the source *before* launching the game, then re-add it with Valorant running.

**The Finals** — collapsing buildings and debris are exactly what eats bitrate, and the game is CPU-heavy from destruction physics. At your 6000 kbps cap, if destruction looks mushy, downscale *that scene's* output to 1600x900 rather than raising bitrate — 900p60 at 6000 beats blocky 1080p60. This is also why I switched the downscale filter to Lanczos.

Your RTX 4060 Ti does support NVENC AV1 (confirmed in the log), worth ~30–40% better quality at the same bitrate — but Twitch only accepts it via Enhanced Broadcasting or partner status. Stay on H.264 unless you're on YouTube.

OBS wants the raw `\\?\usb#…` path. - **Your mic is the webcam.** The only audio input on the machine is `Microphone (Brio 100)`, and Mic/Aux is on "default". For a handcam stream that's a webcam mic doing your voice — worth a real mic. - **Valorant has its perf overlay on** (Client FPS / tick rate / packet loss, top-left). That will be on stream. - **NVIDIA Broadcast is installed** with a virtual camera, and there's a Logitech OBS plugin loaded — you could route the handcam through Broadcast for noise/lighting cleanup. - Game Capture grabbed Valorant fine today despite the Vanguard history, so the fallback stays unchecked. ## Left for you 1. **Open the Brio's privacy shutter** — handcam is wired and otherwise ready. 2. **Stream key** — Settings → Stream.          "hide_transition": {"duration": 0}, "private_settings": {}}

p = os.path.join(os.environ['APPDATA'], 'obs-studio', 'basic', 'scenes', 'Main.json')
d = json.load(io.open(p, encoding='utf-8'))

# A browser source has its own internal canvas. With bounds_type 2
# (scale to inner bounds) a non-matching aspect gets letterboxed, which is
# why the frame rendered narrower than the 16:9 camera box it had to wrap.
for s in d['sources']:
    if s['id'] != 'browser_source':
        continue
    if s['name'].startswith('Reactive Frame'):
        s['settings']['width'], s['settings']['height'] = 640, 360   # 1.778

# Bars: 760x120 canvas (6.333). Make every placement match that aspect.
for s in d['sources']:
    if s['id'] != 'scene':
        continue
    for i in s['settings']['items']:
        if i['name'] == 'Reactive Bars':
            w = i['bounds']['x']
            h = round(w / (760 / 120.0))
            if h != i['bounds']['y']:
                print("%-20s bars box %dx%d -> %dx%d" % (
                    s['name'], w, i['bounds']['y'], w, h))
                i['bounds']['y'] = float(h)

d['current_scene'] = d['current_program_scene'] = 'Valorant'
json.dump(d, io.open(p, 'w', encoding='utf-8'), indent=4, ensure_ascii=False)

    items = s['settings']['items']
    cam = next((i for i in items if 'Handcam' in i['name']), None)
    frm = next((i for i in items if 'Reactive Frame' in i['name']), None)
    if cam and frm:

input.content:
"""
OBS Autopilot - per-game scene switching + reaction-triggered clipping.

Talks to OBS's built-in obs-websocket v5. No third-party OBS plugin.

  python obs-autopilot.py            run the watcher
  python obs-autopilot.py --selftest connect, prove every call works, exit
  python obs-autopilot.py --probe    print the foreground process once a second

What it does
  1. Watches the foreground window. When you alt-tab into a known game it
     switches OBS to that game's scene.
  2. Watches your mic level. A sustained shout saves the replay buffer, so
     your own reaction clips the play. Cooldown prevents spam.

What it deliberately does NOT do
  It only ever switches *away from* a scene in MANAGED. If you are on
  BRB, Starting Soon, Stream Ended or any VAL - * scene, it keeps its
  hands off, so a manual Clutch Cam or break is never stolen from you.
"""
import asyncio, base64, ctypes, hashlib, json, os, sys, time
from ctypes import wintypes

try:
    from websockets.asyncio.client import connect
except ImportError:                                    # older websockets
    from websockets import connect                     # type: ignore

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
CONFIG_PATH = os.path.join(HERE, 'autopilot.config.json')
CLIPLOG = os.path.join(HERE, 'clips.log')

DEFAULTS = {
    "host": "127.0.0.1",
    "port": 4455,
    "password": "Z43a5wrhJVqJtKXW",
    # foreground executable -> scene name
    "games": {
        "VALORANT-Win64-Shipping.exe": "Valorant",
        "Discovery.exe": "The Finals",
        "THEFINALS.exe": "The Finals"
    },
    # scenes autopilot is allowed to switch away from
    "managed": ["Valorant", "The Finals", "Single Player", "Just Chatting"],
    "fallback_scene": None,          # None = leave the scene alone on desktop
    "switch_poll_seconds": 1.0,
    # --- reaction clipping ---
    "clip_enabled": True,
    "clip_input": "Mic/Aux",
    "clip_threshold_db": -12.0,      # how loud counts as a reaction
    "clip_sustain_frames": 6,        # ~300ms, so a single pop won't fire
    "clip_cooldown_seconds": 45,
    "clip_only_in_managed": True,    # don't clip while on BRB etc.
}


def load_config():
    cfg = dict(DEFAULTS)
    if os.path.exists(CONFIG_PATH):
        try:
            cfg.update(json.load(open(CONFIG_PATH, encoding='utf-8')))
        except Exception as e:
            log("config unreadable (%s); using defaults" % e)
    else:
        json.dump(cfg, open(CONFIG_PATH, 'w', encoding='utf-8'), indent=2)
        log("wrote default config -> %s" % CONFIG_PATH)
    return cfg


def log(msg):
    print("[%s] %s" % (time.strftime('%H:%M:%S'), msg), flush=True)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# foreground window -> executable name
# --------------------------------------------------------------------- #
_u32, _k32 = ctypes.windll.user32, ctypes.windll.kernel32
_PROC_QUERY_LIMITED = 0x1000


def foreground_exe():
    hwnd = _u32.GetForegroundWindow()
    if not hwnd:
        return None
    pid = wintypes.DWORD()
    _u32.GetWindowThreadProcessId(hwnd, ctypes.byref(pid))
    if not pid.value:
        return None
    h = _k32.OpenProcess(_PROC_QUERY_LIMITED, False, pid.value)
    if not h:
        return None
    try:
        size = wintypes.DWORD(32768)
        buf = ctypes.create_unicode_buffer(size.value)
        if _k32.QueryFullProcessImageNameW(h, 0, buf, ctypes.byref(size)):
            return os.path.basename(buf.value)
    finally:
        _k32.CloseHandle(h)
    return None


# --------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# obs-websocket client
# --------------------------------------------------------------------- #
class OBS:
    def __init__(self, cfg):
        self.cfg = cfg
        self.ws = None
        self._id = 0
        self._pending = {}
        self._send_lock = asyncio.Lock()
        self.current_scene = None

    async def connect(self):
        url = "ws://%s:%d" % (self.cfg['host'], self.cfg['port'])
        self.ws = await connect(url, max_size=2 ** 22)
        hello = json.loads(await self.ws.recv())
        d = {"rpcVersion": 1, "eventSubscriptions": (1 << 0) | (1 << 2) | (1 << 16)}
        auth = hello.get('d', {}).get('authentication')
        if auth:
            pw = self.cfg['password']
            secret = base64.b64encode(
                hashlib.sha256((pw + auth['salt']).encode()).digest()).decode()
            d['authentication'] = base64.b64encode(
                hashlib.sha256((secret + auth['challenge']).encode()).digest()).decode()
        await self.ws.send(json.dumps({"op": 1, "d": d}))
        ident = json.loads(await self.ws.recv())
        if ident.get('op') != 2:
            raise RuntimeError("identify failed: %s" % ident)
        log("connected to obs-websocket (rpc %s)" % ident['d'].get('negotiatedRpcVersion'))

    async def request(self, rtype, data=None, timeout=8):
        self._id += 1
        rid = str(self._id)
        fut = asyncio.get_running_loop().create_future()
        self._pending[rid] = fut
        async with self._send_lock:
            await self.ws.send(json.dumps({"op": 6, "d": {
                "requestType": rtype, "requestId": rid,
                "requestData": data or {}}}))
        try:
            return await asyncio.wait_for(fut, timeout)
        finally:
            self._pending.pop(rid, None)

    async def pump(self, on_meter=None, on_event=None):
        """Single reader. Everything arrives here."""
        async for raw in self.ws:
            m = json.loads(raw)
            op = m.get('op')
            if op == 7:
                d = m['d']
                fut = self._pending.get(d['requestId'])
                if fut and not fut.done():
                    if d['requestStatus'].get('result'):
                        fut.set_result(d.get('responseData') or {})
                    else:
                        fut.set_exception(RuntimeError(
                            d['requestStatus'].get('comment') or
                            d['requestStatus'].get('code')))
            elif op == 5:
                et, ed = m['d']['eventType'], m['d'].get('eventData') or {}
                if et == 'InputVolumeMeters':
                    if on_meter:
                        on_meter(ed)
                else:
                    if et == 'CurrentProgramSceneChanged':
                        self.current_scene = ed.get('sceneName')
                    if on_event:
                        on_event(et, ed)

    async def scene(self):
        r = await self.request('GetCurrentProgramScene')
        self.current_scene = r.get('currentProgramSceneName') or r.get('sceneName')
        return self.current_scene

    async def set_scene(self, name):
        await self.request('SetCurrentProgramScene', {"sceneName": name})
        self.current_scene = name


# --------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# the two behaviours
# --------------------------------------------------------------------- #
async def scene_switcher(obs, cfg, stop):
    games = {k.lower(): v for k, v in cfg['games'].items()}
    managed = set(cfg['managed'])
    last_exe = None
    while not stop.is_set():
        try:
            exe = foreground_exe()
            if exe != last_exe:
                last_exe = exe
                target = games.get((exe or '').lower()) or cfg.get('fallback_scene')
                cur = obs.current_scene or await obs.scene()
                if target and target != cur:
                    if cur in managed:
                        await obs.set_scene(target)
                        log("%s -> scene '%s'" % (exe, target))
                    else:
                        log("%s wants '%s' but holding on '%s' (not managed)"
                            % (exe, target, cur))
        except Exception as e:
            log("switcher: %s" % e)
        await asyncio.sleep(cfg['switch_poll_seconds'])


class ClipTrigger:
    def __init__(self, obs, cfg):
        self.obs, self.cfg = obs, cfg
        self.hot = 0
        self.last_clip = 0.0
        self.queue = asyncio.Queue()

    def on_meter(self, ed):
        if not self.cfg['clip_enabled']:
            return
        for inp in ed.get('inputs', []):
            if inp.get('inputName') != self.cfg['clip_input']:
                continue
            peak = 0.0
            for ch in inp.get('inputLevelsMul') or []:
                for s in ch:
                    peak = max(peak, s)
            db = 20 * (peak and __import__('math').log10(peak) or -10)
            if peak <= 0:
                db = -200.0
            if db >= self.cfg['clip_threshold_db']:
                self.hot += 1
                if self.hot >= self.cfg['clip_sustain_frames']:
                    self.hot = 0
                    self.queue.put_nowait(db)
            else:
                self.hot = max(0, self.hot - 1)

    async def run(self, stop):
        managed = set(self.cfg['managed'])
        while not stop.is_set():
            try:
                db = await asyncio.wait_for(self.queue.get(), 1.0)
            except asyncio.TimeoutError:
                continue
            now = time.time()
            if now - self.last_clip < self.cfg['clip_cooldown_seconds']:
                continue
            cur = self.obs.current_scene
            if self.cfg['clip_only_in_managed'] and cur not in managed:
                continue
            try:
                st = await self.obs.request('GetReplayBufferStatus')
                if not st.get('outputActive'):
                    log("reaction detected but replay buffer is off - skipping")
                    continue
                await self.obs.request('SaveReplayBuffer')
                self.last_clip = now
                log("clip saved (mic hit %.1f dBFS on '%s')" % (db, cur))
            except Exception as e:
                log("clip: %s" % e)


def on_event(et, ed):
    if et == 'ReplayBufferSaved':
        path = ed.get('savedReplayPath', '?')
        log("replay written: %s" % path)
        with open(CLIPLOG, 'a', encoding='utf-8') as f:
            f.write("%s\t%s\n" % (time.strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S'), path))
    elif et == 'CurrentProgramSceneChanged':
        log("scene is now '%s'" % ed.get('sceneName'))


# --------------------------------------------------------------------- #
async def main():
    cfg = load_config()

    if '--probe' in sys.argv:
        log("foreground probe - alt-tab around, Ctrl+C to stop")
        last = None
        while True:
            exe = foreground_exe()
            if exe != last:
                last = exe
                mapped = cfg['games'].get(exe or '', '(no mapping)')
                log("foreground: %-38s -> %s" % (exe, mapped))
            await asyncio.sleep(1)

    obs = OBS(cfg)
    await obs.connect()
    stop = asyncio.Event()
    clips = ClipTrigger(obs, cfg)
    pump = asyncio.create_task(obs.pump(on_meter=clips.on_meter, on_event=on_event))

    if '--selftest' in sys.argv:
        scenes = [s['sceneName'] for s in
                  (await obs.request('GetSceneList'))['scenes']]
        log("scenes (%d): %s" % (len(scenes), ', '.join(scenes)))
        start = await obs.scene()
        log("current scene: %s" % start)
        probe = next((s for s in ('Just Chatting', 'Valorant') if s in scenes), None)
        if probe and probe != start:
            await obs.set_scene(probe)
            await asyncio.sleep(0.6)
            log("switch test -> %s (now: %s)" % (probe, await obs.scene()))
            await obs.set_scene(start)
            log("restored -> %s" % await obs.scene())
        rb = await obs.request('GetReplayBufferStatus')
        log("replay buffer active: %s" % rb.get('outputActive'))
        log("foreground right now: %s" % foreground_exe())
        log("SELFTEST OK")
        stop.set(); pump.cancel()
        return

    rb = await obs.request('GetReplayBufferStatus')
    if not rb.get('outputActive'):
        try:
            await obs.request('StartReplayBuffer')
            log("replay buffer started")
        except Exception as e:
            log("could not start replay buffer: %s" % e)
    await obs.scene()
    log("autopilot running - games: %s" % ', '.join(sorted(set(cfg['games'].values()))))
    log("clipping: %s (mic > %.0f dBFS, %ds cooldown)" % (
        'on' if cfg['clip_enabled'] else 'off',
        cfg['clip_threshold_db'], cfg['clip_cooldown_seconds']))
    await asyncio.gather(scene_switcher(obs, cfg, stop), clips.run(stop), pump)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    try:
        asyncio.run(main())
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        pass

Two separate things. Let me do the scene removal first, then investigate what's actually possible for in-game automation.

The Riot local API is live (port 57322). OBS is open too, so I'll remove the scenes over websocket rather than editing the file under it. First, let me confirm what game state Valorant actually exposes:

The schema has moved — state now lives in nested blobs. Digging in:

That's exactly what I needed. `matchPresenceData.sessionLoopState` reports **MENUS / PREGAME / INGAME**, plus `matchMap` and `provisioningFlow`. So in-match automation is genuinely possible.

First, removing those two scenes (over websocket, since OBS is open):

"Audio Only" still shows in the list though the count dropped by one — likely a propagation lag. Re-checking:

Both gone — 11 scenes. Now adding the in-Valorant automation to autopilot:

Testing against the live match:

Let me prove the watcher actually drives the switch, by temporarily remapping INGAME and watching it act:

Confirmed — it drove the switch and OBS acknowledged it. Putting your scene back where it was:

Both done.

## Scenes removed

`Desktop` and `Audio Only` are gone — **11 scenes** left. I removed them over websocket rather than editing the file, since you had OBS open and it would have overwritten my edit on exit. `Display Capture` survives (Just Chatting still uses it); the `Background` color source was orphaned and dropped with `Audio Only`.

## Automating scene changes *inside* Valorant

This turned out to be properly possible. The Riot Client runs a **local REST API** on 127.0.0.1 — the same thing its Discord rich presence uses — and its presence blob exposes `matchPresenceData.sessionLoopState`. I queried yours live and got:

```
state: INGAME   map: /Game/Maps/Duality/Duality   flow: Matchmaking   queue: swiftplay
```

So autopilot now watches that every 2s and maps it:

| Valorant state | Scene |
|---|---|
| `PREGAME` | **VAL - Agent Select** |
| `INGAME` | **Valorant** |
| `MENUS` | **Valorant** |
| range (`matchMap` contains `/range`) | **VAL - Warmup Split** |

Agent select, matches, and the practice range now switch themselves. Verified by temporarily remapping INGAME and watching it actually drive OBS — the log shows `valorant INGAME -> scene 'VAL - Agent Select'` and OBS confirming the change. Your scene is back on `Valorant` now.

**Clutch Cam (F9) and Replay (F11) stay manual on purpose.** They're deliberately excluded from `valorant_managed`, so nothing automatic can ever switch away from them — and no local data source exposes "you're in a 1v3" anyway, so auto-detecting a clutch isn't something I can do honestly. Press F9, play it out, press F2.

Two caveats worth knowing:

- This is read-only localhost HTTP against your own client — it doesn't touch the game process, so Vanguard is not involved. But the API is **unofficial**; a patch can change the schema. I wrote it to log "valorant state unavailable" and stop switching rather than crash, so a break degrades to manual F-keys.
- It reads the lockfile fresh each poll, so restarting Valorant or Riot Client is handled automatically.

Everything's tunable in `autopilot.config.json` under `valorant_scenes` / `valorant_managed` / `valorant_poll_seconds`, and `python obs-autopilot.py --selftest` now reports your live Valorant state as part of its check.

VAL_LOCKFILE = os.path.join(os.environ.get('LOCALAPPDATA', ''), 'Riot Games',
                            'Riot Client', 'Config', 'lockfile')


class ValorantState:
    def __init__(self):
        self._lock_sig = None
        self._conn = None      # (port, auth_header, proto)
        self._puuid = None

    def _ssl(self):
        import ssl
        c = ssl.create_default_context()
        c.check_hostname = False
        c.verify_mode = ssl.CERT_NONE
        return c

    def _get(self, path):
        import urllib.request
        port, auth, proto = self._conn
        req = urllib.request.Request("%s://127.0.0.1:%s%s" % (proto, port, path),
                                     headers={"Authorization": auth})
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, context=self._ssl(), timeout=4) as r:
            return json.load(r)

    def _ensure(self):
        """(Re)read the lockfile if the client restarted."""
        st = os.stat(VAL_LOCKFILE)          # raises if client is closed
        sig = (st.st_mtime, st.st_size)
        if sig != self._lock_sig or self._conn is None:
            _, _pid, port, pw, proto = open(VAL_LOCKFILE).read().strip().split(':')
            self._conn = (port, "Basic " + base64.b64encode(
                ("riot:" + pw).encode()).decode(), proto)
            self._lock_sig = sig
            self._puuid = None
        if not self._puuid:
            self._puuid = self._get('/chat/v1/session').get('puuid')

    def read(self):
        """-> dict(state, map, flow, queue) or None when unavailable."""
        self._ensure()
        for p in self._get('/chat/v4/presences').get('presences', []):
            if p.get('puuid') != self._puuid or not p.get('private'):
                continue
            if p.get('product') != 'valorant':
                continue
            blob = json.loads(base64.b64decode(p['private']))
            m = blob.get('matchPresenceData') or {}
            if not m.get('sessionLoopState'):
                continue
            return {"state": m.get('sessionLoopState'),
                    "map": m.get('matchMap') or '',
                    "flow": m.get('provisioningFlow') or '',
                    "queue": m.get('queueId') or ''}
        return None


async def valorant_watcher(obs, cfg, stop):
    if not cfg.get('valorant_states_enabled'):
        return
    val = ValorantState()
    managed = set(cfg['valorant_managed'])
    mapping = cfg['valorant_scenes']
    last_key = None
    warned = False
    while not stop.is_set():
        try:
            info = await asyncio.to_thread(val.read)
            warned = False
            if info:
                key = info['state']
                if (info['flow'] or '').lower() == 'shootingrange' \
                        or '/range' in info['map'].lower():
                    key = 'RANGE'
                if key != last_key:
                    last_key = key
                    target = mapping.get(key)
                    cur = obs.current_scene or await obs.scene()
                    if target and target != cur:
                        if cur in managed:
                            await obs.set_scene(target)
                            log("valorant %s -> scene '%s'" % (key, target))
                        else:

        except Exception as e:
            if not warned:
                log("valorant state unavailable (%s)" % e)
                warned = True
            last_key = None
        await asyncio.sleep(cfg['valorant_poll_seconds'])

"""Remove the replay scene and add the live scoreboard, over obs-websocket."""
import asyncio, base64, hashlib, json, os

from websockets.asyncio.client import connect

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
C = json.load(open(os.path.join(HERE, 'autopilot.config.json'), encoding='utf-8'))

URL = "http://127.0.0.1:%d/scoreboard.html?accent=valorant" % C['hud_port']
SETTINGS = {
    "url": URL, "width": 520, "height": 56,
    "css": "body { background-color: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0); margin: 0px auto; overflow: hidden; }",
    "shutdown": False, "restart_when_active": True, "reroute_audio": False,
    "fps_custom": False, "webpage_control_level": 1,
}
# strip sits just above each scene's handcam box
PLACE = {
    "Valorant":           (1384, 636, 520, 56),
    "VAL - Agent Select": (1340, 436, 540, 58),
    "VAL - Clutch Cam":   (1370, 656, 520, 56),
    "VAL - Warmup Split": (1330, 316, 560, 60),
}
NAME = "VAL Scoreboard"


async def main():
    ws = await connect("ws://%s:%d" % (C['host'], C['port']))
    hello = json.loads(await ws.recv())
    d = {"rpcVersion": 1, "eventSubscriptions": 0}
    a = hello['d'].get('authentication')
    if a:
        s = base64.b64encode(hashlib.sha256(
            (C['password'] + a['salt']).encode()).digest()).decode()
        d['authentication'] = base64.b64encode(hashlib.sha256(
            (s + a['challenge']).encode()).digest()).decode()
    await ws.send(json.dumps({"op": 1, "d": d}))
    await ws.recv()

    n = [0]

    async def req(t, data=None, tolerant=False):
        n[0] += 1
        rid = str(n[0])
        await ws.send(json.dumps({"op": 6, "d": {
            "requestType": t, "requestId": rid, "requestData": data or {}}}))
        while True:
            m = json.loads(await ws.recv())
            if m.get('op') == 7 and m['d']['requestId'] == rid:
                st = m['d']['requestStatus']
                if not st.get('result'):
                    msg = "%s: %s" % (t, st.get('comment') or st.get('code'))
                    if tolerant:
                        print("   (skip) %s" % msg)
                        return None
                    raise RuntimeError(msg)
                return m['d'].get('responseData') or {}

    scenes = [s['sceneName'] for s in (await req('GetSceneList'))['scenes']]
    print("scenes before (%d)" % len(scenes))

    # --- 1. drop the replay scene + its media source -------------------
    if 'VAL - Replay' in scenes:
        await req('RemoveScene', {"sceneName": 'VAL - Replay'})
        print("removed scene 'VAL - Replay'")
    await req('RemoveInput', {"inputName": 'Replay Player'}, tolerant=True)

    # --- 2. add the scoreboard ------------------------------------------
    inputs = [i['inputName'] for i in (await req('GetInputList'))['inputs']]
    if NAME in inputs:
        await req('RemoveInput', {"inputName": NAME}, tolerant=True)

    first = True
    for scene, (x, y, w, h) in PLACE.items():
        if scene not in scenes:
            print("   (skip) no scene '%s'" % scene)
            continue
        if first:
            r = await req('CreateInput', {
                "sceneName": scene, "inputName": NAME,
                "inputKind": "browser_source", "inputSettings": SETTINGS,
                "sceneItemEnabled": True})
            first = False
        else:
            r = await req('CreateSceneItem', {
                "sceneName": scene, "sourceName": NAME, "sceneItemEnabled": True})
        item_id = r['sceneItemId']
        await req('SetSceneItemTransform', {
            "sceneName": scene, "sceneItemId": item_id,
            "sceneItemTransform": {
                "positionX": float(x), "positionY": float(y),
                "alignment": 5, "boundsType": "OBS_BOUNDS_SCALE_INNER",
                "boundsAlignment": 0,
                "boundsWidth": float(w), "boundsHeight": float(h)}})
        print("added to '%-20s' at (%d,%d) %dx%d" % (scene, x, y, w, h))

    after = [s['sceneName'] for s in (await req('GetSceneList'))['scenes']]
    print("\nscenes after (%d): %s" % (len(after), ', '.join(after)))
    await ws.close()


asyncio.run(main())

-- Starts OBS Autopilot when OBS starts.
--
-- Autopilot exits by itself when the obs-websocket connection drops, so
-- closing OBS closes it too. That also covers an OBS crash, which an
-- explicit kill-on-unload would miss.
--
-- Add via Tools -> Scripts -> "+" and pick this file. Nothing to configure.

obs = obslua

local PYTHONW = "C:\\Users\\Srini\\AppData\\Local\\Programs\\Python\\Python313\\pythonw.exe"
local SCRIPT  = "C:\\Users\\Srini\\obs-tools\\obs-autopilot.py"

function script_description()
  return "Launches OBS Autopilot (per-game scene switching, reaction " ..
         "clipping, live Valorant HUD) when OBS starts. It shuts itself " ..
         "down when OBS closes."
end

function script_load(settings)
  -- "start" detaches so OBS never waits on it; pythonw means no console.
  local cmd = 'start "" "' .. PYTHONW .. '" "' .. SCRIPT .. '"'
  obs.script_log(obs.LOG_INFO, "launching autopilot: " .. cmd)
  os.execute(cmd)
end

output:
Here's what's genuinely still open, in priority order.

## Blocking — stream won't work without these

1. **Stream key.** Still unset. This is the only thing that stops you going live, and it means the streaming path is the one part of this whole setup I've never been able to test end to end.
2. **The Lua launcher.** Tools → Scripts → "+" → `autopilot-launcher.lua`. Until you do this, autopilot never starts, which means no auto-switching, no clipping, and a blank HUD.

## Worth 5 minutes before your first stream

- **Measure your upload.** I set 6000 kbps on an assumption you never confirmed. You want ~9–12 Mbps stable. If it's below that, drop to 4500 — and for The Finals specifically, 900p60 beats blocky 1080p60.
- **Fire a Test Alert** from the StreamElements dashboard. Alerts are the one component I could only verify renders blank-when-idle; I've never seen one actually fire, and `reroute_audio` means the sound should land in your OBS mixer as its own channel.
- **Check your mic levels.** The gate (−35/−45 dB) and compressor (3:1 @ −18 dB) are sensible defaults, not calibrated to your voice. Talk at normal volume and confirm you're peaking around −12 to −6 in the mixer.
- **Turn off Valorant's perf overlay.** Your client has Client FPS / tick rate / packet loss / shooting error showing top-left — I saw it in the capture. That'll be on stream.

## Two things I'd flag as real

**Your mic is your webcam.** Confirmed from the OBS log: `Microphone (Brio 100) initialized (source: Mic/Aux)` — it's the only audio input on the machine. For a handcam stream where you're talking over gameplay, a webcam mic is the weakest link in the whole setup. Nothing I can fix in software.

**Your obs-websocket password is embedded in overlay URLs.** `reactive.html` and the scoreboard carry `?pw=Z43a5wrhJVqJtKXW` in their source URL, visible in OBS's properties panel and in `Main.json`. Harmless locally, but it would leak if you ever screenshot that panel on stream or share your scene collection. If that bothers you, rotate it in Tools → WebSocket Server Settings and I'll update the URLs.

## Minor, just so you know

- Handcam runs at **1080p30** — that's the Brio's only mode, so it's 30fps inside a 60fps canvas. Normal, not a misconfiguration.
- **The Finals mapping is still unverified** (`Discovery.exe`). Run `--probe`, alt-tab in, correct the config if it differs.
- Clips land in `D:\Recordings` alongside VODs, distinguished by the `Replay ` filename prefix.

Want me to knock out the ones I can do without you — rotating the websocket password and moving it out of the URLs, or setting up a split folder for clips vs VODs?

questions.question: Which reactive components should I add?

options.label: Mic-muted badge (Recommended)
options.description: Reacts to obs-websocket's InputMuteStateChanged. A clear 'MIC MUTED' badge appears whenever Mic/Aux is muted, so you never talk over a dead mic for ten minutes. Cheapest to build, highest practical payoff, and it fixes the single most common streaming mistake.

options.label: Round win/loss flash
options.description: I already poll ally/enemy score every 2s. When your score increments, a brief teal flare; when theirs does, a crimson one. Genuinely reactive to gameplay rather than audio, and derived entirely from data I'm already reading.

options.label: 'CLIPPED' confirmation flash
options.description: Right now auto-clipping gives you no on-screen feedback — you can't tell whether your shout actually saved a clip. A 3-second badge when the replay buffer fires closes that loop, and doubles as a cue to viewers that the moment was saved.

options.label: Win streak + stream uptime on the HUD
options.description: Extends the existing Today cell: a '3 WIN STREAK' flag computed from daily.json, plus an uptime counter driven by StreamStateChanged. Small additions to a bar that's already there.

"""Add the mic-mute badge to non-Valorant scenes, and the season-stats
strip to the two Valorant scenes that have dead time for it."""
import asyncio, base64, hashlib, json, os

from websockets.asyncio.client import connect

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
C = json.load(open(os.path.join(HERE, 'autopilot.config.json'), encoding='utf-8'))
BASE = "http://127.0.0.1:%d/scoreboard.html" % C['hud_port']
CSS = ("body { background-color: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0); margin: 0px auto; "
       "overflow: hidden; }")

# name -> (url, canvas w, h, {scene: (x, y)})
SOURCES = {
    "Mic Badge": (
        BASE + "?mic_only=1&accent=valorant", 320, 64,
        {"The Finals": (1584, 632), "Single Player": (1584, 632),
         "Just Chatting": (1584, 632)},
    ),
    "VAL Stats": (
        BASE + "?mode=stats&accent=valorant", 900, 64,
        {"VAL - Agent Select": (1004, 352), "VAL - Warmup Split": (1004, 234)},
    ),
}


async def main():
    ws = await connect("ws://%s:%d" % (C['host'], C['port']))
    hello = json.loads(await ws.recv())
    d = {"rpcVersion": 1, "eventSubscriptions": 0}
    a = hello['d'].get('authentication')
    if a:
        sec = base64.b64encode(hashlib.sha256(
            (C['password'] + a['salt']).encode()).digest()).decode()
        d['authentication'] = base64.b64encode(hashlib.sha256(
            (sec + a['challenge']).encode()).digest()).decode()
    await ws.send(json.dumps({"op": 1, "d": d}))
    await ws.recv()

    n = [0]

    async def req(t, data=None, tolerant=False):
        n[0] += 1
        rid = str(n[0])
        await ws.send(json.dumps({"op": 6, "d": {
            "requestType": t, "requestId": rid, "requestData": data or {}}}))
        while True:
            m = json.loads(await ws.recv())
            if m.get('op') == 7 and m['d']['requestId'] == rid:
                st = m['d']['requestStatus']
                if not st.get('result'):
                    msg = "%s: %s" % (t, st.get('comment') or st.get('code'))
                    if tolerant:
                        return None
                    raise RuntimeError(msg)
                return m['d'].get('responseData') or {}

    scenes = [s['sceneName'] for s in (await req('GetSceneList'))['scenes']]
    existing = [i['inputName'] for i in (await req('GetInputList'))['inputs']]

    for name, (url, w, h, places) in SOURCES.items():
        if name in existing:
            await req('RemoveInput', {"inputName": name}, tolerant=True)
        settings = {"url": url, "width": w, "height": h, "css": CSS,
                    "shutdown": False, "restart_when_active": True,
                    "reroute_audio": False, "fps_custom": False,
                    "webpage_control_level": 1}
        first = True
        for scene, (x, y) in places.items():
            if scene not in scenes:
                print("   (skip) no scene '%s'" % scene)
                continue
            if first:
                r = await req('CreateInput', {
                    "sceneName": scene, "inputName": name,
                    "inputKind": "browser_source", "inputSettings": settings,
                    "sceneItemEnabled": True})
                first = False
            else:
                r = await req('CreateSceneItem', {
                    "sceneName": scene, "sourceName": name,
                    "sceneItemEnabled": True})
            await req('SetSceneItemTransform', {
                "sceneName": scene, "sceneItemId": r['sceneItemId'],
                "sceneItemTransform": {
                    "positionX": float(x), "positionY": float(y),
                    "alignment": 5, "boundsType": "OBS_BOUNDS_SCALE_INNER",
                    "boundsAlignment": 0,
                    "boundsWidth": float(w), "boundsHeight": float(h)}})
            print("%-10s -> %-20s (%d,%d) %dx%d" % (name, scene, x, y, w, h))

    await ws.close()


asyncio.run(main())

Good question — and there's a trap in it I should close first. Adding the script while autopilot is already running would spawn a **second** instance, and two copies would both switch scenes and double-save clips. Let me make that impossible:

The guard failed, and the reason is a classic Windows gotcha: Python's `HTTPServer` sets `allow_reuse_address = 1`, and on Windows `SO_REUSEADDR` lets you bind an **already-bound** port. So the port is not a usable lock here. Switching to a named mutex, which is the correct Windows mechanism:

Backslash got mangled through the heredoc again. Sidestepping it entirely with a name that needs no escaping:

The old instance predates the mutex code, so there was nothing to collide with. Testing properly with both copies on the new code:

Now it's safe to explain — I verified the guard: a second copy exits immediately with `another autopilot is already running`, and the first keeps serving.

## Why this step exists

OBS has no built-in "run a program when I start". But OBS's **script system** does load Lua when OBS launches, so `autopilot-launcher.lua` is a ~20-line script whose `script_load` spawns autopilot. Pair that with autopilot exiting when the OBS connection drops (verified earlier) and you get exactly the lifecycle you asked for: starts with OBS, dies with OBS, never runs at login.

## What to click

1. In OBS, menu bar → **Tools** → **Scripts**
2. The Scripts window opens. The left pane lists loaded scripts — you'll see `instant-replay.lua` there.
3. Click the **`+`** button under that list.
4. A file dialog opens, defaulting to OBS's own scripts folder. Navigate to `C:\Users\Srini\obs-tools\` and select **`autopilot-launcher.lua`**. *Tip: paste that path straight into the filename box rather than clicking through.*
5. It loads immediately — you'll see its description appear in the right-hand pane.
6. **While you're there:** click `instant-replay.lua`, then the **`–`** button to remove it. It's inert now that the replay scene is gone.
7. Close the window. It's saved with the scene collection — nothing to confirm.

## What you'll see right now

Adding it fires `script_load` straight away, so it'll try to launch autopilot — but one is already running, so the new copy exits instantly. Harmless, and that's the guard working.

## How to confirm it actually worked

Close OBS completely, reopen it, then check any one of these:

- `C:\Users\Srini\obs-tools\autopilot.log` has a fresh `connected to obs-websocket` line timestamped at the reopen
- Task Manager shows **`pythonw.exe`** running
- Easiest: get into a Valorant match and the HUD appears

## One cosmetic snag

The script uses `os.execute`, which goes through `cmd`, so you may see a console window flash for a fraction of a second as OBS starts. It doesn't stay open.

If you ever upgrade Python, the two paths at the top of the `.lua` need updating — they point at `Python313`.

questions.question: Which should I build? (All work in both games unless noted.)

options.label: Input display — keys + mouse (Recommended)
options.description: An on-screen WASD/mouse cluster that lights up as you play — the natural companion to a handcam, since viewers watch both for mechanics. Works in every game, fully local, no API. Privacy by design: it polls only a fixed allowlist of game keys (WASD, shift, ctrl, space, Q/E/C/X/F/R, mouse buttons) via GetAsyncKeyState — it never reads text or logs anything.

options.label: The Finals rank + RS + daily change
options.description: Live rank, rank score and today's movement from the community leaderboard API, shown in The Finals scene the way the Valorant bar works. I need your Embark ID (name#1234) — and it only resolves if you're inside the top 10,000, which I can check as soon as you give it to me.

options.label: Stream health indicator
options.description: Reads dropped frames and encoder congestion from obs-websocket. Stays completely invisible while healthy and only surfaces a discreet warning when your connection actually degrades — so you find out mid-stream instead of from VOD comments. Especially relevant since The Finals' destruction is the most likely thing to saturate 6000 kbps.

options.label: APM / input intensity meter
options.description: Built from the same input polling as the key display — a rolling actions-per-minute figure, which reads well on a handcam stream and spikes visibly during fights. Cheap to add if the input display is in.

import io

    "hud_port": 4466,
}''', '''    "hud_enabled": True,
    "hud_port": 4466,
    # --- input display / APM ---
    "input_display_enabled": True,
    "input_poll_hz": 30,
    # --- stream health ---
    "health_warn_pct": 1.0,      # skipped frames %% that counts as a warning
    "health_bad_pct": 5.0,
    # --- The Finals rank (community leaderboard API) ---
    "finals_embark_id": "",      # e.g. "Name#1234"; blank disables
    "finals_season": "s7",

}''')

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- input poll
anchor = """# --------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Valorant Tracker (Overwolf) log reader."""

block = '''# --------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Input display + APM.
# Polls a FIXED ALLOWLIST of game keys with GetAsyncKeyState. It never
# reads text, never records anything, and cannot see keys outside this
# table - it is an on-screen input display, not an input log.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------- #
KEYMAP = [
    ("W", 0x57), ("A", 0x41), ("S", 0x53), ("D", 0x44),
    ("SHIFT", 0x10), ("CTRL", 0x11), ("SPACE", 0x20),
    ("Q", 0x51), ("E", 0x45), ("C", 0x43), ("X", 0x58),
    ("F", 0x46), ("R", 0x52), ("V", 0x56),
    ("M1", 0x01), ("M2", 0x02), ("M3", 0x04), ("M4", 0x05), ("M5", 0x06),
]
_APM_WINDOW = 60.0


def input_poller(cfg, stop):
    """Runs in a thread; publishes pressed keys + APM into LATEST."""
    gks = _u32.GetAsyncKeyState
    down = {name: False for name, _ in KEYMAP}
    presses = []                      # timestamps of key-down transitions
    period = 1.0 / max(5, int(cfg.get('input_poll_hz') or 30))
    while not stop.is_set():
        now = time.time()
        pressed = []
        for name, vk in KEYMAP:
            is_down = bool(gks(vk) & 0x8000)
            if is_down:
                pressed.append(name)
            if is_down and not down[name]:
                presses.append(now)
            down[name] = is_down
        cutoff = now - _APM_WINDOW
        while presses and presses[0] < cutoff:
            presses.pop(0)
        LATEST['keys'] = pressed
        LATEST['apm'] = len(presses)
        time.sleep(period)


''' + anchor

            st = await obs.request('GetStreamStatus')
            LATEST['streaming'] = bool(st.get('outputActive'))

            LATEST['streaming'] = bool(st.get('outputActive'))
            LATEST['uptime_ms'] = int(st.get('outputDuration') or 0)

            # Stream health: skipped frames on the encode + network side.
            total = int(st.get('outputTotalFrames') or 0)
            skipped = int(st.get('outputSkippedFrames') or 0)
            pct = (100.0 * skipped / total) if total else 0.0
            cong = float(st.get('outputCongestion') or 0.0)
            stats = await obs.request('GetStats')
            rt = int(stats.get('renderTotalFrames') or 0)
            rs = int(stats.get('renderSkippedFrames') or 0)
            rpct = (100.0 * rs / rt) if rt else 0.0

"""Add the input display to the live scenes, and a Finals rank strip."""
import asyncio, base64, hashlib, json, os

from websockets.asyncio.client import connect

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
C = json.load(open(os.path.join(HERE, 'autopilot.config.json'), encoding='utf-8'))
ROOT = "http://127.0.0.1:%d" % C['hud_port']
CSS = ("body { background-color: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0); margin: 0px auto; "
       "overflow: hidden; }")

# Sits just left of the handcam in the play scenes - the two read as one
# block, and that strip of screen is empty in both games.
SOURCES = {
    "Input Display": (
        ROOT + "/inputs.html?accent=valorant", 440, 210,
        {"Valorant": (1040, 700), "VAL - Clutch Cam": (966, 720),
         "VAL - Warmup Split": (876, 380), "Single Player": (1040, 700)},
    ),
    "Input Display (Finals)": (
        ROOT + "/inputs.html?accent=finals", 440, 210,
        {"The Finals": (1040, 700)},
    ),
    "Finals Rank": (
        ROOT + "/scoreboard.html?mode=finals&accent=finals", 760, 64,
        {"The Finals": (1144, 632)},
    ),
}


async def main():
    ws = await connect("ws://%s:%d" % (C['host'], C['port']))
    hello = json.loads(await ws.recv())
    d = {"rpcVersion": 1, "eventSubscriptions": 0}
    a = hello['d'].get('authentication')
    if a:
        sec = base64.b64encode(hashlib.sha256(
            (C['password'] + a['salt']).encode()).digest()).decode()
        d['authentication'] = base64.b64encode(hashlib.sha256(
            (sec + a['challenge']).encode()).digest()).decode()
    await ws.send(json.dumps({"op": 1, "d": d}))
    await ws.recv()

    n = [0]

    async def req(t, data=None, tolerant=False):
        n[0] += 1
        rid = str(n[0])
        await ws.send(json.dumps({"op": 6, "d": {
            "requestType": t, "requestId": rid, "requestData": data or {}}}))
        while True:
            m = json.loads(await ws.recv())
            if m.get('op') == 7 and m['d']['requestId'] == rid:
                st = m['d']['requestStatus']
                if not st.get('result'):
                    if tolerant:
                        return None
                    raise RuntimeError("%s: %s" % (t, st.get('comment') or st.get('code')))
                return m['d'].get('responseData') or {}

    scenes = [s['sceneName'] for s in (await req('GetSceneList'))['scenes']]
    existing = [i['inputName'] for i in (await req('GetInputList'))['inputs']]

    for name, (url, w, h, places) in SOURCES.items():
        if name in existing:
            await req('RemoveInput', {"inputName": name}, tolerant=True)
        settings = {"url": url, "width": w, "height": h, "css": CSS,
                    "shutdown": False, "restart_when_active": True,
                    "reroute_audio": False, "fps_custom": False,
                    "webpage_control_level": 1}
        first = True
        for scene, (x, y) in places.items():
            if scene not in scenes:
                print("   (skip) no scene '%s'" % scene)
                continue
            if first:
                r = await req('CreateInput', {
                    "sceneName": scene, "inputName": name,
                    "inputKind": "browser_source", "inputSettings": settings,
                    "sceneItemEnabled": True})
                first = False
            else:
                r = await req('CreateSceneItem', {
                    "sceneName": scene, "sourceName": name,
                    "sceneItemEnabled": True})
            await req('SetSceneItemTransform', {
                "sceneName": scene, "sceneItemId": r['sceneItemId'],
                "sceneItemTransform": {
                    "positionX": float(x), "positionY": float(y),
                    "alignment": 5, "boundsType": "OBS_BOUNDS_SCALE_INNER",
                    "boundsAlignment": 0,
                    "boundsWidth": float(w), "boundsHeight": float(h)}})
            print("%-24s -> %-20s (%d,%d) %dx%d" % (name, scene, x, y, w, h))

    await ws.close()


asyncio.run(main())

async def main():
    ws = await connect("ws://%s:%d" % (C['host'], C['port']))
    hello = json.loads(await ws.recv())
    d = {"rpcVersion": 1, "eventSubscriptions": 0}
    a = hello['d'].get('authentication')
    if a:
        sec = base64.b64encode(hashlib.sha256(
            (C['password'] + a['salt']).encode()).digest()).decode()
        d['authentication'] = base64.b64encode(hashlib.sha256(
            (sec + a['challenge']).encode()).digest()).decode()
    await ws.send(json.dumps({"op": 1, "d": d}))
    await ws.recv()

    n = [0]

    async def req(t, data=None, tolerant=False):
        n[0] += 1
        rid = str(n[0])
        await ws.send(json.dumps({"op": 6, "d": {
            "requestType": t, "requestId": rid, "requestData": data or {}}}))
        while True:
            m = json.loads(await ws.recv())
            if m.get('op') == 7 and m['d']['requestId'] == rid:
                st = m['d']['requestStatus']
                if not st.get('result'):
                    if tolerant:
                        return None
                    raise RuntimeError("%s: %s" % (t, st.get('comment') or st.get('code')))
                return m['d'].get('responseData') or {}

    # make the browser canvases match what the layout assumes
    for name, (w, h) in CANVAS.items():
        if name.startswith('Handcam'):
            continue
        await req('SetInputSettings', {
            "inputName": name, "inputSettings": {"width": w, "height": h},
            "overlay": True}, tolerant=True)

    scenes = [s['sceneName'] for s in (await req('GetSceneList'))['scenes']]
    for scene, items in LAYOUT.items():
        if scene not in scenes:
            print("(skip) no scene %r" % scene)
            continue
        present = {i['sourceName']: i['sceneItemId']
                   for i in (await req('GetSceneItemList', {"sceneName": scene}))['sceneItems']}
        print("\n%s" % scene)
        for src, x, y, w, h in items:
            iid = present.get(src)
            if iid is None:
                print("   (skip) %r not in this scene" % src)
                continue
            await req('SetSceneItemTransform', {
                "sceneName": scene, "sceneItemId": iid,
                "sceneItemTransform": {
                    "positionX": float(x), "positionY": float(y),
                    "alignment": 5, "boundsType": "OBS_BOUNDS_SCALE_INNER",
                    "boundsAlignment": 0,
                    "boundsWidth": float(w), "boundsHeight": float(h)}})
            cw, ch = CANVAS.get(src, (16, 9))
            warn = "" if abs((w / h) - (cw / ch)) < 0.06 else "  <-- aspect mismatch"
            print("   %-26s (%4d,%4d) %4dx%-4d%s" % (src, x, y, w, h, warn))

    await ws.close()

old = s[start:end]

new = '''def _build_keymap():
    """Full keyboard. Because this watches every typing key, the poller
    blanks itself unless a game has focus - see input_only_in_game."""
    km = [("ESC", 0x1B)]
    km += [("F%d" % i, 0x70 + i - 1) for i in range(1, 13)]
    km += [("TILDE", 0xC0)]
    km += [(c, 0x30 + int(c)) for c in "1234567890"]
    km += [("MINUS", 0xBD), ("EQUALS", 0xBB), ("BACKSPACE", 0x08)]

The cause was a genuine bug of mine, not a limitation: in the full-keyboard rewrite I wired the script to iterate `[data-k]` elements, but left the mouse SVG parts with only `id="m1"…"m5"` and no `data-k`. So the keyboard worked and the mouse silently never toggled. Five attributes fixed it.

"""Temporarily unblank the input display so it can be tested without a game.

    python test_inputs.py [seconds]      default 90

Creates input_gate_off.flag, which autopilot picks up within ~0.4s, then
always removes it again - including on Ctrl+C or a crash - so the overlay
can never be left permanently exposed to desktop typing.
"""
import json
import os
import sys
import time
import urllib.request

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
FLAG = os.path.join(HERE, 'input_gate_off.flag')
CFG = json.load(open(os.path.join(HERE, 'autopilot.config.json'), encoding='utf-8'))
URL = "http://127.0.0.1:%d/state.json" % CFG['hud_port']
SECONDS = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 90


def state():
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(URL, timeout=3) as r:
            return json.load(r)
    except Exception:
        return None


def main():
    if state() is None:
        print("autopilot is not running (nothing serving port %d)." % CFG['hud_port'])
        print("Open OBS first - the launcher script starts it.")
        return 1

    open(FLAG, 'w').write('temporary')
    print("Gate bypassed for %ds. Press keys now - they should light up." % SECONDS)
    print("The display is live on stream while this runs, so do not type")
    print("anything private until it restores.\n")
    try:
        end = time.time() + SECONDS
        seen = set()
        while time.time() < end:
            d = state() or {}
            keys = d.get('keys') or []
            seen.update(keys)
            left = int(end - time.time())
            print("\r  %3ds left | gated=%-5s | down: %-46s"
                  % (left, d.get('input_gated'), ','.join(keys)[:46]), end='')
            time.sleep(0.25)
        print()
        print("\nkeys seen during the test (%d): %s"
              % (len(seen), ', '.join(sorted(seen)) or 'none - check autopilot'))
    finally:
        if os.path.exists(FLAG):
            os.remove(FLAG)
        time.sleep(0.6)
        print("Gate restored (input_gated=%s)." % (state() or {}).get('input_gated'))
    return 0


if __name__ == '__main__':
    try:
        sys.exit(main())
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        if os.path.exists(FLAG):
            os.remove(FLAG)
        print("\nstopped; gate restored")

"""Report OBS inputs that are in no scene, and local files that are dead."""
import asyncio, base64, hashlib, json, os

from websockets.asyncio.client import connect

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
C = json.load(open(os.path.join(HERE, 'autopilot.config.json'), encoding='utf-8'))

# one-shot utilities whose work is already applied and persisted in OBS
ONE_SHOT = ['apply_hud.py', 'resize_hud.py', 'add_badges.py', 'add_inputs.py',
            'obs_remove_scenes.py', 'val_probe.py', 'autopilot.out', 'dup.out']
KEEP = ['obs-autopilot.py', 'layout.py', 'autopilot-launcher.lua',
        'autopilot.config.json', 'identity.json', 'daily.json', 'clips.log',
        'autopilot.log', 'run-autopilot.bat', 'test_inputs.py',
        'scan_orphans.py']


async def main():
    ws = await connect("ws://%s:%d" % (C['host'], C['port']))
    hello = json.loads(await ws.recv())
    d = {"rpcVersion": 1, "eventSubscriptions": 0}
    a = hello['d'].get('authentication')
    if a:
        sec = base64.b64encode(hashlib.sha256(
            (C['password'] + a['salt']).encode()).digest()).decode()
        d['authentication'] = base64.b64encode(hashlib.sha256(
            (sec + a['challenge']).encode()).digest()).decode()
    await ws.send(json.dumps({"op": 1, "d": d}))
    await ws.recv()

    n = [0]

    async def req(t, data=None):
        n[0] += 1
        rid = str(n[0])
        await ws.send(json.dumps({"op": 6, "d": {
            "requestType": t, "requestId": rid, "requestData": data or {}}}))
        while True:
            m = json.loads(await ws.recv())
            if m.get('op') == 7 and m['d']['requestId'] == rid:
                return m['d'].get('responseData') or {}

    inputs = [i['inputName'] for i in (await req('GetInputList'))['inputs']]
    scenes = [s['sceneName'] for s in (await req('GetSceneList'))['scenes']]

    used = {}
    for sc in scenes:
        for it in (await req('GetSceneItemList', {"sceneName": sc}))['sceneItems']:
            used.setdefault(it['sourceName'], []).append(
                (sc, it['sceneItemEnabled']))

    print("=== OBS inputs (%d) ===" % len(inputs))
    for name in sorted(inputs):
        where = used.get(name)
        if not where:
            print("  ORPHAN   %-28s in no scene" % name)
        else:
            on = sum(1 for _, e in where if e)
            print("  used     %-28s %d scene(s), %d enabled" % (name, len(where), on))

    print("\n=== scenes with no items ===")
    for sc in scenes:
        items = (await req('GetSceneItemList', {"sceneName": sc}))['sceneItems']
        if not items:
            print("  EMPTY    %s" % sc)

    print("\n=== obs-tools files ===")
    for f in sorted(os.listdir(HERE)):
        if f.endswith('.pyc') or f == '__pycache__':
            continue
        tag = "one-shot" if f in ONE_SHOT else ("keep" if f in KEEP else "review")
        print("  %-9s %s" % (tag, f))

    await ws.close()


asyncio.run(main())

"""Build arena-crimson by transforming a known-good stock style.

Authoring the JSON from scratch was silently rejected by NohBoard, so this
copies a shipped style (guaranteed-valid schema) and rewrites only the
colours, on both DefaultKeyStyle and every per-element override.

Critically it also clears the green key outlines: green is the chroma-key
colour, so green borders would be punched out of every key in OBS.
"""
import io, json, os

SRC = r"C:\Users\Srini\NohBoard\keyboards\wheels\alienware 17\normal-black_normal-white.style"
DST = r"C:\Users\Srini\NohBoard\keyboards\wheels\alienware 17\arena-crimson.style"

INK = {"Red": 13, "Green": 18, "Blue": 25}      # key fill, idle
BONE = {"Red": 242, "Green": 239, "Blue": 233}  # outline + label
CRIMSON = {"Red": 255, "Green": 70, "Blue": 85}  # key fill, pressed
DARK = {"Red": 20, "Green": 4, "Blue": 6}       # label on a pressed key
TEAL = {"Red": 74, "Green": 214, "Blue": 196}
GREEN = {"Red": 0, "Green": 255, "Blue": 0}     # background only

d = json.load(io.open(SRC, encoding='utf-8-sig'))


def paint(ks):
    """Recolour one KeyStyle in place, preserving every other field."""
    for face, fill, text in (('Loose', INK, BONE), ('Pressed', CRIMSON, DARK)):
        f = ks.get(face)
        if not isinstance(f, dict):
            continue
        f['Background'] = dict(fill)
        f['Text'] = dict(text)
        f['Outline'] = dict(BONE)        # never green
        f['OutlineWidth'] = 2
        f['ShowOutline'] = True
        # the stock PNGs are not shipped in this folder; drop them
        f['BackgroundImageFileName'] = None
        if isinstance(f.get('Font'), dict):
            f['Font']['FontFamily'] = 'Bahnschrift'
            f['Font']['Style'] = 1       # bold
            f['Font'].pop('DownloadUrl', None)


d['BackgroundColor'] = dict(GREEN)
d['BackgroundImageFileName'] = None
paint(d['DefaultKeyStyle'])

ms = d.get('DefaultMouseSpeedIndicatorStyle')
if isinstance(ms, dict):
    ms['InnerColor'] = dict(TEAL)
    ms['OuterColor'] = dict(BONE)
    ms['OutlineWidth'] = 2

overrides = d.get('ElementStyles') or []
painted = 0
for entry in overrides:
    val = entry.get('Value') if isinstance(entry, dict) else None
    if isinstance(val, dict) and val.get('__type') == 'KeyStyle':
        paint(val)
        painted += 1

io.open(DST, 'w', encoding='utf-8').write(json.dumps(d, indent=2))
print("derived from:", os.path.basename(SRC))
print("per-element overrides recoloured:", painted, "of", len(overrides))
print("wrote:", DST)

# sanity: no green left anywhere except the single background entry
blob = json.dumps(d)
greens = blob.count('"Green": 255')
print("green-255 occurrences:", greens, "(expected: background + any teal/bone greens)")

"""Capture NohBoard into OBS with a chroma key, in the input-deck slot."""
import asyncio, base64, hashlib, json, os

from websockets.asyncio.client import connect

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
C = json.load(open(os.path.join(HERE, 'autopilot.config.json'), encoding='utf-8'))

NAME = "NohBoard"
# title:class:exe. The class suffix (_r7_ad1) changes between WinForms runs,
# so priority 2 matches on executable only and survives that.
WINDOW = ("NohBoard v1.3.0:WindowsForms10.Window.8.app.0.141b42a_r7_ad1"
          ":NohBoard.exe")

SETTINGS = {
    "window": WINDOW,
    "method": 1,          # BitBlt - reliable for WinForms, no capture border
    "priority": 2,        # match by executable
    "cursor": False,
    "client_area": True,  # drop the title bar from the capture
    "compatibility": False,
}

# NohBoard's client area is 853x289 (aspect 2.951); boxes keep that exactly
PLACE = {
    "Valorant":           (716, 668, 758, 257),
    "The Finals":         (716, 668, 758, 257),
    "Single Player":      (716, 668, 758, 257),
    "VAL - Clutch Cam":   (642, 727, 758, 257),
    "VAL - Warmup Split": (1330, 760, 560, 190),
}


async def main():
    ws = await connect("ws://%s:%d" % (C['host'], C['port']))
    hello = json.loads(await ws.recv())
    d = {"rpcVersion": 1, "eventSubscriptions": 0}
    a = hello['d'].get('authentication')
    if a:
        sec = base64.b64encode(hashlib.sha256(
            (C['password'] + a['salt']).encode()).digest()).decode()
        d['authentication'] = base64.b64encode(hashlib.sha256(
            (sec + a['challenge']).encode()).digest()).decode()
    await ws.send(json.dumps({"op": 1, "d": d}))
    await ws.recv()

    n = [0]

    async def req(t, data=None, tolerant=False):
        n[0] += 1
        rid = str(n[0])
        await ws.send(json.dumps({"op": 6, "d": {
            "requestType": t, "requestId": rid, "requestData": data or {}}}))
        while True:
            m = json.loads(await ws.recv())
            if m.get('op') == 7 and m['d']['requestId'] == rid:
                st = m['d']['requestStatus']
                if not st.get('result'):
                    if tolerant:
                        print("   (skip) %s: %s" % (t, st.get('comment') or st.get('code')))
                        return None
                    raise RuntimeError("%s: %s" % (t, st.get('comment') or st.get('code')))
                return m['d'].get('responseData') or {}

    scenes = [s['sceneName'] for s in (await req('GetSceneList'))['scenes']]
    existing = [i['inputName'] for i in (await req('GetInputList'))['inputs']]
    if NAME in existing:
        await req('RemoveInput', {"inputName": NAME}, tolerant=True)

    first = True
    for scene, (x, y, w, h) in PLACE.items():
        if scene not in scenes:
            print("   (skip) no scene %r" % scene)
            continue
        if first:
            r = await req('CreateInput', {
                "sceneName": scene, "inputName": NAME,
                "inputKind": "window_capture", "inputSettings": SETTINGS,
                "sceneItemEnabled": True})
            first = False
            # green screen -> transparent
            await req('CreateSourceFilter', {
                "sourceName": NAME, "filterName": "Chroma Key",
                "filterKind": "chroma_key_filter_v2",
                "filterSettings": {
                    "key_color_type": "green",
                    "key_color": 65280,        # 0x00FF00 in BGR
                    "similarity": 400,
                    "smoothness": 80,
                    "spill": 100,
                    "opacity": 1.0,
                }})
            print("added chroma key filter")
        else:
            r = await req('CreateSceneItem', {
                "sceneName": scene, "sourceName": NAME, "sceneItemEnabled": True})
        await req('SetSceneItemTransform', {
            "sceneName": scene, "sceneItemId": r['sceneItemId'],
            "sceneItemTransform": {
                "positionX": float(x), "positionY": float(y),
                "alignment": 5, "boundsType": "OBS_BOUNDS_SCALE_INNER",
                "boundsAlignment": 0,
                "boundsWidth": float(w), "boundsHeight": float(h)}})
        print("%-10s -> %-20s (%d,%d) %dx%d" % (NAME, scene, x, y, w, h))

    await ws.close()


asyncio.run(main())

-- Starts OBS Autopilot and NohBoard when OBS starts, and stops NohBoard
-- when OBS exits.
--
-- Autopilot shuts itself down when the obs-websocket connection drops, so
-- it needs no kill here - that also covers an OBS crash, which an explicit
-- kill-on-unload would miss. NohBoard has no such self-exit, so it is
-- terminated in script_unload.
--
-- NohBoard must stay running and NOT minimised: OBS captures it with
-- BitBlt, which tolerates the window being covered by other windows but
-- not being minimised to the taskbar.
--
-- Add via Tools -> Scripts -> "+" and pick this file. Nothing to configure.

obs = obslua

-- Starts OBS Autopilot and NohBoard when OBS starts, and stops NohBoard
-- when OBS exits.
--
-- Autopilot shuts itself down when the obs-websocket connection drops, so
-- it needs no kill here - that also covers an OBS crash, which an explicit
-- kill-on-unload would miss. NohBoard has no such self-exit, so it is
-- terminated in script_unload.
--
-- NohBoard must stay running and NOT minimised: OBS captures it with
-- BitBlt, which tolerates the window being covered by other windows but
-- not being minimised to the taskbar.
--
-- Add via Tools -> Scripts -> "+" and pick this file. Nothing to configure.

obs = obslua

local PYTHONW   = [[C:\Users\Srini\AppData\Local\Programs\Python\Python313\pythonw.exe]]
local AUTOPILOT = [[C:\Users\Srini\obs-tools\obs-autopilot.py]]
local NOHBOARD  = [[C:\Users\Srini\NohBoard\NohBoard.exe]]
local NOHBOARD_DIR = [[C:\Users\Srini\NohBoard]]

function script_description()
  return "Launches OBS Autopilot (per-game scene switching, reaction " ..
         "clipping, live Valorant HUD) and NohBoard (input display) when " ..
         "OBS starts. Autopilot exits with OBS on its own; NohBoard is " ..
         "closed when this script unloads."
end

function script_load(settings)
  -- "start" detaches so OBS never blocks on either process.
  -- Autopilot guards itself with a named mutex, so a duplicate just exits.
  local ap = 'start "" "' .. PYTHONW .. '" "' .. AUTOPILOT .. '"'
  obs.script_log(obs.LOG_INFO, "launching autopilot")
  os.execute(ap)

  -- NohBoard is NOT single-instance, so only launch it when absent -
  -- otherwise every OBS restart stacks another copy at the same position.
  -- /D sets the working directory; NohBoard resolves keyboards/ relative
  -- to it and silently loads nothing if it is wrong.
  local nb = 'tasklist /FI "IMAGENAME eq NohBoard.exe" | find /I "NohBoard.exe" >nul' ..
             ' || start "" /D "' .. NOHBOARD_DIR .. '" "' .. NOHBOARD .. '"'
  obs.script_log(obs.LOG_INFO, "launching NohBoard if not already running")
  os.execute(nb)
end

function script_unload()
  -- NohBoard will not close itself, so close it with OBS.
  os.execute('taskkill /IM NohBoard.exe >nul 2>&1')
end

import io

P = r"C:\Users\Srini\obs-tools\obs-autopilot.py"
s = io.open(P, encoding='utf-8').read()

# --- a real process check, so the exit condition is "OBS is gone", not
#     "one websocket hiccup happened during startup" -------------------
helper = '''
def process_running(exe_name):
    """True if a process with this image name exists. Uses the toolhelp
    snapshot API directly - no subprocess, so no console window flash."""
    TH32CS_SNAPPROCESS = 0x2
    MAX_PATH = 260

    class ENTRY(ctypes.Structure):
        _fields_ = [("dwSize", wintypes.DWORD),
                    ("cntUsage", wintypes.DWORD),
                    ("th32ProcessID", wintypes.DWORD),
                    ("th32DefaultHeapID", ctypes.POINTER(ctypes.c_ulong)),
                    ("th32ModuleID", wintypes.DWORD),
                    ("cntThreads", wintypes.DWORD),
                    ("th32ParentProcessID", wintypes.DWORD),
                    ("pcPriClassBase", ctypes.c_long),
                    ("dwFlags", wintypes.DWORD),
                    ("szExeFile", ctypes.c_char * MAX_PATH)]

    snap = _k32.CreateToolhelp32Snapshot(TH32CS_SNAPPROCESS, 0)
    if snap == -1:
        return True                      # cannot tell; assume still there
    try:
        e = ENTRY()
        e.dwSize = ctypes.sizeof(ENTRY)
        want = exe_name.lower().encode()
        if not _k32.Process32First(snap, ctypes.byref(e)):
            return False
        while True:
            if e.szExeFile.lower() == want:
                return True
            if not _k32.Process32Next(snap, ctypes.byref(e)):
                return False
    finally:
        _k32.CloseHandle(snap)


'''

anchor = "# --------------------------------------------------------------------- #\n# obs-websocket client"
assert anchor in s
s = s.replace(anchor, helper.lstrip('\n') + anchor, 1)

# --- supervisor: reconnect while OBS lives, exit once it is gone -------
old = """            GRACE = 90
            started = time.time()
            while True:
                try:
                    asyncio.run(main())
                    log("OBS closed - exiting")
                    break
                except KeyboardInterrupt:
                    raise
                except Exception as e:
                    if CONNECTED_ONCE[0]:
                        log("OBS connection lost (%s) - exiting" % e)
                        break
                    if time.time() - started > GRACE:
                        log("OBS never appeared within %ds - exiting" % GRACE)
                        break
                    time.sleep(3)"""

new = """            GRACE = 90
            started = time.time()
            while True:
                try:
                    asyncio.run(main())
                except KeyboardInterrupt:
                    raise
                except Exception as e:
                    detail = str(e) or type(e).__name__
                else:
                    detail = "connection closed"
                # OBS drops early connections while it is still loading, so
                # a single disconnect is not a reason to quit. Only the OBS
                # process disappearing is.
                if not process_running('obs64.exe'):
                    log("OBS has exited - stopping (%s)" % detail)
                    break
                if not CONNECTED_ONCE[0] and time.time() - started > GRACE:
                    log("OBS never became reachable within %ds - stopping" % GRACE)
                    break
                log("reconnecting in 3s (%s)" % detail)
                time.sleep(3)"""

assert old in s
s = s.replace(old, new, 1)

io.open(P, 'w', encoding='utf-8', newline='').write(s)
print("process_running added :", "def process_running" in s)
print("supervisor reconnects :", "reconnecting in 3s" in s)

import io

P = r"C:\Users\Srini\obs-tools\obs-autopilot.py"
s = io.open(P, encoding='utf-8').read()

old = """    await asyncio.gather(scene_switcher(obs, cfg, stop),
                         valorant_watcher(obs, cfg, stop),
                         status_watcher(obs, cfg, stop),
                         tracker_watcher(stop),
                         finals_watcher(cfg, stop),
                         clips.run(stop), pump)"""

new = """    # gather() waits for *every* task, and pump() ends cleanly (no
    # exception) when OBS closes the socket - so gather would hang on the
    # remaining infinite loops and this process would never exit.
    # FIRST_COMPLETED means whichever task finishes first ends the run.
    workers = [
        asyncio.create_task(scene_switcher(obs, cfg, stop)),
        asyncio.create_task(valorant_watcher(obs, cfg, stop)),
        asyncio.create_task(status_watcher(obs, cfg, stop)),
        asyncio.create_task(tracker_watcher(stop)),
        asyncio.create_task(finals_watcher(cfg, stop)),
        asyncio.create_task(clips.run(stop)),
        pump,
    ]
    try:
        done, pending = await asyncio.wait(workers,
                                           return_when=asyncio.FIRST_COMPLETED)
    finally:
        stop.set()
        for t in workers:
            if not t.done():
                t.cancel()
        await asyncio.gather(*workers, return_exceptions=True)
    # re-raise whatever ended the run, so the supervisor can log it
    for t in done:
        exc = t.exception()
        if exc is not None:
            raise exc"""
